packages.area: v142 sub-CPU payload — the IC303 tone-generator CONTROL register (bank +0x000) and the word built for it
packages.summary: The +0x000 CONTROL register is written by exactly twelve sites in the whole ROM (a thirteenth bank-0 latch, in ToneGen_Read_Register, is the read-back). It carries three command forms: the literal note-on gate 0x8100 (3 sites, always exactly 0x8100, never computed), the literal free 0x7E00 (4 sites), and a computed hand-off word with bit 15 set (5 sites), built by Voice_Build_GateCommand (0x025589) / Voice_Build_GateCommand_NoPartial (0x0255F3) into the live slot record at +0x2D (0x0430BB + slot*0x47). The same word with bit 15 CLEARED is the update-without-re-gate form, emitted by ToneGen_ReadPitch_AndScale (0x02E18D, `res 15, bc` at 0x02E1E3). Contrary to the task framing, the run-time block at 0x0451CC never has its word 0 stored and ToneGen_WriteVoiceParams starts at +0x02 — the control word is NOT staged there at run time; it lives in the live slot record. Word 0 of a 68-byte block IS the control word in the block *format*, proven by ToneGen_Config_Init handing template word 0 (ROM 0x00F8D5 = 0x1200) to ToneGen_WriteSingleReg. The four measured hand-off values reconcile with the code arithmetic exactly: F0FF/F1D7/F187 are `0xF000 | (P[0]!=0 ? 0x100 : 0) | (0xFF - 4*(P[0] & 0x3F))`, and F000 is the NoPartial twin's bare literal — the only producer of a 0x00 low byte, since the computed byte is always ≡ 3 (mod 4). The absence of the 0xFExx family is also explained: 0x04134C is written only at the head of Voice_AllVoices_UpdateVelocity (0x028C39) and the audio-side reset calls it with A = 1, which is not in {0,5,6}, so the 0xFE00 arm is unreachable after boot. Seven comment-only edits are proposed; no instruction, directive, label or branch target is touched and nothing is renamed, so the assembled bytes are unchanged.

Voice_Build_GateCommand:
	push xiz
	ld xiz, xwa
	ld xwa, (xiz + 23)
edits.replacement:
; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
; THE TONE GENERATOR CONTROL REGISTER (bank +0x000), AND THE WORD BUILT FOR IT
;
; Register address (0x0000 + slot) on IC303 is the per-voice CONTROL/gate register. This
; routine and its twin Voice_Build_GateCommand_NoPartial (0x0255F3) build the word that is
; handed to it and park it in the LIVE slot record at +0x2D (0x0430BB + slot*0x47). They
; touch no hardware; the writers listed below push it.
;
; FROM THE CODE -- the command set. Every bank-0x0000 access in the ROM was enumerated by
; scanning the binary for the address latch `ld (0x100000),WA` (f2 00 00 10 50) whose
; preceding instruction is NOT `add WA,imm16`, plus the one immediate-form latch
; (f2 00 00 10 02 with a value < 0x40). Thirteen sites, no others; one is the read-back:
;
;   NOTE-ON GATE   literal 0x8100. Always exactly that value, never computed. Three sites,
;                  all mid-burst: ToneGen_WriteVoiceParams (data write at 0x02D2B4),
;                  ToneGen_WriteVoiceParams_Ext (0x02D6CA), _Ext2 (0x02D777).
;   FREE           literal 0x7E00. Four sites: ToneGen_SilenceChannel (0x02B4D4),
;                  ToneGen_Config_Init (0x02E085), Voice_Reset_Engine phase B (0x021F94),
;                  and the dormant probe ToneGen_ConfigInit_AltData (0x02E17D).
;   HAND-OFF       the word built here, bit 15 SET. Five sites: ToneGen_WriteSingleReg
;                  (0x02D41B), ToneGen_WriteVoice_Direct (0x027FBB), and the tails of
;                  ToneGen_WriteVoiceParams_Ext (0x02D731) / _Ext2 (0x02D7B9).
;                  The SAME word with bit 15 CLEARED is the update-without-re-gate form,
;                  emitted by ToneGen_ReadPitch_AndScale (`res 15, bc` at 0x02E1E3).
;   READ-BACK      0x021026, inside ToneGen_Read_Register: bank 0x0000 indices 0..3 read as
;                  four 16-bit ACTIVE-VOICE BITMAPS (Voice_Manager_PollBank, 0x02219F).
;
; HOW THIS ROUTINE BUILDS THE WORD (IN: XWA = live slot record; OUT: record+0x2D):
;   bits 7..0   0xFF - 4*(P[0] & 0x3F), where P = the u32 pointer at record+0x17 and P[0]
;               is its first BYTE. Range 0x03..0xFF, and always == 3 (mod 4).
;   bit 8       SET iff that same byte P[0] is non-zero. Meaning not established.
;   bits 15..9  0xFE00 when the global mode byte 0x04134C is 0, 5 or 6, else 0xF000; the
;               selector is skipped and 0xF000 forced when byte +0x12 of the record at
;               record+0x23 is zero.
;   then        Voice_Apply_GateRouting (0x02552A) may overwrite bits [14:12] and [11:9]
;               from the two nibbles of (0x04138D + channel*0x11F). Neither arm can clear
;               bit 15 -- the masks are 0x8FFF and 0xF1FF -- so the hand-off word always
;               leaves here with bit 15 set.
; The twin Voice_Build_GateCommand_NoPartial stores the bare literal 0xFE00 / 0xF000 with no
; level byte at all, so it is the ONLY producer of a 0x00 low byte.
;
; MEASURED (capture of a running machine, 1705 note-ons of the built-in demo): only FOUR
; hand-off values are ever issued -- F0FF, F000, F1D7, F187 -- and the LOW BYTE is an OUTPUT
; LEVEL (0xFF full, 0x00 silent), not a mode flag. All four reconcile with the arithmetic
; above, exactly:
;   F0FF  this routine, P[0] == 0            -> 0xFF - 0    = 0xFF, bit 8 clear
;   F1D7  this routine, P[0] & 0x3F == 0x0A  -> 0xFF - 0x28 = 0xD7, bit 8 set
;   F187  this routine, P[0] & 0x3F == 0x1E  -> 0xFF - 0x78 = 0x87, bit 8 set
;   F000  the NoPartial twin's literal -- unreachable from here, because the computed low
;         byte is always == 3 (mod 4) and can never be 0x00.
; The 0xFExx family being absent from the capture is a code fact too: the ONLY writer of
; 0x04134C is the head of Voice_AllVoices_UpdateVelocity (0x028C39), and the audio-side
; reset (Voice_ResetAllControllers) calls it with A = 1, which is not in {0,5,6}, so the
; 0xFE00 arm is not reachable after boot unless a SysEx re-selects the mode.
;
; A voice handed F000 is meant to be INAUDIBLE, and the firmware relies on it: the capture
; shows one voice left gated and never freed at the end of boot, with its envelope
; programmed to hold. The code makes that state stable -- Voice_Manager_PollBank_SlotLoop
; (0x02222A) frees a slot only on a 1 -> 0 edge of the active-voice bitmap it reads back
; through ToneGen_Read_Register, so a voice whose envelope never decays never produces the
; edge and never reaches ToneGen_SilenceChannel.
;
; INFERENCE: read in the same field layout, the 0x8100 note-on gate is "gate on, both
; routing fields 0, level 0" -- the burst gates the voice silent and the hand-off word that
; follows supplies the routing and the level. Not proven; 0x8100 is a literal in the ROM.
; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Voice_Build_GateCommand:
	push xiz
	ld xiz, xwa
	ld xwa, (xiz + 23)
edits.why: The routine that builds the CONTROL-register hand-off word had no header at all. This is the deep annotation the task asks for: the full command set, the exact bit layout as built, and the capture reconciled value by value, with CODE and MEASURED kept separate.

Voice_Build_GateCommand_NoPartial:
	push xiz
	ld xiz, xwa
	ld xwa, (xiz + 19)
edits.replacement:
; The level-less twin of Voice_Build_GateCommand (0x025589 -- the CONTROL register, bank
; +0x000, is documented in full there). IN: XWA = live slot record; OUT: record+0x2D.
;
; It runs the SAME high-field selector (record+0x23 byte +0x12, then the global mode byte
; 0x04134C in {0,5,6}) and the SAME Voice_Apply_GateRouting patch, but stores a bare literal
; -- `ldw (xiz + 45), 0xFE00` / `0xF000` at 0x025613 / 0x02561A / 0x025621 -- with no level
; byte and no bit 8. Its first instruction, `ld xwa, (xiz + 19)`, loads a pointer that the
; next load immediately discards; dead code, kept for byte fidelity.
;
; ★ THIS IS WHERE 0xF000 COMES FROM. The computed sibling cannot produce a 0x00 low byte
; (its byte is 0xFF - 4*k, always == 3 mod 4), so every F000 the chip receives is this
; literal. MEASURED (demo capture, 1705 note-ons): F000 is one of only four hand-off values
; ever issued, and its low byte 0x00 means output level zero -- the voice is gated but
; inaudible.
; Callers, all of them slot-parameter rebuilds that end in ToneGen_WriteVoiceParams:
; Voice_Init_Type1 (0x02C3CC), Voice_Init_Type2 (0x02C0B6), and the TypeB arm of
; Voice_AllVoices_UpdateVelocity (0x028C39).
Voice_Build_GateCommand_NoPartial:
	push xiz
	ld xiz, xwa
	ld xwa, (xiz + 19)
edits.why: This twin is the sole source of the measured F000 value, the most load-bearing fact in the capture, and it had no header. The dead first load is noted so a future pass does not chase it.

; register; the bit15 set/clear pair around the whole burst is the load strobe of the
; SEPARATE 0x0080 register. This is the single biggest consumer of TG bandwidth in the
; firmware.
; Two facts about that gate, both from a scan of every bank-0x0000 access in the ROM:
;   - it is the literal 0x8100 at all three of its sites (here at 0x02D2B4, and in
;     ToneGen_WriteVoiceParams_Ext 0x02D6CA and _Ext2 0x02D777) -- never computed, and the

edits.why: The existing text called 0x8100 a "key/gate command" without saying it is invariant, and could be read as implying the burst carries the block's +0x00 word. Both corrections are checkable against the three literal sites.

uncertain: The task framed the control register as "staged in the block at 0x0451CE". It is not, at run time: ToneGen_WriteVoiceParams reads the block from +0x02 upwards, and no store to 0x0451CC exists in the source. I could only prove absence by grep plus reading the writer; a store performed through a pointer register loaded from something other than a literal 0x0451CC would not show up in that grep.

Bit 8 of the hand-off word. The code sets it iff the first byte of the record at slot+0x17 is non-zero, independently of the level byte. Whether it is a ninth level bit, a per-recording flag, or something else is not established. If it were a level bit, F1D7/F187 would decode differently from the way the capture read them.

CODE/CAPTURE TENSION I could not resolve, flagged so nobody trips over it later. The literal-F000 builder (Voice_Build_GateCommand_NoPartial) is called by Voice_Init_Type1 (0x02C3CC) and Voice_Init_Type2 (0x02C0B6), which sit on real note-on paths — Voice_SetPitch and Voice_NoteOff call Voice_Init_Type1 and then hand +0x2D to the chip. If low byte 0x00 is silence unconditionally, those note-ons would be silent. Two readings both fit the evidence I have: (a) the demo's audible notes all come through the Voice_Build_GateCommand family (types 0x40/0xC0 in Voice_AllVoices_UpdateVelocity) and the F000 hand-offs in the capture are exactly the voices that stayed silent, or (b) those voices take their level entirely from the 0x0800/0x0840 envelope registers. Deciding it needs a capture correlating each hand-off value with per-slot audio, not more reading. The proposed comments state the measurement and the code fact side by side without asserting a resolution.

"0x81xx" in the task versus 0x8100 in the ROM. Every bank-0x0000 gate write in the binary is the literal 0x8100 (three sites, verified by immediate scan). If the capture logged gate words with a varying low byte, they did not come from those three sites — but the enumeration found no other writer.

The "one voice gated and never freed at the end of boot" observation is the capture's, not mine. I identified a code path that makes such a state stable (Voice_Manager_PollBank frees only on a 1 -> 0 bitmap edge) but I did not identify WHICH routine gates that particular voice, nor which slot it is. ToneGen_Config_Init frees all 64 with 0x7E00 at boot, so whatever gates it runs later.

The bank-0x0000 map is write-64 / read-4: writes address (0x0000 + slot) for 64 slots, reads address (0x0000 + bank) for four 16-bit bitmaps. I verified both sides in code but have no datasheet, so whether reading (0x0000 + slot) for slot >= 4 means anything is unknown.

Reproducibility: the enumeration recipe and the offset derivation are written out in the evidence, but I am read-only and could not commit them. Per the standing rule they belong in the repo (suggested: scripts/scan_tg_bank0.py plus a README line naming the question it answers) in the same commit as these comments.

packages.area: v142 sub-CPU payload — ToneGen_WriteVoiceParams (0x02D101) and the IC303 parameter-latch bus protocol
packages.summary: ToneGen_WriteVoiceParams is a 794-byte straight-line burst (0x02D101-0x02D41A) that ships one voice's whole register set to IC303 over a two-port register-indirect bus (0x100000 = address latch, 0x100002 = data) plus a hand-driven select on P6.7 (SFR 0x18 bit 7, the CPU's A23 pin taken out of bus mode by the payload's own RESET code). It performs 23 writes to 22 distinct registers and ZERO reads: there is no handshake, no status poll, no timeout and no ei/di anywhere in the routine — the only flow control is fixed padding (one NOP between the address word and the data word; a zero-displacement `jr` plus three NOPs after each data word). The frame is opened by forcing bit 15 SET on the 0x080 word (write #2, `set 0x0f,WA` @0x02D145) and closed by re-writing the same word with bit 15 CLEAR (write #23, `res 0x0f,WA` @0x02D40A); the 0x040 wave/zone selector is written BEFORE the frame opens and the fixed 0x8100 gate command is written ten writes before it closes. The 21 block words it transmits (+0x02..+0x2A) are exactly the 21 rows of the staging-block table above Voice_Build_OutputLevel, in that table's own top-to-bottom order — the table is this burst read out sequentially — and two independent artefacts (the boot ROM's field-by-field annotated twin record at 0xFF824C, and ToneGen_Config_Init's raw 0x800<-0xFF80 / 0x840<-0xFF00 mute matching template words 12/13) confirm the map is not merely this routine restated. Three comment-only edits are proposed: a full replacement header for the routine, a correction of a shipped wrong comment that calls the P6.7 toggle a "maskable-interrupt gate", and a one-line addition to the staging-block table noting word 0 (0x0451CC), which this routine does not read.

ToneGen_WriteVoiceParams:
edits.replacement:
; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
; ToneGen_WriteVoiceParams (0x02D101-0x02D41A, 794 bytes) -- THE IC303 PARAMETER-LATCH BURST
; Existing name kept; documentation only.
;
; In:  WA = tone-generator channel, 0..0x3F.  XBC = long pointer to a staging block; the
;      routine reads 21 consecutive words at +0x02..+0x2A and nothing else (+0x04 twice).
;      Neither argument is range-checked -- see HAZARDS.
; Out: nothing.  XBC and IZ come back unchanged; XWA is clobbered.
;
; THE BUS.  IC303 is a register-indirect device on two word ports plus one hand-driven pin:
;
;     write 0x100000  = 16-bit REGISTER-ADDRESS latch
;     write 0x100002  = 16-bit DATA for the register last latched
;     read  0x100000  = read-back for the register last latched.  Used by exactly one
;                       routine in the whole payload, ToneGen_Read_Register (0x021023).
;     P6.7  (SFR 0x18 bit 7) = an out-of-band select the firmware drives by hand
;
; P6.7 is the CPU's A23 pin taken out of bus mode.  RESET (0x01F924) programs it:
; `ldio 0x18,0xFF` (P6 data = high), `ldio 0x1B,0x7F` (P6FC: bits 0..6 stay A16..A22, bit 7
; becomes plain port) and `ldio 0x1A,0x80` (P6CR: bit 7 = output).  The source comment kept
; at ToneGen_Poll_Read records the net as the tone generator's D5VNAD / NAD / EXADL0 pins.
; MEASURED over this file: in a linear scan, the most recent P6.7 write before EVERY one of
; the 282 instruction-level accesses to the 0x10xxxx / 0x11xxxx window matches bit 1 of that
; access's address, with no exceptions -- 139 LOW/0x100000 writes, 138 HIGH/0x100002 writes,
; 1 LOW/0x100000 read-back, and 4 keybed accesses at 0x110000 / 0x110002.
; INFERENCE: the chip needs that select valid before /CS, so the firmware presents it one
; instruction early and holds it across the cycle.
;
; ONE REGISTER WRITE.  All 23 writes below are this identical sequence, with no variation:
;
;     res 7,(0x18)            ; select LOW
;     ld  (0x100000),WA       ; WA = register address = bank | channel
;     nop                     ; setup pad
;     set 7,(0x18)            ; select HIGH
;     ld  (0x100002),WA       ; WA = the data word
;     jr  <next instruction>  ; pipeline flush (opcode 68 00, displacement 0)
;     nop / nop / nop         ; recovery pad
;
; The address is built as `ld wa,iz / add wa,BANK`.  Every bank is a multiple of 0x40 and
; the channel is <= 0x3F, so the add acts as an OR: bits 5..0 = channel, 15..6 = register.
;
; NO HANDSHAKE, NO BUSY WAIT.  23 latch writes, 23 data writes, ZERO reads -- the routine
; never looks at the chip.  No status bit is polled, no counter is kept, and there is no
; `ei`/`di` in 0x02D101..0x02D41A.  The only flow control is the fixed padding above.  (The
; boot ROM's structurally identical twin HARDWARE_PARAM_BLOCK_WRITE at 0xFF8D0A is also
; unconditional, but ITS caller then polls a status word at 0x100004 up to 1000 times.  The
; v1.42 payload never touches 0x100004 at all; 0x100000 and 0x100002 are its only TG ports.)
; MEASURED in emulation only (kn7000_mame tools/kn5000_tgbus_trace.lua, organ demo, 65
; gates): consecutive writes land ~3 us apart, ~31 us from the mid-burst gate to the
; closing strobe.  That is emulated TLCS-900 timing, not a hardware measurement.
;
; THE BURST, IN ORDER.  blk = XBC.
;
;    #   register       data                      notes
;    1   0x040 | ch     blk[+0x02]                wave/zone selector -- BEFORE the strobe
;    2   0x080 | ch     blk[+0x04] | 0x8000       STROBE UP   (`set 0x0f,WA` @ 0x02D145)
;    3   0x0C0 | ch     blk[+0x06]
;    4   0x100 | ch     blk[+0x08]
;    5   0x140 | ch     blk[+0x0A]
;    6   0x180 | ch     blk[+0x0C]
;    7   0x400 | ch     blk[+0x0E]
;    8   0x440 | ch     blk[+0x10]
;    9   0x480 | ch     blk[+0x12]
;   10   0x4C0 | ch     blk[+0x14]
;   11   0x500 | ch     blk[+0x16]
;   12   0x800 | ch     blk[+0x18]
;   13   0x000 | ch     0x8100 IMMEDIATE          the gate/key command, mid-frame; never
;                                                 taken from the block
;                                                 (`ld (0x100002),0x8100` @ 0x02D2B4)
;   14   0x840 | ch     blk[+0x1A]
;   15   0x880 | ch     blk[+0x1C]
;   16   0x8C0 | ch     blk[+0x1E]
;   17   0x900 | ch     blk[+0x20]
;   18   0x940 | ch     blk[+0x22]

;
; So: 23 writes to 22 DISTINCT registers.  0x080 is the only register written twice and
; blk[+0x04] the only word sent twice.  blk[+0x00] is not read here (see THE BLOCK).
;
; THE BIT-15 STROBE.  Bit 15 of the 0x080 word is a frame marker, not level data.  Five
; independent places agree: this routine forces it set on write #2 and clear on write #23;
; the boot ROM's twin performs the same `set 15` / `res 15` on the same word +0x04 of the
; same record shape; Voice_Build_OutputLevel forces it set when it STAGES the word; the two
; ROM default records carry it already set (0x00F8D5 word 2 = 0x8000, 0x00F919 word 2 =
; 0x83FF); and the dead single-register writer at 0x02D0DC exists only to do the clear half.
; WHAT THE CHIP DOES BETWEEN THE EDGES IS NOT ESTABLISHED BY THE ROM.  INFERENCE, and the
; assumption MAME's HLE encodes: the framed writes are staged and commit on the falling
; edge.  The ROM cannot separate that from "every write takes effect immediately", and any
; model must respect two facts it does give: the 0x040 selector is written BEFORE the strobe
; rises, and the 0x8100 gate is written ten writes BEFORE it falls.
;
; THE BLOCK.  Callers pass a 34-word (68-byte) record; only words 1..21 go out here.
;   word 0 (+0x00) is the value for register 0x000|ch and is shipped by the CALLER right
;     after this routine returns, via ToneGen_WriteSingleReg -- see ToneGen_Config_Init
;     (0x02DFCF), ToneGen_SetupPolyVoice (0x0355AD) and ToneGen_SetupPercussionVoice
;     (0x035656).  At the main staging block 0x0451CC nothing ever writes word 0: there is
;     no direct-address store to 0x0451CC anywhere in the payload, and every
;     `lda_24 xbc,0x0451cc` site immediately calls a TG writer that only reads the block.
;   words 22..33 (+0x2C..+0x43) complete the record shape and are not transmitted here.
;
; BLOCK BASES ACTUALLY USED -- 9 call sites in the ROM, 8 assembled as call/calr plus one
; hidden inside the `.byte` blob ToneGen_ConfigInit_AltData:
;   0x0451CC  x5   main voice staging block (callers at 0x0273A0, 0x02B56E, 0x02BD7F,
;                  0x02C123, 0x02C448)
;   0x003B1C  x2   auxiliary 8-voice pool (0x035640, 0x0356B4)
;   caller's  x1   0x02E010 -- DSP_Config_Init's 0x2AA4 copy of the 0x00F8D5 template
;   0x00F919  x1   0x02E0F7 -- the dormant liveness probe; unreachable in v1.42
;
; CROSS-CHECK against the staging-block table documented above Voice_Build_OutputLevel: the
; 21 transmitted words are exactly that table's 21 rows, in the table's own top-to-bottom
; order, one word each, 0x0451CE->+0x040 through 0x0451F6->+0xA40.  The table IS this burst
; read out sequentially.  Two confirmations that the map is not merely this routine
; restated: (a) the boot ROM annotates its own copy of the record field by field
; (ToneGen_ProbeVoice_ParamBlock at 0xFF824C, byte-identical to payload 0x00F919); (b)
; ToneGen_Config_Init mutes a channel with two raw writes, 0x800|ch <- 0xFF80 and
; 0x840|ch <- 0xFF00, then bursts a template whose words 12 and 13 are 0xFF80 and 0xFF00 --
; a shifted map would have the burst undo the mute it had just set.
;
; HAZARDS for anyone implementing or emulating this:
;   * The channel is never masked.  `add wa,BANK` with a channel >= 0x40 carries into the
;     register field; the callers, not this routine, do the `cp ...,0x40` gating.
;   * Interrupts stay enabled for the whole burst and no lock is taken.  The address latch
;     is a single shared register, so another TG writer entered from an interrupt between a
;     0x100000 write and its 0x100002 partner would mis-pair the two.
;   * `lds wa,0` at 0x02D109 is dead code -- WA is reloaded from IZ two instructions later.
;
; This is the single biggest consumer of TG bandwidth in the firmware.
ToneGen_WriteVoiceParams:
edits.why: Replaces a header that was thin and carried two defects -- it counted 23 WRITES as "23 registers" (there are 22 distinct; 0x080 is written twice) and pointed at an "offset->register map in the file header" that does not exist (the map lives above Voice_Build_OutputLevel). The new block documents the actual bus (both ports, the P6.7 select and how RESET configures it), proves the absence of any handshake, gives the write order write-by-write with ROM addresses for the two strobe instructions, states plainly which part of the strobe's meaning is inference, and records the cross-check against the staging-block table. uncertain: What the chip actually does between the bit-15 edges. The ROM proves the bit frames the burst, nothing more. "Stage everything and commit on the falling edge" and "every write takes effect as it lands" are both consistent with the code: the 0x040 selector is written before the frame opens and the 0x8100 gate ten writes before it closes, and a ~31 us commit delay would be inaudible either way. Why the boot ROM's twin needs no P6.7 toggle while the payload toggles it on every single word. The boot ROM never programs P6/P6CR/P6FC, so its burst runs with the pin in whatever state reset leaves it; I did not establish the TMP94C241 reset default for that pin, and no schematic was consulted. It is possible the toggle is redundant on real hardware and only the two port addresses matter.

Whether P6.7 is genuinely a second copy of the A1 select or something else that merely happens to track A1 in all 282 observed accesses. The correlation is exceptionless but it is a correlation over one firmware image, not a pin-level measurement.

The 3 us / 31 us figures are emulated TLCS-900 timing from a MAME trace. Real IC303 setup/hold requirements, and whether the nop + jr + 3-nop padding is a minimum or has margin, are unknown; nothing in this pass measured hardware.

I did not verify that no access to the 0x10xxxx window is made through a register-indirect address (e.g. an index register preloaded with 0x100000). The 282-access census covers direct-address forms only.

Whether any TG writer is actually reachable from an interrupt handler while a burst is in flight. The header states the hazard structurally -- no lock, interrupts enabled, one shared latch -- without claiming the race is reachable in practice.

packages.area: Wave ROM directory format (IC304–IC307) as seen from the KN5000 sub-CPU firmware — v142/subcpu/kn5000_subprogram_v142.s
packages.summary:
**The firmware does NOT walk the wave ROM directory. IC303 does.** That is the headline finding, and it is a hard negative with three independent legs, all re-verified in this pass:

1. **No CPU can see the wave ROMs.** A census of `v142/subcpu/kn5000_subprogram_v142.s` finds 139 writes to the IC303 address latch `0x100000`, 137 writes to the data port `0x100002`, and **exactly one read anywhere in the payload** — `ldw_da xhl, 0x100000` at line 2651, inside `ToneGen_Read_Register`, which the file already documents as returning the active-voice bitmap (latch 0..3) or a channel's envelope level (latch 0x180+ch). The sub-CPU boot ROM is the same shape: 29 latch writes, 28 data writes, one status read at `0x100004`. Neither ever reads a wave byte.
2. **The MAME driver agrees**: `mame_driver/src/mame/matsushita/kn5000.cpp:770-774` puts the four wave ROMs in their own `ROM_REGION16_LE("waveform")`, which appears in neither `maincpu_mem` (141-157) nor `subcpu_mem` (159-172).
3. **The machine's own Wave ROM Check (service test E3+E4) is acoustic**, not a read-back — documented in `../technics-docs/kn7000-expansion-and-wave-dump.md`. The KN7000 has a CPU-visible wave read port; the KN5000 has no equivalent.

The firmware's entire contribution is one opaque 16-bit index. All twelve instructions in the ROM that touch the selector word `0x0451CE` are accounted for: eight stores (the six `WaveSel_Emit_ZoneRecord_S*` variants and `WaveSel_StageB_Store_Reg040`, each copying word 0 of a zone record verbatim, plus `Voice_InitVoiceState` storing 0), one read-modify-write that doubles the top nibble when bit 2 of `0x041343` is set, and `Voice_Slot_ApplyPitchJitter`'s `add (0x0451CE), (tick & 7)` reached from `Voice_Init_Type1` (line 22346). Nothing splits the word, range-checks the entry against a count, or dereferences anything with it. `ToneGen_WriteVoiceParams` then pushes it as the **first** word of its 23-register burst (shadow base `0x0451CC`, so `+0x02` = `0x0451CE` → register `0x0040 + ch`).

So the package is four comment blocks, all in `v142/subcpu/kn5000_subprogram_v142.s`, that (a) state the negative plainly at the three places a future reader will look for the walk, and (b) document the on-ROM format the chip resolves the index against, since nothing else in the file is meaningful without it. **No instruction, directive, label or branch target is touched — comments only, zero effect on the assembled bytes.**

Everything in the format block was re-measured this pass from `kn5000_original_roms/kn5000/kn5000_waveform_rom.ic307` (SHA1 `4b511bff6625f4655cabd96a263bf548d2ef4bf7`): the four-page split with self-declaring counts 198/168/1072/57, the 1495/1495 back-reference validation, the record-body pair census, and the bit-7-is-only-ever-last property (0 exceptions in 7184 pairs). Reproducible probes for all of it are already committed in `kn7000_mame/tools/kn5000-rom-structure/`, and the comment names them.

edits.replacement:
; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
; WHAT +0x040 SELECTS: THE WAVE ROM'S OWN DIRECTORY -- WHICH THIS FIRMWARE NEVER READS
;
; NEGATIVE RESULT FIRST, because it is the answer to the obvious question: nothing in this
; ROM, nor in the sub-CPU boot ROM, nor in the main program, walks the waveform ROMs. It
; cannot. IC304-IC307 hang on IC303's private bus and are in NO CPU's address space:
;   * this payload's only channel to IC303 is the address latch 0x100000 / data port
;     0x100002. A census of this file finds 139 writes to the latch, 137 to the data port,
;     and exactly ONE read anywhere -- `ldw_da xhl, 0x100000` inside ToneGen_Read_Register
;     -- which returns the active-voice bitmap (latch 0..3) or a channel's envelope level
;     (latch 0x180+ch). The boot ROM has the same shape: 29 latch writes, 28 data writes,
;     one status read at 0x100004. No wave byte reaches either CPU.
;   * MAME's kn5000.cpp keeps the four wave ROMs in their own ROM_REGION16_LE("waveform"),
;     which appears in neither maincpu_mem nor subcpu_mem.
;   * the machine's own WAVE ROM CHECK service test (E3+E4) is ACOUSTIC -- the ROMs are made
;     to sound and a technician listens for distortion -- not a read-back. The KN7000 does
;     have a CPU-visible wave read port; the KN5000 has no equivalent. See
;     ../technics-docs/kn7000-expansion-and-wave-dump.md.
; So IC303 does the walk. The firmware's entire contribution is one 16-bit index. The rest
; of this block documents the format that index is resolved against, because none of the
; per-voice work in this file means anything without it.
;
; THE SELECTOR. 0x0451CE is shadow+0x02, the FIRST word ToneGen_WriteVoiceParams pushes
; (register 0x0040 + ch). Its layout is
;
;     class = word >> 12       selects one 1 MB PAGE of one wave socket
;     entry = word & 0x0FFF    plain 0-based index into that page's directory, base 0
;
; and the firmware treats it as opaque. Every instruction in this ROM that touches 0x0451CE
; is accounted for: eight stores (the six WaveSel_Emit_ZoneRecord_S* variants and
; WaveSel_StageB_Store_Reg040, each copying word 0 of a zone record verbatim, plus
; Voice_InitVoiceState storing 0), one read-modify-write that doubles the top nibble when
; bit 2 of 0x041343 is set, and Voice_Slot_ApplyPitchJitter's `add (0x0451CE), (tick & 7)`
; reached from Voice_Init_Type1. Nothing splits the word, range-checks the entry against a
; count, or dereferences anything with it. INFERENCE: that the only arithmetic on the low
; bits is a +0..7 step fits consecutive directory entries being variants of one recording
; (the shared-wave runs below are 6 and 7 entries long), but the musical reading of that
; step is not proven here.
;
; THE PAGE FORMAT, measured on kn5000_waveform_rom.ic307 (SHA1
; 4b511bff6625f4655cabd96a263bf548d2ef4bf7), the only hardware-rooted wave dump that
; exists -- IC304/IC305/IC306 have no genuine dump (the files carrying those names are
; placeholders, 83.4% 0xFF against IC307's 1.3%; the driver declares all three NO_DUMP).
; Each 1 MB page is independently self-describing:
;
;     u16 param_ptr, u16 wave_off      x N     ; the directory, at page offset 0
;     ... variable-length parameter records ...
;     ... signed 16-bit little-endian PCM ...
;
;     N          = u16[page + 0] / 4           ; entry 0's param_ptr points just past the
;                                              ; directory, so THE DIRECTORY DECLARES ITS
;                                              ; OWN LENGTH -- there is no count field
;     PCM start  = page + wave_off * 16        ; 16-byte (8-sample) granule
;     PCM end    = page + 16 * (next strictly greater wave_off in the directory)
;     param rec  = page + param_ptr .. page + (next strictly greater param_ptr)
;
; wave_off is a u16 scaled by 16, so it reaches 0x0FFFF0 and no further: that is WHY the
; page is 1 MB, and why a 4-bit class field spans exactly the 16 MB of four 4 MB sockets.
; IC307's four pages, all four measured:
;
;   page  base       N    directory      parameter records  pad   PCM
;   0     0x000000   198  0x0000-0x0317  0x0318-0x1A26      10 B  0x001A30-0x0FEF60
;   1     0x100000   168  0x0000-0x029F  0x02A0-0x182C      20 B  0x001840-0x0FEB60
;   2     0x200000  1072  0x0000-0x10BF  0x10C0-0x2694      12 B  0x0026A0-0x0FFEE0
;   3     0x300000    57  0x0000-0x00E3  0x00E4-0x022C      20 B  0x000240-0x0FF5C0
;
; 1495 slots, 1413 distinct wave offsets, in one 4 MB chip. Both directory columns rise
; monotonically except three entries on page 1 (79, 82, 85) whose wave_off steps backwards
; to re-use an earlier recording. The parameter block always ends 10-20 bytes short of the
; first PCM byte -- padding up to the 16-byte granule.
;
; IT IS SELF-VALIDATING. The first word of every parameter record repeats that entry's own
; wave_off. It holds 198/198, 168/168, 1072/1072, 57/57 -- 1495 of 1495, no exceptions.
; That redundancy is the cheapest possible check that a (class, entry) pair landed on a
; real slot, and it is also what proves the four-page reading is not pattern-matching on
; noise: mis-framed data cannot satisfy a back-reference 1072 times in a row.
;
; WHAT A PARAMETER RECORD CONTAINS. The redundant wave_off word, then zero or more
; { value:8, flag:8 } pairs (little-endian word = value | flag << 8). 7184 real pairs over
; the 1495 records; 964 records have none at all (960 of those on page 2, which holds short
; one-shot material), and the largest record is 850 bytes.
;   flag 0x00        KEY-SPLIT BOUNDARY. 591 of them, 539 multiples of 8, listed
;                    DESCENDING within a record. The unit is NOT MIDI -- 116 of the 591
;                    values exceed 0x7F. Against the firmware's own zone table the relation
;                    is key = 1.5 * (value - 0x28), i.e. one unit = 1/8 octave (MEASURED
;                    relation; INFERRED unit interpretation).
;   flag 0x01-0x2F   PER-ZONE FINE TUNE. 6209 pairs, 6170 of them (99.4%) with a value
;                    >= 0xE0, i.e. signed -1..-32. Two page-0 records (180 and 181) are 53
;                    and 130 such pairs and nothing else: a per-key detune table across the
;                    keyboard, which is exactly what a stretched multisample needs.
;   flag bit 7       END OF RECORD. Set on 286 records and, across all 7184 pairs, NEVER on
;                    a pair that is not the last one of its record. Not every record uses
;                    it -- the extent is delimited by the next param_ptr regardless.
;   flag bit 6       A MARKER, 258 occurrences, 65 of them mid-record, so bit 6 is NOT a
;                    terminator. 0xC0 = both bits.
; NOT PRESENT: no root note and no loop points. Every field in every record is a single
; byte, while a loop offset into a 1.5 M-sample wave would need >= 21 bits; the pitch
; origin comes from the firmware side (the tone database's zone records and this file's
; pitch chain), not from the wave ROM.
;
; MULTISAMPLES SHOW UP AS RUNS OF CONSECUTIVE ENTRIES sharing one wave_off with shifted
; split lists -- page 0 entries 185-190 (wave 0xFCA6) and 191-197 (wave 0xFEF6), each
; successive entry's splits shifted by +8 units. The firmware's own key zones for those
; same entries tile the keyboard contiguously with no overlap: a cross-check between two
; ROMs written by different tools.
;
; PROVENANCE. Format, four-page split and the class decode:
; kn7000_mame/notes/kn5000-structural-validation.md (2026-07-25) and
; notes/kn5000-ic307-content-map.md; re-runnable probes in
; kn7000_mame/tools/kn5000-rom-structure/ (waverec.py prints the per-page counts and record
; histograms, flagcensus.py prints "back-reference OK: 1495 / 1495" and "bit7 set: 286
; bit6 set: 258", loopprobe.py is the loop-point negative). flagcensus's pair total of 7203
; exceeds the 7184 above by exactly the 19 zero words that pad each page's last record.
; The class -> page assignment was PREDICTED from the firmware alone -- max(entry)+1 over
; the 1444 (class, entry) pairs the table-data ROM's zone records produce -- and then
; checked against IC307's self-declared counts: class 4 needs 198 and page 0 has 198,
; class 5 needs 168 and page 1 has 168, class 7 needs 57 and page 3 has 57. Three exact
; hits, zero out-of-range entries; hence page = class & 3, bank = (class >> 2) & 3, with
; IC307 = bank 1. A pitch regression of class 7 onto page 3 gives slope 1.003 / R^2 0.998,
; where every wrong page gives slope ~0.
; STILL OPEN: WHICH PHYSICAL SOCKET IS BANK 0. That is a wiring fact, not a decoding one,
; and it cannot be settled until one of IC304/IC305/IC306 is really dumped.
; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
;
; THE THREE ENVELOPES share one word format, (target << 8) | rate, and are written with the

This is the natural home for it: the block immediately above already tabulates 0x0451CE -> +0x040 as the "recording selector, (class << 12) | entry" but says nothing about what the chip does with it, and a reader arriving here has no way to know the directory is unreadable by any CPU. ;        It is also the ONLY read of IC303 in the whole payload: 139 writes to the address

uncertain: WHICH PHYSICAL SOCKET IS BANK 0 (IC304, IC305 or IC306). The class->page assignment is forced by the firmware's own entry ranges, but the bank->socket wiring is not derivable from anything we hold. Stated as open in the proposed comment; do not let a future edit quietly resolve it.

THE SEMANTICS OF THE FLAG BYTE'S LOW 6 BITS in a parameter-record pair. They are structured, not arbitrary — the values observed are 0..5, 8..12, 16..21, 25..29, 34..37, 41, 43..45, i.e. (a<<3)|b with b never 6 or 7 — which reads like a (zone-group, sub-index) tag, but I could not pin it and the proposed comment does not claim it. Only the VALUE semantics (key split for flag 0x00, signed fine-tune for flags 0x01-0x2F) are asserted, and the fine-tune reading is inherited from notes/kn5000-ic307-content-map.md §3.2 rather than re-derived here.

WHY 245 OF THE 531 BODIED RECORDS DO NOT SET FLAG BIT 7. Bit 7 is provably exclusive to the final pair (0 exceptions in 7184 pairs), so it is an end marker, but it is optional and the record extent is really delimited by the next param_ptr. Whether IC303 reads to the terminator or is told the length some other way is unknown. The comment says exactly this and no more.

THE 'PITCH JITTER' READING OF Voice_Slot_ApplyPitchJitter. The mechanism is certain (`add (0x0451CE), (tick & 7)` — an increment of the entry ordinal). Whether that is round-robin sample variation, a deliberate humanise, or something else is not established; I marked it INFERENCE in the comment. Note that on page 0 consecutive entries of a shared-wave run are different KEY ZONES of one recording, so a +0..7 step there would not be a subtle effect — this deserves its own investigation and I did not open it.

I verified the main CPU has no wave-ROM window in maincpu_mem, which settles it structurally, but I did not exhaustively grep the v7/v9/v10 maincpu sources for a walk. packages.area: hdae5000 — UI object descriptor pool 0x29DC12-0x2A5D2B (hdae5000/hdae5000_data_tables.s, hdae5000/hdae5000_init_data.s)
packages.summary:
CONFIRMED, with a sharper finding than the ticket predicted. The pool is ONE array of 769 variable-length records; there is NO fixed stride (lengths 22..82 B, 26 distinct values). Record i starts at HDAE5000_UiObject_PtrTable[i] (0x2A5D2C) and ends where the next pool pointer starts; the 769th ends exactly at 0x2A5D2C, and the 769 record lengths sum to exactly 33,050 = the pool span.

There are NO .incbin directives in the pool (the region is emitted as raw .byte/.ascii/.fill). The five-way cut is made by LABELS, and all five are mid-record: HDAE5000_UI_Descriptors is +0x02 into record #0 (it splits the class-id .long in half), and the other four are +0x28/+0x3A/+0x20/+0x28 into records #18/#177/#645/#743 — each landing exactly on that record's INLINE CAPTION STRING. So "UI_Page_Titles" is object #18's caption "LYRICS WINDOW"; "Panel_Save_UI" is object #177's "CURRENT PANEL"; "Credits" is object #645's "Technosoft, CH-Samstagern" (one of four credit captions under ABOUT_HELP); "Demo_Data" is object #743's "RHYTHM CUSTOM" — there is no demo song data in the pool at all.

Record layout established and negative-controlled: +0x00 .long class id (high half 0x016A = a class of this ROM, low half = index into HDAE5000_ClassName_Table at 0x2F9832; high half 0x0160 = host KN5000 widget library), +0x04/+0x06/+0x08/+0x0A = parent/first-child/next-sibling/prev-sibling object indices, +0x0C = an undecoded kind word, +0x0E..+0x14 = x1,y1,x2,y2, then a class-specific body of CONSTANT length per class (40 of 41 classes), then an optional inline caption arena. Cross-checked against HDAE5000_WindowGeometry_Init (ROM 0x2F9C4C): its 20 records use the identical layout and their links agree with the ROM tree 33/33.

PACKAGE: 13 byte-neutral edits. Two of the five labels (UI_Page_Titles, Panel_Save_UI) are byte-affecting because hdae5000_init_data.s derives 7 `.set`s from them, so edit 7 re-bases those `.set`s onto the new pool label with verified-identical values FIRST; after that all five labels are free to rename. No .incbin, .byte, .short or instruction is touched; only comments, label names, one label moved 2 bytes up to the real record boundary, and two non-build files (symbols reference, a one-shot tool). Apply edits 1 and 7 before 2-5.

REPRODUCIBILITY: I was read-only, so I could not commit the verifier. Its full text is in evidence[0] and MUST be added as scripts/tools/verify_hdae5000_ui_pool.py in the same commit — every number in the header comment comes out of it.

; =============================================================================
; HD-AE5000 UI OBJECT DESCRIPTOR POOL  (0x29DC12 - 0x2A5D2B, 33,050 bytes)
; =============================================================================
; ONE array of 769 variable-length records.  It is not five tables.  The labels
; that used to cut it up - HDAE5000_UI_Descriptors here, and _UI_Page_Titles /
; _Panel_Save_UI / _Credits / _Demo_Data further down - each landed 0x02 to
; 0x3A bytes INSIDE a record, and the last four landed on a record's inline
; caption string.  See the retraction note at each of those four addresses.
;
; BOUNDARIES.  Record i begins at HDAE5000_UiObject_PtrTable[i] (0x2A5D2C) and
; ends where the next pool pointer begins; the 769th ends at 0x2A5D2C itself,
; so the pool is exactly the gap between the class-name strings above and that
; table, and the 769 lengths sum to exactly 33,050 bytes with nothing over.
; Those 769 addresses are the ONLY legal places for a label inside this pool.
; The pointer table has 789 entries plus a NULL; the other 20 objects keep
; their descriptor in sub-CPU work RAM at 0x239CC4-0x239FD1, initialised from
; HDAE5000_WindowGeometry_Init (ROM 0x2F9C4C) in this same record format.
;
; STRIDE.  There is none.  Lengths run 22..82 bytes in 26 distinct values, all
; even (42 B x178, 26 B x125, 40 B x105, 36 B x58, 60 B x46, 38 B x39, ...).
; A record is a fixed 22-byte header, a class-specific body whose length is
; constant per class, and an optional inline caption arena:
;
;   +0x00  .long   class id.  High half 0x016A = a class defined by THIS ROM,
;                  low half = index into HDAE5000_ClassName_Table (0x2F9832).
;                  High half 0x0160 = a class of the host KN5000 widget
;                  library, for which this ROM carries no name table.
;                  41 distinct ids: 12 of the 0x016A family, 29 of 0x0160.
;   +0x04  .short  parent object index,           or 0xFFFF
;   +0x06  .short  first-child object index,      or 0xFFFF
;   +0x08  .short  next-sibling object index,     or 0xFFFF
;   +0x0A  .short  previous-sibling object index, or 0xFFFF
;   +0x0C  .short  0x0008 (622 records) / 0x000A (62) / 0x0018 (85).
;                  INFERENCE: an object-kind or attribute word.  NOT decoded.
;   +0x0E  .short  x1  \
;   +0x10  .short  y1   |  bounding box, absolute screen pixels; the whole
;   +0x12  .short  x2   |  pool fits inside 0,0 - 321,239
;   +0x14  .short  y2  /
;   +0x16  ...     class-specific body, constant length F per class
;   tail           inline NUL-terminated captions for the classes that have
;                  caption slots, word-aligned with at most one 0x00 pad byte
;
; class      n   F  caption slot(s)   class      n   F  caption slot(s)
;   0160:0010    1  22  -             0160:0012   11  36  -
;   0160:001B   50  58  +0x1C         0160:001C    1  42  -
;   0160:001F   77  40  -             0160:0020   11  44  -
;   0160:0022   19  42  -             0160:0026    4  40  +0x1E,+0x1A
;   0160:0028    8  28  -             0160:0029   10  26  -  (see note 1)
;   0160:002B   97  32  +0x16         0160:002D    3  26  -
;   0160:002E   37  26  -             0160:0030    6  40  +0x16
;   0160:0033    1  34  -             0160:0035   13  36  -
;   0160:0036   43  40  +0x1A         0160:0037   16  38  +0x1A
;   0160:003D    2  50  +0x2A         0160:003E   25  44  +0x28
;   0160:003F   16  46  +0x2A         0160:0041   16  54  +0x2A
;   0160:0046    2  22  -             0160:0049   34  26  -
;   0160:004B    2  36  -             0160:004C    1  64  -  (see note 2)
;   0160:004D    4  26  -             0160:0052   27  26  -
;   0160:0069    9  26  -             016A:0000   31  60  -
;   016A:0001    1  26  -             016A:0002   24  42  +0x22
;   016A:0003    1  36  -             016A:0004    1  26  -
;   016A:0006   25  42  +0x22         016A:0007    1  42  +0x22
;   016A:0008    4  36  -             016A:0009   11  34  -
;   016A:000A  122  42  -             016A:000B    1  46  -
;   016A:000C    1  32  -
;
; EVIDENCE (all read out of original_ROMs/hd-ae5000_v2_06i.ic4, base 0x280000,
; by scripts/tools/verify_hdae5000_ui_pool.py):
;  * The four link fields are self-consistent with NO exception.  Over the
;    pairs whose both ends are ROM descriptors: next/prev symmetric 498/498;
;    a first child's parent is its owner 173/173; a chain head is its parent's
;    first child 173/173; siblings share a parent 498/498.  NEGATIVE CONTROL:
;    reading the same four .shorts at any other offset 0x00..0x16 scores 0 or
;    1 out of the same populations.  78 records have parent == 0xFFFF and they
;    are exactly the top-level screens (HDDMENU, SETUPS_TOOLS, SELECT_FILE,
;    SELECT_DIR, FD_FILE_SELECT, HARD_TEST, PC_DATA_LINK, LOAD_BY_NUM,
;    FLS_FILE_SEL, ...).
;  * The bounding box satisfies x1<=x2<=321 and y1<=y2<=239 for 769/769
;    records at +0x0E and at NO other offset (next best +0x1C with 478
;    violations, then +0x0C with 524, +0x10 with 739).  Record #0 is
;    0,0-319,239: the full screen.
;  * The class id decodes against HDAE5000_ClassName_Table[0..12], with four
;    exact hits and no counter-example: 016A:0003 is the single object named
;    HddNamingWindow and [3] is "AcHddNamingWindowProc"; 016A:0009 contains
;    the object named IV_HDDMENU and [9] is "IvScreenR2Proc"; 016A:000B is a
;    child of Tech_lyrics and [11] is "LyricBoxProc"; 016A:000C is a child of
;    LoadLyricFD and [12] is "FDFileSelectProc".  Semantically: 016A:0000 =
;    [0] "SelectListProc" holds SEL_DIR / LBN_*_BOX / CP_FD_LIST / SEL_FLS;
;    016A:0002 and 016A:0006 = the two "TtlScreenR*Proc" titled screens.
;    016A:0005 ("HDTitleMenuProc") has no static descriptor.
;  * 13 of the 41 classes carry a .long caption pointer at a fixed body
;    offset - 329 slots in 325 records.  Every one points into its OWN record
;    and the string it names runs to the record end.  Classes 0160:0026 (pool)
;    and 0160:004E (RAM image only) carry TWO: a toggle soft key whose two
;    states each have a caption - object 73 RUN_STOP is +0x1E "RUN" / +0x1A
;    "STOP", objects 75/76/77 PPORT_SW / FD_SW / HDD_SW repeat one word twice.
;  * Body length F is constant per class for 40 of the 41 classes.  Full
;    accounting: 30,252 B of bodies + 2,616 B of inline strings + 182 pad
;    bytes = 33,050 B, zero unexplained bytes.
;  * Independent confirmation of the whole layout: HDAE5000_WindowGeometry_Init
;    (ROM 0x2F9C4C-0x2F9F59) holds the 20 run-time descriptors in this same
;    format.  Their record lengths equal the RAM address deltas in the pointer
;    table, and every link field they carry agrees with the ROM tree, 33/33.
;
; NOTE 1: object #127 (class 0160:0029, under SETUP_TOOLS_P2) is the only
; record longer than its class body - it has "! HD FORMAT !" bolted on at
; +0x1A with no pointer of its own.  That string is the caption of the RAM
; object #128 SW_HD_FORMAT and is cited from the init image instead; it is
; HDAE5000_Str_Alert_HDFormat in hdae5000_init_data.s.
; NOTE 2: object #442 "HddNamingCursorBox" (class 0160:004C) ends with six
; 4-byte literals "ABC" "ABC" "abc" "abc" "!#$" "!#$" at +0x28..+0x3C.  Those
; are the captions of the RAM objects #443/444/445 HddNamingABC/abc/Symbol and
; are HDAE5000_Str_CharSet_* in hdae5000_init_data.s.
;
; Symbolising the 769 records is still a follow-up package; the boundaries it
; must use are the .long values of HDAE5000_UiObject_PtrTable, nothing else.
; =============================================================================

HDAE5000_UiDescriptor_Pool:	; 0x29DC12 = HDAE5000_UiObject_PtrTable[0]
	; ---- object #0 "HDDMENU", class 016A:0002 TtlScreenRProc, 52 bytes,
	;      full-screen 0,0-319,239, caption "HD-AE5000" at +0x2A ----
	.byte 0x02
	.byte 0x00

packages.area: symbols/maincpu_symbols_reference.txt — staleness audit, consumer census, and regeneration procedure
packages.summary:
The file is far staler than the LABEL_* count suggests, and CLAUDE.md's documented regeneration procedure cannot fix it.

STALENESS. Measured against rebuilt_ROMs/kn5000_v10_program.llvm.elf (whose .llvm.rom is byte-identical to original_ROMs/kn5000_v10_program.rom, so it is a valid current build): only 1,332 of 39,449 rows (3.4%) agree with the build on name+address. The 35,924 LABEL_* rows are the visible half; the other half is that of the 3,525 already-named rows, only 1,332 are right — 2,062 are ALL-CAPS manglings of MixedCase ELF symbols (this file says ACACCORDIONTABPROC, the source and ELF say AcAccordionTabProc) and 131 name routines that exist nowhere in any source. Addresses fared much better than names: 33,877 of the 39,235 distinct addresses still carry some symbol in the build.

ROOT CAUSE (three layers). (1) The file was generator output on 2026-02-01 (d95188d) from an ASL .map; ASL is case-insensitive here (no CASESENSITIVE anywhere under archive/asl/) so its map uppercases everything — hence the 2,062 manglings. Its "# Generated from:" provenance line was stripped on 2026-02-25 by 38da364; all four sibling files still carry theirs. (2) 3d87c95 (2026-03-23) moved sources maincpu/ -> v10/maincpu/ and 38e7d9f made the LLVM tree authoritative; since then 44 commits touched v10/maincpu and only 4 touched this file. (3) The tooling that kept them in step is dead: 44 scripts still edit "maincpu/kn5000_v10_program.s", a path deleted by 3d87c95; 11 of those also write this file.

WHY CLAUDE.md's PROCEDURE CANNOT WORK. It assembles archive/asl/maincpu/kn5000_v10_program.asm and extracts an ASL map — but that .asm is the deliberately ARCHIVED pre-rename tree: 35,786 of its 37,402 column-0 label definitions are still LABEL_*. Running it would reproduce the current staleness and re-apply the uppercasing on top. Its cleanup line also rm's maincpu/*.map, a directory that has not existed since 3d87c95.

CORRECT PROCEDURE (verified, ~1 second). Regenerate from the linked ELF via llvm-nm, filtering to type 't'. llvm-nm splits the table cleanly into 39,393 't' (.text ROM symbols) and 1,153 'a' (ABS register equates from tmp94c241.inc, constants not addresses). I built the candidate output and validated it: 39,393 rows, zero LABEL_, every row matching ^NAME 0x[0-9A-F]{6}$, address order strictly non-decreasing. I did NOT write it into the repo.

CONSUMERS. Nothing in the build reads it — no Makefile target mentions symbols/, there is no `make symbols`, and extract_symbols_from_map.py is unreferenced by the Makefile. So regenerating cannot change a ROM byte. All real consumers are prose, and they are already carrying wrong names: of the 13 addresses kn7000_mame/notes/HANDOFF-kn5000-demo-playback.md quotes as the accompaniment chain plus the one in FINDINGS-sound-name-error.md, not one of the 14 agrees with the build. docs/accompaniment-style-reader.md is built entirely on names (all 15 introduced by 3710b8b) that exist only in this file and that doc.

DELIVERABLE. Three comment/prose-only edits below: a documented header block in the symbols file, a corrected procedure in CLAUDE.md, and a corrected count table. No renames are proposed. No instruction, .byte/.short/.incbin directive, or branch-target label is touched, and none of these files is an assembler input, so no edit here can alter an assembled byte.

**Update procedure - directly edit the reference files when modifying assembly:**

Because regenerating from scratch takes ~70 minutes for maincpu, **always edit the symbol reference files directly** instead of regenerating:

- **Adding a label:** Insert a new line in the appropriate reference file, maintaining address sort order
- **Renaming a label:** Find and replace the old name with the new name
- **Removing a label:** Delete the corresponding line

**Example:** When adding `FDC_INIT_ROUTINE` at address `0xE12345` to maincpu:
```
# Find the correct position (after 0xE12344, before 0xE12346) and insert:
FDC_INIT_ROUTINE 0xE12345
```

**Full regeneration** (only if files become corrupted or majorly out of sync):
```bash
# Generate map files from archived ASL sources (maincpu takes ~70 minutes, others are fast)
ASL=../tools/asl/asl

$ASL -w -g map archive/asl/maincpu/kn5000_v10_program.asm -o /tmp/maincpu.p
$ASL -w -g map archive/asl/subcpu/kn5000_subprogram_v142.asm -o /tmp/subcpu.p
$ASL -w -g map archive/asl/subcpu/boot/kn5000_subcpu_boot.asm -o /tmp/subcpu_boot.p
$ASL -w -g map archive/asl/table_data/kn5000_table_data.asm -o /tmp/table_data.p
$ASL -w -g map archive/asl/hdae5000/hd-ae5000_v2_06i.asm -o /tmp/hdae5000.p

# Extract symbols from map files
python scripts/analysis/extract_symbols_from_map.py archive/asl/maincpu/kn5000_v10_program.map symbols/maincpu_symbols_reference.txt
python scripts/analysis/extract_symbols_from_map.py archive/asl/subcpu/kn5000_subprogram_v142.map symbols/subcpu_symbols_reference.txt
python scripts/analysis/extract_symbols_from_map.py archive/asl/subcpu/boot/kn5000_subcpu_boot.map symbols/subcpu_boot_symbols_reference.txt
python scripts/analysis/extract_symbols_from_map.py archive/asl/table_data/kn5000_table_data.map symbols/table_data_symbols_reference.txt
python scripts/analysis/extract_symbols_from_map.py archive/asl/hdae5000/hd-ae5000_v2_06i.map symbols/hdae5000_symbols_reference.txt

# Clean up intermediate files
rm /tmp/*.p maincpu/*.map subcpu/*.map subcpu/boot/*.map table_data/*.map hdae5000/*.map
```

NM="$HOME/compartilhado/llvm-project/build/bin/llvm-nm"
{  echo "# Symbol Reference File"
   echo "# Format: SYMBOL_NAME ADDRESS"
   "$NM" --defined-only rebuilt_ROMs/kn5000_v10_program.llvm.elf \
     | awk '$2=="t"{print $1, $3}'                               \
     | LC_ALL=C sort -k1,1 -k2,2                                 \
     | awk '{printf "%s 0x%s\n", $2, toupper(substr($1,3))}'
} > symbols/maincpu_symbols_reference.txt
```

The same shape works for the other four files against their own ELFs
(`kn5000_subprogram_v142`, `kn5000_subcpu_boot`, `kn5000_table_data`,
`hd-ae5000_v2_06i` — all eight `.llvm.elf` artifacts survive a build).
Verified 2026-08-21:

- `llvm-nm` splits the table cleanly into 39,393 `t` (`.text`, the ROM symbols)
  and 1,153 `a` (ABS register equates from `archive/asl/tmp94c241.inc`, which are
  constants, not addresses). Filtering on `t` is what drops the equates.
- `substr($1,3)` strips the leading `00` of llvm-nm's 8-digit address; every
  `.text` address is in `0x00E00000-0x00FFFFFF`, so this is lossless and gives
  the 6-digit form these files use.
- addresses are fixed-width hex, so `LC_ALL=C` lexicographic sort *is* numeric
  sort; the output was checked strictly non-decreasing over all 39,393 rows.
- `rebuilt_ROMs/` is `.gitignore`d, so the ELF must be built first. The build is
  byte-exact (`cmp rebuilt_ROMs/kn5000_v10_program.llvm.rom
  original_ROMs/kn5000_v10_program.rom`).

**Do NOT regenerate from an ASL map.** The old recipe assembled
`archive/asl/maincpu/kn5000_v10_program.asm` with `-g map` and ran
`scripts/analysis/extract_symbols_from_map.py`. Two things make that wrong now:

1. That `.asm` is the **archived pre-rename tree**: 35,786 of its 37,402 column-0
   label definitions are still `LABEL_*`. Regenerating from it reintroduces the
   staleness it is meant to cure.
2. ASL is case-insensitive here (no `CASESENSITIVE` directive anywhere under
   `archive/asl/`), so its map **uppercases every symbol**: you get
   `ACACCORDIONTABPROC` where the source and the ELF say `AcAccordionTabProc`.

The old recipe's cleanup line also removed `maincpu/*.map`, a directory deleted
by `3d87c95` (2026-03-23) when the tree moved to `v10/maincpu/`.

**Nothing in the build reads these files** — no Makefile target mentions
`symbols/` and `extract_symbols_from_map.py` is unreferenced by the Makefile — so
regenerating cannot change a ROM byte. It *will* invalidate names quoted in prose:
`docs/accompaniment-style-reader.md` and, in the `kn7000_mame` repo,
`notes/HANDOFF-kn5000-demo-playback.md`, `notes/FINDINGS-sound-name-error.md` and
`notes/kn5000-envelope-engine.md`. Fix those in the same commit.
edits.why: The documented procedure is the root cause: it regenerates from a deliberately archived pre-rename ASL tree (35,786/37,402 labels still LABEL_*) through a case-insensitive assembler, so following it reproduces the staleness plus uppercase mangling. The 'always hand-edit, never regenerate' rule it justifies with a ~70-minute cost is what let maincpu drift to 3.4% agreement while 44 commits changed v10/maincpu. Prose-only edit to a documentation file; no assembler input touched.

packages.area: Label misnomers: maincpu FDC seek handler + three HD-AE5000 registry-name contradictions
packages.summary:
All four backlog claims are CONFIRMED, and one is confirmed only in part.

(1) FDC_STATUS_HANDLER (0xF97696 in v9/v10, 0xF97289 in v7) is the SEEK command handler. Disassembled from the ROM it is instruction-for-instruction the twin of the bootloader's FDC_CmdSeek: compare target track vs track cache, return if equal, delay 2, clear result buffer, `ld WA,0x000f` (= FDC SEEK opcode 0x0F), issue, wait, invalidate cache on error, settle 16 ticks. It touches no status register. Correct name: FDC_CmdSeek (same twin-naming convention as the already-landed FDC_SeekRecalibrate -> FDC_CmdRecalibrate). It is NOT a label: it is a `.set` alias whose value is consumed by one `calr` per tree, so it IS call-target-bearing -- definition and use must be renamed together (byte-neutral, the value is an absolute constant). Bonus, verified the same way: the docs-only FDC_STATUS_HANDLER_2 (0xF976C9) is boot's FDC_SubmitReadDataCmd (issues 0xC6 = MT|MF READ DATA).

(2) HDAE5000_Alloc_Memory_4 (0x280395) -> HDAE5000_BitmapHdd_icon. CONFIRMED against the firmware registry.
(3) HDAE5000_Dir_Event_Check (0x28F2F7) -> HDAE5000_LanguageTextReturn. CONFIRMED; it returns the six-entry language-text file-stem table at 0x2E5D72 and has nothing to do with directories.
(4) HDAE5000_HD_Format_Dispatch (0x2837F2) -> HDAE5000_SEL_DIR_Screen. CONFIRMED; every arm drives RAM 0x23A08E, the browser row-base offset, over five 24-byte row slots. It formats nothing.

PARTIALLY WRONG PREMISE: the backlog wrote "HDAE5000_Alloc_Memory*" with a star. Only the FOURTH one is registry-named. I read all registry tables out of the ROM and cross-checked all 96 name/handler pairs: there are EXACTLY three mismatches repo-wide, and they are exactly the three above. 0x28030E / 0x28033B / 0x280368 / 0x28F543 appear in NO registry table, so there is no firmware name for them to contradict. They are still misnomers on code evidence (they allocate nothing), but I have deliberately NOT renamed them -- a rename there would be an invented name, not the firmware's. That call belongs to Felipe; their full reference list is in "uncertain".

The 32 edits below are comments plus renames only. No instruction, no .byte/.short/.incbin, no assembled byte changes: every rename touches the symbol's definition and every use in the same assembly unit, and every renamed symbol's value is an absolute constant or an in-file label whose displacement is unchanged.

### FDC_STATUS_HANDLER (0xF97696) - Status/Interrupt Handler

Checks and updates FDC status, handles interrupts.

```asm

edits.replacement:
### FDC_CmdSeek (0xF97696) - Command 2: Seek

Seeks to the target track.  No-op when the track cache (0x8B04) already matches
the requested track (0x8A36); otherwise it delays 2, clears the result buffer,
issues SEEK (`LD WA, 000Fh` -> 0x0F), waits for the result, sets the track cache
to 0xFF if the error byte 0x8A24 is non-zero, and settles for 16 ticks.
Instruction-for-instruction twin of the bootloader's `FDC_CmdSeek`
(table_data/boot_fdc_driver.s, 0xFFE31A).  It reads and writes no status
register and handles no interrupt: the old name FDC_STATUS_HANDLER was a
misnomer.

```asm
FDC_CmdSeek:                ; F97696
edits.why: Documentation only. Column 29 for the `;` is preserved (FDC_CmdSeek: is 12 chars + 16 spaces, matching FDC_SH_L1: below it).

packages.summary:
SCOPE. "DSP zone files" = the two files that own zones A0 (0x00F7E6-0x012114), A (0x012195-0x014738) and B (0x0147B3-0x01E17E): v142/subcpu/subcpu_data_tables.s and symbols/proposals/subcpu-region-01.txt. subcpu_data_tables.s carries NO [UNCERTAIN] entries of its own — only three cross-references (lines 210, 1387, 4028) pointing into the proposal files. Every actual [UNCERTAIN] entry for these zones lives in region-01, in three blocks (lines 520, 535, 562) that decompose into 16 individual claims. I also checked the one zone-related [UNCERTAIN] in region-05.

FIRST FINDING — THE BACKLOG ITEM IS ALREADY DONE. The task's premise ("entries for 0x00F7E6-0x012114 and 0x012171-0x014738 should be retired") was executed on 2026-08-08 in commit d2aba93 ("issues: reconcile the wave-audited records with the live tracker"). `git show d2aba93 -- symbols/proposals/subcpu-region-01.txt` shows the two [DATA] entries and the "Not resolved in this pass" bullet all rewritten with RETIRED/RESOLVED 2026-08-08 prose, and the same commit retired region-05's "0x00FEE4/0x0119C8/0x010764/0x011AE8 are all unnamed, buried in the anonymous blob" bullet. Working tree is clean. There is nothing left to retire for those two ranges, and I propose no edit there. Re-doing it would have produced a duplicate retirement notice.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY STILL RETIRABLE — 16 claims audited, 5 retired, 11 kept.

RETIRED (evidence below, edits attached):
1. ToneGen_WorkArea (0x014777) "declared 44,991-byte extent swallows the touch curves and the FP pool" — FALSE now. Next symbol is DSP_Bytecode_Global_Config (0x0147B3): implied extent 0x3C = 60 bytes. The name half of the bullet stands and gets sharper (60 = 5 x the 12-byte descriptor the interpreter reads; 5 = the slot count declared by the chip table at 0x01ED6D = 00 00 01 01 01; all 60 bytes are zero in the image).
2. Audio_DSP_StateTable_Packed (0x012171) "9,672-byte extent" — FALSE now. Next symbol ToneGen_VoiceType_Default_Level (0x012177): 6 bytes, exactly the pitch-bias table. Name half stands.
3. PitchDetune_OffsetTable "10,706-byte mixed data segment with at least 60 members" — FALSE now. Next symbol Voice_Part_Trim_Table_B (0x00F79A): 19 bytes. Its ELF address is 0x00F787 (not 0x00F77F as the bullet says), 8 bytes past the selector-matrix column at 0x00F77F, landing one byte inside the 20-byte s16 trim table at 0x00F786-0x00F799. "Neither pitch nor detune established" stands.
4. "The consumer of the 10-entry pointer array at 0x01F3F0" — FOUND. Two consumers over two 5-entry runs: EFF_Disconnect (0x037F4F, base 0x01F3F0) and EFF_Link (0x037FAE, base 0x01F404), both computing *(base + 12*mode + 4*slot) and feeding DSP_WriteGlobalConfig. All ten pointer values verified byte-for-byte against the ROM.
5. "The exponential-looking 4-byte ramp starting near 0x00F0A0" — FOUND, and the note was wrong about where it is. It starts at 0x00F140 (0x00F09D-0x00F0BB is 31 bytes of zeros), is 128 x u32 ending at exactly 0x7FFFFF00, and its consumer is DSP_MixerCoeff_Compute (0x03C067), three sites `lda_d16 xbc, 61760`. Both its edges are exact: DSP_Reset copies 0x122 = 290 bytes from 0x00F01E to DRAM 0x448E and 0x00F01E + 0x122 = 0x00F140; at 0x00F340 the double-precision libm pool begins.

KEPT, and why (11):
- The eleven 8-byte-skewed ELF symbols (0x00F693..0x00F787): re-verified as STILL TRUE today against a freshly built ELF; llvm-nm still reports PitchBend_DispatchTable 0x00F69B / Voice_GroupOffsets_A 0x00F6AF / ... while the ROM shows the real tables start at the code-referenced anchors. Closing it needs label re-anchoring, which is out of my brief.
- FPConst_Ln2 (0x00F42C = sqrt(2)), Voice_Pitch_Table_High, Voice_KeyTable_Remapping, Voice_SFX_ModulationTable, Const_ChannelMax/Const_Zero_Byte, MIDI_NoteFreqTable, OFFSETS_F460/OFFSETS_14739/OFFSETS_14745/CALL_TABLE_12159: llvm-nm confirms every one of these names is unchanged in the current build, so the uncertainty (should we rename?) is untouched by the zone carve. I did strengthen the FPConst_Ln2 case — the REAL ln(2) is at 0x00F3D2 and is referenced by subcpu_fp_math.s:2851 — but a fact getting stronger is not a rename getting done.
- The Voice_ToneRampFilter_Curve index overrun (region-05, cross-referenced from subcpu_data_tables.s:1387): the neighbouring table is named now but that does not decide "deliberate second domain vs firmware defect". The 26-entry curve ends 0xF6,0xFF and the bytes it runs into are 0x20,0x20,0x20,0x20,0x21 — a hard discontinuity, suggestive but not proof of intent. Left alone.
- The effect-metadata bases 0x143AD/0x14411/0x145A1: re-verified still unfound — no absolute operand for any of the three exists in either .s file, exactly as subcpu_data_tables.s:2911 already says.
- The external-interrupt vectors 11..19 and the ToneGen_Poll_All keybed-vs-tone-generator conflict: unrelated to the DSP zones and untouched by the carve.

ONE OUT-OF-BAND CORRECTION noted but NOT edited: region-01:285 says "The trailing 0x00 at 0x00F785 is padding, not a 4th row". The ROM says 0x00F77D..0x00F785 = 00 01 06 03 05 08 02 04 07 — nine bytes, exactly the three rows the same entry lists; 0x00F785 holds 0x07, and the 0x00 is at 0x00F786, where it is the first byte of the trim table. Fix it while applying edit 3 if you want; I left it out of the package to keep the package to UNCERTAIN work.

All 8 edits are COMMENT-ONLY. No instruction, no .byte/.short/.long/.incbin/.zero/.fill directive, no label, and no branch target is touched. No rename is proposed or applied. Edits 4 and 6 mention candidate names for 0x01F3F0/0x01F404 as prose only, and say explicitly that adding them would require splitting a data run and is the integrator's call.

   XBC to DSP_ParameterWriteEngine at three further sites (v142/subcpu/kn5000_subprogram_v142.s

edits.anchor: * The consumer of the 10-entry pointer array at 0x01F3F0 (into 0x01E5C8..0x01E630).
edits.replacement:
* RESOLVED 2026-08-21 (was: the consumer of the 10-entry pointer array at 0x01F3F0). There are
   TWO consumers, over two contiguous five-entry runs, both in region 13's effect layer:
     EFF_Disconnect (0x037F4F)  base 0x01F3F0, and
     EFF_Link       (0x037FAE)  base 0x01F404   (`ld xbc, 0x1F404` in the body).
   Each computes *(base + 12*mode + 4*slot), takes chip = byte(0x01ED6D + slot) (00 00 01 01 01),
   and calls DSP_WriteGlobalConfig(chip, program). The ten targets are therefore ten small DSP
   global-configuration bytecode programs of 11-12 bytes each: five "disconnect" programs
   (0x01E5C8, 0x01E5D3, 0x01E5DE, 0x01E5EA, 0x01E5F6) and five "link" programs (0x01E602,
   0x01E60D, 0x01E618, 0x01E624, 0x01E630) -- all ten read straight out of the ROM image.
   The sibling array at 0x01F3E0 (4 x u32 -> 0x01EA78, 0x01EA87, 0x01EA96, 0x01EAA5) belongs to
   DSP_Unmute_WithDebug (0x037F1C).
   WHAT REPLACES THIS BULLET as the open item is the stride defect the answer exposes, already
   flagged in the source header at kn5000_subprogram_v142.s:45211-45215: five pointers per run
   means a natural mode stride of 20, but both routines compute 12 (`xde = mode*3; sll 2`). With
   mode == 1, EFF_Disconnect slots 2/3/4 fetch 0x01F404/0x01F408/0x01F40C -- LINK programs -- and
   EFF_Link slot 4 fetches 0x01F420, which is past the end of the array (it lands inside the
   tone-generator velocity block and reads 0x1000D000, not a payload address at all). I did not
   establish whether mode == 1 with slot >= 2 is reachable in practice; that is the next step.
edits.why: The bullet asks a question the tree now answers with a literal `ld xbc, 0x1F3F0` / `ld xbc, 0x1F404` in two named routines, and every pointer value in the note is reproducible from the ROM. Leaving it listed as unresolved sends the next reader hunting for something already documented 6,000 lines away in the code file. The replacement keeps an open item rather than closing the topic, because the answer surfaces a genuine out-of-bounds read whose reachability is still unknown.

packages.area: v142 sub-CPU: the three envelope generators (IC303 registers 0x20-0x29) and their builders
packages.summary: All three envelopes are built from ONE parameter record, `paramA` = the u32 at voice-slot+0x17 (NOT the tone record at slot+0x23 — three existing comment blocks say "tonerec+NN" where the code reads paramA+NN). Envelope 1 (amplitude, regs 0x20/0x21/0x22) is built by the four Voice_Calc_LevelPair_* routines from paramA+0x27..+0x2C on the type-4 path and from paramA+0x08..+0x0D on the type-1/2 path; envelope 2 (regs 0x24/0x25/0x26) by Voice_Level_ComputeTriplet from paramA+0x09..+0x0E; envelope 3 (regs 0x27/0x28/0x29) by Voice_StereoLevel_Compute from paramA+0x3D..+0x44. Envelope 3's parameter block is envelope 2's block moved up EXACTLY 54 bytes — 17 of 17 fields mirror, including the per-tick writers EGB/EGC. The distinguishing difference is the rate byte: envelope 1's rates are unsigned indexes into Voice_EnvelopeRate_Table (0x011963, 0x00..0x7F, bit 7 always clear), while envelopes 2 and 3 push a SIGNED byte through Detune_ScaleSymmetric, giving -0x7F..+0x7F with bit 7 set for negative parameters — which collides with the documented "apply now" meaning of bit 7. The measured write pattern has a mechanical cause: a census of every `add wa, <bank>` latch in the file shows banks +0x880/+0x980/+0xA40 (segment 2 of each envelope) and +0x8C0 have NO per-tick writer at all — only ToneGen_WriteVoiceParams's 22-register dump reaches them — whereas segments 0 and 1 have a second, parallel shadow (0x0451F8..0x045202) that ToneGen_WriteLevelBurst pushes on every tick. Rate 0 = "arrive immediately" is confirmed from the firmware side three ways: the mute idiom (11 literal sites) is r0x21<-0xFF00 / r0x20<-0xFF80, both rate 0; every per-tick level writer emits rate 0; and the `max(rate,4)` applied to segment 1 in all four builders is a pure rate-0 guard, because entry 0 is the only entry of Voice_EnvelopeRate_Table below 4. That same evidence fixes the target polarity (0xFF = silent) and shows two existing comments have it backwards.

; In: XWA = voice work record; XIZ = (record+0x17) = the patch parameter block.

; 0x0E) are used as-is or negated. If (patch+0x11) != 0 an envelope-scaled offset from
; PitchBend_Scale is added to each of the three level bytes (patch+0x09/0x0B/0x0D)
; after they are mapped through the byte table at 0x0118FE.
; Velocity modulation uses Pan_ScaleWithVelocity with limits (patch+0x13)..0x7F and
; depths (patch+0x14) / (patch+0x15).

; 0x0451EC, 0x0451EE and 0x0451F0. Callers 0x02B510, 0x02BD03.
edits.replacement:
; ENVELOPE 2 -- IC303 registers r0x24 / r0x25 / r0x26 (banks +0x900 / +0x940 / +0x980).
; In: XWA = voice-slot record; XIZ = paramA = the u32 at slot+0x17 (the patch parameter
; block -- NOT the tone record, which is the pointer at slot+0x23).
; Out: the three staging words 0x0451EC, 0x0451EE, 0x0451F0. Callers 0x02B510 inside
; Voice_Build_Register_Set (0x02B4E3, type-4 note-on) and 0x02BD03 inside
; Voice_Release_Type4 (0x02BCD6, the per-tick rebuild) -- type-4 voices ONLY. On the
; type-1/type-2 path this envelope is never built: Voice_Level_ClearAllOutputRegs zeroes
; all three words instead.
;
; Same word format as envelope 1, (target << 8) | rate, one (target,rate) couple per
; segment, consecutive in the record:
;   seg 0  target Voice_EnvelopeLevel_Curve[paramA+0x09]   rate from paramA+0x0A
;   seg 1  target Voice_EnvelopeLevel_Curve[paramA+0x0B]   rate from paramA+0x0C
;   seg 2  target Voice_EnvelopeLevel_Curve[paramA+0x0D]   rate from paramA+0x0E
; The three targets share one key-scale term, PitchBend_Scale(paramA+0x11, slot+0x0C,
; shift 4), added only when paramA+0x11 != 0, and each is clamped 0..0xFF. Velocity
; modulation is Pan_ScaleWithVelocity(baseline paramA+0x13, limits 0..0x7F, control word
; slot+0x08) with depth paramA+0x14 on segment 0 and paramA+0x15 shared by segments 1/2.
; Target 0x00 is the LOUD end and 0xFF the silent end (0x0118FE descends 0xFF..0x04).
;
; THE RATE BYTES ARE SIGNED HERE -- this is what distinguishes envelopes 2 and 3 from
; envelope 1. They do NOT pass through Voice_EnvelopeRate_Table; each is (i8)paramA+0x0A /
; +0x0C / +0x0E pushed through Detune_ScaleSymmetric, which clamps |x| to 0x32, looks up
; Detune_Scale_Curve (0x0119C8) and NEGATES the result for negative inputs, so the low byte
; spans -0x7F..+0x7F and has bit 7 SET whenever the parameter is negative. The whole triple
; is negated up front when (i8)paramA+0x07 < 0. Rate 0 still comes out as 0, since
; Detune_Scale_Curve[0] = 0.
; INFERENCE: bit 7 of the low byte is documented as the "apply now" strobe in bank +0x800.
; If it means the same thing in banks +0x900/+0x9C0, a negative parameter raises that strobe
; as a side effect; the alternative is that bit 7 is a rate SIGN in these banks. Nothing in
; the firmware settles it -- no code here ever tests bit 7 of a value it reads back.
;
; MIRROR: envelope 3 (Voice_StereoLevel_Compute, 0x024664) is this same parameter block
; moved up by exactly 54 bytes. 0x07/0x09/0x0A/0x0B/0x0C/0x0D/0x0E/0x11/0x13/0x14/0x15 map
; onto 0x3D/0x3F/0x40/0x41/0x42/0x43/0x44/0x47/0x49/0x4A/0x4B, 11 for 11, and the per-tick
; writers mirror too (EGB reads 0x0F/0x10/0x16, EGC reads 0x45/0x46/0x4C). The one field
; whose ROLE differs is the first: paramA+0x07 is a sign flag that negates envelope 2's
; rates, while paramA+0x3D is ADDED to each of envelope 3's rate offsets.
edits.why: The existing header calls the low byte a "detune" and the base record "the patch parameter block" while the sibling routines call the same pointer "tonerec"; it also does not say which segment each couple feeds or that this envelope is only built for type-4 voices. The exact-54-byte mirror onto envelope 3 (17 fields verified) is the cleanest statement of what distinguishes the three envelopes' sources.

; PitchBend_Scale(tonerec+71, voice+12) is added to all three. tonerec+74 / tonerec+75
; add an LFO/tremolo term via Pan_ScaleWithVelocity. Each result is clamped 0..0xFF and
; packed as (level << 8) | Detune_ScaleSymmetric(clamp(tonerec+61 + tonerec+64/66/68,
; -0x32..+0x32)) -- i.e. an 8-bit level in the high byte and a signed spread coefficient in
; the low byte, the same layout the mute path uses when it writes 0xFF80.
; Confidence medium only because the *meaning* of the three destination registers is taken
; from technics-docs/tone-generator.md, not proved here.
edits.replacement:
; ENVELOPE 3 -- IC303 registers r0x27 / r0x28 / r0x29 (banks +0x9C0 / +0xA00 / +0xA40).
; In: XWA = voice-slot record. Out: the staging words 0x0451F2, 0x0451F4, 0x0451F6.
; Callers: Voice_Build_Register_Set (0x02B4E3) and Voice_Release_Type4 (0x02BCD6) -- type-4
; voices only; on the type-1/type-2 path Voice_Level_ClearAllOutputRegs zeroes these three
; words instead and this routine never runs.
;
; BASE-RECORD CORRECTION: the record read here is paramA, the u32 at slot+0x17 (`ld xwa,
; (xwa+23)` in the prologue), NOT the tone record -- that is the pointer at slot+0x23, as
; Voice_Calc_LevelPair_Full_OscTablePath states. Every "tonerec+NN" written in the comments
; from here to Voice_StereoLevel_PackCh23 means paramA+NN.
;
; Word format (target << 8) | rate, one couple per segment:
;   seg 0  target Voice_EnvelopeLevel_Curve[paramA+0x3F]   rate offset paramA+0x40
;   seg 1  target Voice_EnvelopeLevel_Curve[paramA+0x41]   rate offset paramA+0x42
;   seg 2  target Voice_EnvelopeLevel_Curve[paramA+0x43]   rate offset paramA+0x44
; Each rate = Detune_ScaleSymmetric(clamp((i8)paramA+0x3D + (i8)offset, -0x32..+0x32)), so
; it is SIGNED, -0x7F..+0x7F, exactly as in envelope 2 and unlike envelope 1's unsigned
; Voice_EnvelopeRate_Table lookup. paramA+0x3D is a bias shared by all three segments (and
; by r0x23, which Voice_PortaLevel_Compute builds from paramA+0x3D + paramA+0x3E).
; Targets take a shared key scale PitchBend_Scale(paramA+0x47, slot+0x0C, shift 4) when
; paramA+0x47 != 0, plus Pan_ScaleWithVelocity(baseline paramA+0x49, limits 0..0x7F,
; control word slot+0x08) with depth paramA+0x4A on segment 0 and paramA+0x4B shared by
; segments 1/2; each is then clamped 0..0xFF. 0xFF is the silent end of the curve.
;
; This parameter block is byte-for-byte envelope 2's block moved up 54 bytes (see
; Voice_Level_ComputeTriplet for the 17-field correspondence), with one role difference:
; paramA+0x07 is a sign flag that NEGATES envelope 2's rates, while paramA+0x3D is ADDED to
; envelope 3's rate offsets before the +-0x32 clamp.
; STILL UNPROVEN: what the chip DOES with registers 0x27..0x29 -- the word format and the
; parameter sources above are read off the code, the register semantics are not.
edits.why: The header names the wrong base record (it reads slot+0x17, not the tone record), which makes every offset in this routine's comments unverifiable, and it describes the low byte as a "spread coefficient" rather than the segment rate that the mirror with envelope 2 and the shared word format identify. Also states the caller set and the type-1/2 exclusion, neither of which was recorded.

edits.replacement:
; _PatchAtk takes its first-pair attack from the patch record, _FixedAtk uses a
; fixed one; _Full adds an oscillator-table branch and _Mono drops the base-pair
; oscillator trim.
;
; WHERE ENVELOPE 1'S SEGMENTS COME FROM. paramA = the u32 at slot+0x17, tonerec = the u32
; at slot+0x23. Targets index a DESCENDING attenuation curve (0xFF = silent); rates index
; Voice_EnvelopeRate_Table (0x011963, 0x00..0x7F, so bit 7 is always clear here -- unlike

;
;   TYPE-4 voices -- _PatchAtk (note-on, from Voice_Build_Register_Set 0x02B4E3) and
;   _Full / _Mono (per-tick rebuild, from Voice_Release_Type4 0x02BCD6):
;     seg 0  target Voice_LevelPair_AttackCurve[clamp(paramA+0x27 + (i8)tonerec[0x6B],
