;            rate   Voice_EnvelopeRate_Table[paramA+0x28]
;     seg 1  target Voice_EnvelopeLevel_Curve[paramA+0x29]
;            rate   max(4, Voice_EnvelopeRate_Table[paramA+0x2A])
;     seg 2  target Voice_EnvelopeLevel_Curve[paramA+0x2B]
;            rate   Voice_EnvelopeRate_Table[paramA+0x2C]     -- no floor
;     Modulation: key scale PitchBend_Scale(paramA+0x2E, slot+0x0C) on segment 0 and
;     paramA+0x2F on segments 1/2; Pan_ScaleWithVelocity with the control triple
;     paramA+0x30..0x32 and depths paramA+0x33 (seg 0) / paramA+0x34 (segs 1,2); every sum
;     re-clamped 0..0xFF.
;
;   TYPE-1/TYPE-2 voices -- _FixedAtk (from Voice_Init_Type1 0x02C3CC / _Type2 0x02C0B6):
;     seg 0  target Voice_LevelPair_AttackCurve[paramA+0x08], key scale paramA+0x0E
;            rate   the CONSTANT 0x7F -- the "FixedAtk" the name refers to
;     seg 1  target Voice_EnvelopeLevel_Curve[paramA+0x09]
;            rate   max(4, Voice_EnvelopeRate_Table[paramA+0x0A])
;     seg 2  target Voice_EnvelopeLevel_Curve[paramA+0x0B]
;            rate   Voice_EnvelopeRate_Table[paramA+0x0C], or 0 when bit 5 of
;                   (*(slot+0x13))[+0x0D] is clear
;     Those are the same bytes envelope 2 reads on the type-4 path, which is legal because
;     the type-1/2 chain calls Voice_Level_ClearAllOutputRegs and never builds envelope 2 or
;     3 -- the two paths bind different record kinds to slot+0x17 (Voice_Allocate_Typed vs
;     Voice_NoteOn_Type3).

; slot+0x3E / slot+0x40 and pushed to 0x0451E6 / 0x0451E8 by Voice_WriteChPanShift 0x02591D
; / _2 0x025B6F, which may add the signed byte tonerec[0x20] to the RATE field (gated on
; bits 8/9 of (*(slot+0x27))[+0x18]) and re-clamps segment 1's rate to [4..0x7F] and
; segment 2's to [0..0x7F]. _Full and _Mono write all three shadows themselves. The seg-0
; word is additionally cached in slot+0x3C.
;
; RATE 0 IS SPECIAL, AND THE FIRMWARE GUARDS IT. Voice_EnvelopeRate_Table begins {0x00,
; 0x04, 0x08, 0x0A, ...}: entry 0 is the ONLY entry below 4. So the max(4, ...) applied to
; segment 1 in all four builders, and the [4..0x7F] clamp Voice_WriteChPanShift applies to
; the same field, have exactly one effect between them -- they turn a rate of 0 into 4.
; Segments 0 and 2 are deliberately left free to carry rate 0. That is the firmware itself
; saying rate 0 means "arrive immediately" (harmless on an attack target and on the final
; target, fatal on a decay that has to be heard), and it agrees with the mute idiom r0x20 <-
; 0xFF80 / r0x21 <- 0xFF00 and with every per-tick writer, all of which emit rate 0.
edits.why: This family header states the word format and the three couples but not where a couple's bytes come from, that _FixedAtk reads a completely different offset window, that segments 1/2 reach the shadows only via Voice_WriteChPanShift, or that the max(4,..) is a rate-0 guard. The last point is the firmware's own evidence for the staging block's 'rate 0 = go now' claim and was nowhere recorded.

It sits on exactly the question 'where does segment 0's target come from', so it misleads at the worst possible place.

edits.anchor: ; Clamps the modulation depth before it is applied.
edits.replacement:
; NOT a modulation depth -- this is segment 1's RATE, floored at 4. Voice_EnvelopeRate_Table
; has exactly one entry below 4 (entry 0 = 0x00), so the floor's sole effect is to turn a
; rate of 0 into 4: a rate-0 guard on the decay segment. Segments 0 and 2 are left free to
; use rate 0, which the chip takes as "arrive immediately".
edits.why: The comment calls a rate a modulation depth, and it hides the single most informative fact about the rate field: that the firmware special-cases the value 0 on the one segment where an instant jump would be audible as a missing decay.

edits.anchor: ; This is the "silence everything except the mode word" primitive used on voice teardown.
edits.replacement:
; NOT a silence primitive, and not teardown-only. The value written is 0x0000 = target 0x00
; at rate 0, and 0x00 is the UN-attenuated end of both level curves -- the silent end is
; 0xFF, per the mute idiom r0x21 <- 0xFF00 / r0x20 <- 0xFF80 that Voice_SetPitch's header
; calls "the documented mute level word". Its only two callers are Voice_Init_Type2 (reached
; from the Voice_SetVelocity note-on paths) and Voice_Init_Type1 (reached from Voice_SetPitch

; included. What it actually does is switch envelopes 2 and 3 and register 0x23 OFF for the
; voice types that do not use them, leaving envelope 1 in sole charge of the level.
edits.why: Both halves of the sentence are wrong and both matter to anyone modelling the envelopes: 0x0000 is full-open rather than silent under the polarity the mute idiom establishes, and the routine's two callers are the type-1/type-2 rebuild paths (one of which is the note-on path), not teardown.

edits.anchor: ; Otherwise stage silence (0x0451F8 = 0x0080, 0x0451FA = 0x0000).
edits.replacement:

; 0xFF00 (Voice_SetPitch), and both level curves put the silent end at 0xFF.
edits.why: Under the polarity the 11-site mute idiom establishes, 0x0080 is the opposite of silence. A model that follows this comment will mute a voice where the hardware opens it fully.

edits.replacement:

uncertain: Whether bit 7 of the low byte means 'apply now' in banks +0x900/+0x9C0 as it does in +0x800. Envelopes 2 and 3 set it as a side effect of a negative rate parameter (Detune_ScaleSymmetric output), and EGB/EGC never set it deliberately, so it may be a rate SIGN in those banks. No firmware code reads the bit back, so the ROM cannot decide it. The proposed comment marks this INFERENCE.

Whether rate 0x7F is the fastest or the slowest non-zero ramp. Rate 0 = 'arrive now' is well supported (the mute idiom, every per-tick writer, the floor-at-4 guard), but Voice_InitVoiceState writes 0xFF7F to 0x0451E4 and _FixedAtk hard-codes 0x7F as its attack rate, and I could not tell from the ROM whether those mean 'as fast as a ramp can go' or 'as slow as it can go'. I made no claim either way.

Whether register 0x23 (+0x8C0) is really 'amplitude envelope segment 3'. Its two bytes come from Voice_PortaLevel_ScaleAndPack via paramA+0x08 and paramA+0x3D+0x3E through Detune_ScaleSymmetric -- the third envelope's parameter family, not the +0x27..+0x2C run that feeds segments 0-2. That is a source-side observation only; it does not contradict the capture-side finding that r0x23 decays to zero on ~4% of notes, so I left the staging-block row as it stands and only noted the source.

The physical meaning of registers 0x24..0x29. Everything above is about which bytes the firmware puts there and when; what IC303 does with three parallel three-segment generators (per-oscillator amplitude? auxiliary send levels? filter/pitch envelopes?) is still not established, and the existing 'confidence medium' caveat on Voice_StereoLevel_Compute is preserved in reworded form.

Whether _FixedAtk's paramA+0x08..+0x0D and Voice_Level_ComputeTriplet's paramA+0x09..+0x0E are literally the same physical fields. Both routines dereference slot+0x17, but the two allocation paths (Voice_Allocate_Typed vs Voice_NoteOn_Type3) bind different record kinds there, and the same byte paramA+0x0A is read once as an unsigned Voice_EnvelopeRate_Table index and once as a signed Detune_ScaleSymmetric input. I stated the overlap and the non-conflict (type-1/2 never builds envelope 2) without claiming the fields are identical.

I could not check the capture that produced 'segment 2 written exactly once per note-on' / 'segment 3 used on ~4% of notes' -- those numbers come from commit 4ff764a and no artefact for them is in the repo. My census shows two rarely-taken routines (ToneGen_WriteEnvSegments, ToneGen_WriteSegRegs_SameLevel) that CAN write +0x880 a second time, so the measurement is consistent with the code only if those branches did not fire; the proposed text says so explicitly.

I did not rebuild the ROM to confirm the edits are comment-only (the task is read-only and forbids `make`). Every proposed change is inside a `;` comment; none touches an instruction, directive, label or symbols/*.txt entry, and no rename is proposed anywhere. Two labels I comment on -- Voice_WriteVolume_OrPan_Muted (`jr z` target) and Voice_Calc_LevelPair_Silence (`call` target) -- are misleadingly named under the 0xFF = silent polarity, but I deliberately propose no rename for either.

packages.area: KN5000 sub-CPU keybed / touch (velocity) front end — boot ROM (IC30) and v1.42 payload
packages.summary:
Key events enter the sub-CPU through TWO ports, not one: (0x110002) = keybed STATUS word, (0x110000) = keybed DATA word. Both the v1.42 payload and the BOOT ROM contain a complete, independent front end for them.

PAYLOAD (runtime path, already partly documented): Audio_Main_Loop -> ToneGen_Process_Notes (0x03D01E) -> Keybed_Read_Event (0x03D0C5) -> Keybed_Decode_Event (0x03D11F). Decoded events do NOT reach the tone generator directly: ToneGen_Process_Notes builds a 3-byte MIDI message 0x90/note/velocity at 0x004A42 and DMAs it to the MAIN CPU (only if the enable byte 0x004A4A == 1). The main CPU then drives the TG voice registers back through the staging block at 0x0451CE / ToneGen_WriteVoicePitch. So the keybed's answer to "how does a key become a note the TG is given" is: it becomes a MIDI note-on sent upstream, and comes back as voice-register writes.

BOOT ROM (completely undocumented as a keybed path — this is the main find): INIT_MEMORY_TEST (0xFF8956) -> SERIAL_INIT (0xFF8B07) -> CONTROL_PANEL_BIT_SET_CLEAR (0xFF8B37) -> INTER_CPU_LATCH_READ_DISPATCH (0xFF8B89) -> NOTE_VELOCITY_LOOKUP_CALCULATE (0xFF8BD2). All four names are wrong. It is the FACTORY KEYBED TEST: gated on the CN12 "Sub CPU Checking Device" strap (PC.0 == 0), it blinks the 4-bit self-test status on the CN12 LED (PC.1) via DELAY_ROUTINE, writes 0x0003 to the keybed port, clears an 8-byte key-down bitmap at 0x0558, and then loops forever lighting the CN12 LED whenever any key is held. Single-caller chain, no other references — dead code unless the strap is fitted.

VELOCITY DERIVATION (identical algorithm, byte-identical tables in both ROMs, verified):
  strength   = Velocity_Input_Curve[raw_touch]            (0xFF804C / 0x01F43E)
  intermediate = gain/128 * (strength - 77) + pivot_out - (black key ? trim : 0)
  velocity   = Velocity_Output_Curve[clamp(intermediate,0,255)]   (0xFF814C / 0x01F53E)
gain/pivot_out/trim are the 3-byte record for the selected touch mode (0xFF802E / 0x01F420, 10 rows); the payload selects with the byte at 0x004A48 (default 6), the boot ROM hard-codes mode 6.

TWO WRONG CLAIMS CORRECTED: (1) bit 7 of the key byte is SET for a key DOWN and CLEAR for a key UP — the payload comments say "bit 7 = release flag", the opposite; ToneGen_Poll_Read (0x03D230) independently sets the bitmap bit when bit 7 is 1. (2) 0x004A4C is indexed by MIDI NOTE (0x4A70..0x4AAC for the 61 keys), not "16 voice slots at 0x4A4C-0x4A5C".

MAME: subcpu_mem maps 0x110000-0x110003 .noprw(), and handler_entry_read_nop returns m_space->unmap() which is initialised to 0 (emumem_aspace.cpp:602). So the status word reads 0, bit 0 is never set, and Keybed_Read_Event returns 0xFFFF on every call — the keybed can never produce an event today. The headers below state the exact port contract an implementation must honour.

edits.anchor:
; INTER_CPU_LATCH_READ_DISPATCH (0xFF8B89) - Inter-CPU communication handler
;
; Reads data from inter-CPU communication latches at 0x110000-0x110002.
; Checks status bits and dispatches to NOTE_VELOCITY_LOOKUP_CALCULATE for processing.
;
; Input: XWA = pointer to parameter buffer
; Output: HL = 0 on success, 0xFFFF on error/no data
edits.replacement:
; INTER_CPU_LATCH_READ_DISPATCH (0xFF8B89)
; ⚠ MISNOMER: nothing inter-CPU happens here.  This is the boot ROM's KEYBED FIFO READER --
; it pops one key event from the keybed scanner and hands it to the touch curve.
;
; The inter-CPU latches are at 0x120000 (IC22/IC23; see INTER_CPU_LATCH at the top of this
; file and INIT_DMA_SERIAL, which programs both DMA channels to 0x120000).  0x110000 and
; 0x110002 are the keybed DATA and STATUS ports -- what MAME's kn5000_state::subcpu_mem calls
; "Tone generator keybed data/status".  The tone generator itself is at 0x100000/0x100002 with
; its status at 0x100004 (AUDIO_HW_WRITE_READ) and is never touched here.
;
; Evidence that this is the keybed: the routine is instruction-for-instruction the same shape
; as Keybed_Read_Event (0x03D0C5) in the v1.42 payload -- same two ports, same status bit 0
; and bit 1 tests, same 0xFF touch test, same bit-7 test, two call sites into the decoder,
; same 0 / 0xFFFF return convention, same redundant "force velocity 0" store on the release
; arm.  Only the register allocation and the P6.7 bracketing differ (see below).
;
; In:  XWA = pointer to a 2-byte event buffer.
; Out: HL = 0 when the buffer was filled, 0xFFFF when there is nothing to report.
;      buffer[0] = MIDI note number, buffer[1] = velocity (0 means key up).
;
; PORT CONTRACT, exactly as this code exercises it (MAME stubs both ports with .noprw(), so
; this is currently the only description of the interface that exists):
;   (0x110002) STATUS word -- read first, every time.
;      bit 0 = an event is waiting.  Clear -> return 0xFFFF without touching the data port.
;      bit 1 = release / second-contact qualifier: when SET the event is routed down the same
;              arm as a 0xFF touch byte.  Bits 2..15 are never tested by either ROM.
;   (0x110000) DATA word -- read only when status bit 0 was set; the read is what advances
;              the scanner (nothing else clears bit 0).
;      low  byte: bits 0..6 = key index; bit 7 = key STATE.
;                 ★ Polarity: bit 7 SET = key DOWN, bit 7 CLEAR = key UP.  Corroborated
;                   independently by ToneGen_Poll_Read (0x03D230) in the payload, which sets
;                   the key's bitmap bit when bit 7 is 1 and clears it when bit 7 is 0.
;      high byte: raw touch reading; 0xFF means "no touch value for this event".
;
; Routing (identical in both ROMs):
;   touch != 0xFF and status bit 1 clear -> decode and keep the velocity.
;   otherwise -> key bit 7 CLEAR (key up)   -> decode, then force velocity 0;
;                key bit 7 SET   (key down) -> DISCARD the event, return 0xFFFF.
;   ★ Returning 0xFFFF for a discarded event also ENDS the caller's drain loop for this pass,
;     deferring whatever else is queued to the next call.
;
; ★ One real difference from the payload, worth recording: Keybed_Read_Event brackets its two
;   reads with `set 7,(P6)` / `res 7,(P6)` (SFR 0x18), documented there as driving A23 to the
;   tone generator's NAD / EXADL0 pins.  THIS routine never touches P6: the boot ROM writes
;   neither P6, P6CR nor P6FC anywhere (the only 0x18 in this file is the unrelated
;   `ldio 0x47,0x18` in BOOT_INIT).  INFERENCE: address bit 1 alone distinguishes STATUS from
;   DATA, and the payload's P6.7 toggle is an extra chip-select the boot path does not need.
;   This is a data point for the open question recorded in
;   symbols/proposals/subcpu-region-01.txt ("one of the two is wrong").
edits.why: The header asserts three things that are false (inter-CPU latches, 'communication handler', 'send/receive'), and this routine is the sub-CPU's keybed entry point. It also captures the port contract MAME needs.

edits.anchor:
; NOTE_VELOCITY_LOOKUP_CALCULATE (0xFF8BD2) - Note/velocity calculation routine
;
; Calculates velocity values based on note index and lookup tables.
; Uses ToneGen_Velocity_Input_Curve (0xFF804C), ToneGen_VelCurve_ModeParams_Mode6
; (0xFF8040), ToneGen_VelCurve_Pivot (0xFF802A), ToneGen_VelCurve_Divisor (0xFF802C)
; and ToneGen_Velocity_Output_Curve (0xFF814C).
;
; Input: XWA = pointer to output buffer
;        C = note index (low byte from latch)
;        E = velocity index (high byte from latch)
edits.replacement:
; NOTE_VELOCITY_LOOKUP_CALCULATE (0xFF8BD2) -- the KN5000 TOUCH CURVE
;
; Turns one raw keybed event into a MIDI note number and a MIDI velocity.  Byte-for-byte the
; same algorithm as Keybed_Decode_Event (0x03D11F) in the v1.42 payload, over byte-identical
; tables; the only difference is that this copy hard-codes touch mode 6 while the payload
; indexes the mode table with the byte at 0x004A48.
;
; In:  XWA = 2-byte output buffer, C = raw key byte, E = raw touch byte.
; Out: (XWA+0) = MIDI note, (XWA+1) = MIDI velocity.
;
; NOTE NUMBER
;   note = (C & 0x7F) + 0x24.  Key index 0 is MIDI note 36 (C2).
;   INFERENCE: the KN5000's keyboard is 61 keys, so indices 0..60 span MIDI 36..96 (C2-C7).
;   What the ROMs prove rather than infer is a bound of 64: the key-down bitmap here and the
;   voice bitmap in the payload are both 8 bytes, and both index it with (key >> 3) & 7.
;   If bit 7 of C is CLEAR (key UP) the routine stores velocity 0 and returns immediately.
;
; VELOCITY
;   strength     = ToneGen_Velocity_Input_Curve[raw touch]          ; 0xFF804C, 256 x u8
;   intermediate = gain/128 * (strength - 77) + pivot_out           ; the 3-byte mode record
;                  - (note % 12 in {1,3,6,8,10} ? black_trim : 0)   ; C#,D#,F#,G#,A#
;   velocity     = ToneGen_Velocity_Output_Curve[clamp(intermediate, 0, 255)]  ; 0xFF814C
;   gain / pivot_out / black_trim are bytes +0/+1/+2 of the selected row of
;   ToneGen_VelCurve_ModeParams; this ROM always uses row 6 (0xFF8040): 96, 152, 16.
;   The 77 and the 128 are ToneGen_VelCurve_Pivot / ToneGen_VelCurve_Divisor.
;   The arithmetic is a 16-bit signed MULS followed by EXTS + DIVS, so gain*(strength-77) is
;   assumed to fit in int16 (worst case 144*178 = 25632, it does).
;
; MEASURED PROPERTIES OF THE TWO CURVES (all reproducible from the ROM image; see the note
; block above ToneGen_Velocity_Input_Curve for the raw data):
;   * Input curve, for raw 31..253, is EXACTLY  clamp(0xE0 - 0x20*(raw>>5) + knee[raw & 31],
;     1, 255) -- one 32-entry knee repeated verbatim, each block 0x20 lower.  223 of the 256
;     entries fit that closed form with zero exceptions.  To within 3 counts it is simply
;     strength = 224 - raw.  Raw 0..8 clamp to 255, raw 9..30 form a steeper head, raw 254
;     and 255 give 0.  Decreasing in raw: a small raw number is a LOUD strike.
;   * Output curve is 1 at index 0, a flat 2 for indices 1..95, a ramp 3..16 for 96..143, and
;     exactly (index - 128) from 144 to 255.  So the whole soft half of the intermediate range
;     is crushed into velocities 1..16 and the loud half is a clean 2:1 divide.
;   * Consequence for mode 0 (gain 0): the intermediate is always 208 and the DELIVERED
;     velocity is always ToneGen_Velocity_Output_Curve[208] = 80.  That is "touch off".
;   * Consequence for mode 6: velocity 127 for raw 0..16, velocity 2 for raw >= 224, and in
;     the linear region the black-key trim is a straight -16 on the MIDI velocity.
;   * Modes 0..8 all cross at intermediate ~208 (velocity 80) at strength ~150-151, i.e. they
;     pivot about the same medium strike.  Mode 9 does not: its pivot_out is 130 where the
;     pattern predicts 124.75, so mode 9 is uniformly ~5 velocity louder, not just steeper.
;   ⚠ UNCERTAIN: the divide is `divs`; the tables above assume it truncates toward zero.  If
;     TLCS-900 DIVS floors instead, velocities in the soft half shift by 1 (387 of the 2560
;     mode/raw combinations change).  The endpoints quoted above are rounding-independent.
;
; ★ In THIS ROM the computed velocity is then thrown away: the caller
;   (CONTROL_PANEL_BIT_SET_CLEAR) only tests it against zero, and the output curve's minimum
;   is 1, so a key-down can never read as 0.  The full curve is evaluated purely to reuse the
;   same code as the payload.  The store of 6 to (0x0560) on entry mirrors the payload's touch
;   mode byte at 0x004A48 but is never read back here.
edits.why: This is the KN5000's touch response and the header described none of it. The measured curve properties are what an emulator or a re-implementation needs, and they are checkable from the ROM image alone.

edits.anchor:
; CONTROL_PANEL_BIT_SET_CLEAR (0xFF8B37) - LED/Output bit manipulation routine
;
; This routine sets or clears bits in an output buffer based on input parameters.
; Parameters are passed on stack:
;   (SP+0): Button/LED index (0x24-based offset)
;   (SP+1): Action (0 = clear bit, non-zero = set bit)
;
; The routine calculates:
;   - Byte offset = (index - 0x24) >> 3 (which byte in buffer)
;   - Bit position = (index - 0x24) & 7 (which bit in byte)
;   - Buffer base = 0x0558
;
; Uses INTER_CPU_LATCH_READ_DISPATCH to send/receive data to hardware.
edits.replacement:
; CONTROL_PANEL_BIT_SET_CLEAR (0xFF8B37) -- drain the keybed FIFO into the KEY-DOWN BITMAP
;
; ⚠ MISNOMER: no control panel and no LED buffer.  This is the boot ROM's keybed drain loop.
; The control panel is the main CPU's business and is reached over the CP serial link; this
; routine's only hardware contact is INTER_CPU_LATCH_READ_DISPATCH, i.e. the keybed ports.
;
; No parameters: it allocates its own 2-byte event buffer on the stack, then
;   1. calls INTER_CPU_LATCH_READ_DISPATCH to fetch one decoded event;
;   2. while it returns 0 (not 0xFFFF):
;        key   = buffer[0] - 0x24                      ; back to a 0-based key index
;        byte  = (key >> 3) & 7,  bit = key & 7        ; 8 bytes = 64 keys
;        buffer[1] != 0  ->  bitmap[byte] |=  (1 << bit)     ; key down
;        buffer[1] == 0  ->  bitmap[byte] &= ~(1 << bit)     ; key up
;      and fetches the next event, until the FIFO reports empty.
;
; The bitmap is 8 bytes at 0x0558 (`lda_d16 xix,(1368)` here; INIT_MEMORY_TEST zeroes exactly
; those 8 bytes and SERIAL_INIT ORs exactly those 8 bytes together).  It is the boot ROM's
; direct-address equivalent of the payload's voice bitmap, which the payload reaches through
; the pointer ToneGen_Voice_Bitmap_Ptr (0x01F41C -> 0x00F002) and updates with the same
; (index >> 3) & 7 / index & 7 split in ToneGen_Poll_Read (0x03D230).
;
; Boot-ROM RAM map for this subsystem:
;   0x0556        self-test status byte (bit 0/1 RAM, bit 2 ROM checksum, bit 3 TG probe)
;   0x0558-0x055F key-down bitmap, 64 bits
;   0x0560        touch mode, written 6 by NOTE_VELOCITY_LOOKUP_CALCULATE, never read
edits.why: The header names a control panel and an LED buffer that do not exist here; the routine is the keybed drain loop and its buffer is a key-down bitmap. Single caller, verified.

edits.anchor:
; SERIAL_INIT (0xFF8B07) - Initialize serial communication
; Checks status bytes and sets interrupt flag accordingly
edits.replacement:
; SERIAL_INIT (0xFF8B07) -- one pass of the FACTORY KEYBED TEST
;
; ⚠ MISNOMER: no serial hardware is touched.  SFR 0x30 is PORT C, not a serial or timer
; register (see P6/P7/PC in v142/subcpu/shared/sfr_tmp94c241.s: PC = 0x30, PCCR = 0x32,
; PCFC = 0x33, and BOOT_INIT programs PC = 0x03, PCCR = 0x02, PCFC = 0x00, i.e. PC.0 input
; and PC.1 output).
;
; Body:
;   1. call CONTROL_PANEL_BIT_SET_CLEAR  -- drain the keybed FIFO into the bitmap at 0x0558
;   2. OR the 8 bitmap bytes 0x0558..0x055F together
;   3. any bit set (some key is held) -> `res 1,(PC)`
;      no bit set                    -> `set 1,(PC)`
;
; PC.1 is the CN12 "Sub CPU Checking Device" LED, active LOW: MAME's kn5000.cpp wires
; m_subcpu->portc_write() to m_checking_device_led_cn12 = (BIT(data,1) == 0).  So the LED
; lights for exactly as long as any key on the keybed is held down.  That is a keybed
; continuity test, and it is the only thing the boot ROM ever does with a key event.
;
; INIT_MEMORY_TEST calls this in an endless loop, and INIT_MEMORY_TEST is only entered when
; PC.0 is LOW -- PC.0 is the CN12 strap itself (m_subcpu->portc_read().set_ioport("CN12");
; the DIP reads 0x00 for "On").  With the checking device absent (MAME's default, 0x01) the
; whole chain SERIAL_INIT -> CONTROL_PANEL_BIT_SET_CLEAR -> INTER_CPU_LATCH_READ_DISPATCH ->
; NOTE_VELOCITY_LOOKUP_CALCULATE is unreachable; nothing else in this ROM calls any of them.
edits.why: The header claims serial init and an interrupt flag; the routine is the factory keybed test pass, and PC.1 is the CN12 LED. This is the only place the boot ROM's keybed path is entered.

edits.anchor: ; Clear serial buffer area
edits.replacement:

	; either ROM -- the v1.42 payload only ever reads 0x110000/0x110002 -- so the meaning

edits.replacement: ; XBC = 0x0560, the loop bound: INC #3,r encodes 8 as 0, so this is +8 not +1

edits.anchor: ; Uses nested loops with timer register 0x30
edits.replacement:
; ⚠ 0x30 is PORT C, not a timer.  This is the CN12 status-code BLINKER: for each of the four
; low bits of A (l runs 0..3) it drives PC.1 low -- CN12 LED ON -- for a long (0xC000) or
; short (0x4000) count depending on the bit, then PC.1 high for a fixed 0x4000 count.
; A is the self-test status byte at 0x0556: bit 0 = RAM low half failed, bit 1 = RAM high
; half failed (both from MemTest_RegionTable), bit 2 = ROM checksum mismatch (ROM_CHECKSUM),
; bit 3 = tone-generator probe timed out (HARDWARE_CALIBRATION_SEQUENCE).  Four flashes,
; long = fault.  Called once by INIT_MEMORY_TEST, just before the keybed test loop starts.
edits.why: 0x30 is Port C per the shared SFR file; calling it a timer register hides that this routine is the factory fault-code display and that PC.1 is the CN12 LED.

edits.replacement:

;        was called ToneGen_Read_Voice_Data, which is wrong.
;        P6.7 is toggled around the two accesses; see the A23 note below.
;
; ⚠ IN MAME THIS ROUTINE CAN NEVER RETURN AN EVENT.  subcpu_mem maps 0x110000-0x110003 with
; .noprw(), and handler_entry_read_nop::read() returns m_space->unmap(), initialised to 0
; (src/emu/emumem_aspace.cpp:602).  The status word therefore reads 0x0000, bit 0 is never

;     bit 0  an event is queued.  Clear -> the drain loop stops for this pass.
;     bit 1  release / second-contact qualifier: when SET the event takes the same arm as a
;            0xFF touch byte.  Bits 2..15 are never tested.
;   (0x110000) DATA, read only when status bit 0 was set; the read is what advances the
;              scanner -- nothing in either ROM writes anything back to clear bit 0.
;     low  byte  bits 0..6 = key index (bounded at 64 by the 8-byte bitmaps both ROMs keep);
;                bit 7 = key state, SET = DOWN, CLEAR = UP.

edits.replacement:
; qualifier.  Data low byte = key index in bits 0..6; bit 7 is the key STATE and its sense is
; ★ SET = key DOWN, CLEAR = key UP -- NOT a "release flag".  Independent corroboration:
; ToneGen_Poll_Read (0x03D230) SETS the key's bitmap bit when bit 7 is 1 and clears it when
; bit 7 is 0, and Keybed_Decode_Event stores velocity 0 exactly on the bit-7-clear path.
; High byte = the RAW TOUCH reading, not a velocity: it is a table index, and 0xFF means "no
; touch value", which routes the event to the note-off arm.
edits.why: 'bit 7 = release flag' inverts the polarity of the single most important bit in the interface; an implementation written from this comment would emit note-offs for presses.

edits.anchor: ; In:  C = raw key byte (bit 7 = release), E = raw velocity, XWA = 2-byte output buffer.
edits.replacement:
; In:  C = raw key byte (bit 7 SET = key DOWN, CLEAR = key UP), E = raw TOUCH reading (an

; Measured properties of the two tables (reproducible from the ROM image):

;     Raw 0..8 clamp to 255, raw 254/255 give 0.  Small raw = loud, so it reads as a TIME.
;   * 0x01F53E is 1 at 0, a flat 2 across 1..95, a ramp 3..16 across 96..143, and exactly
;     (index - 128) from 144 up.  The soft half of the range collapses into velocities 1..16.
;   * curve 0 (gain 0) always yields intermediate 208, i.e. MIDI velocity 80 -- touch OFF.
;   * curve 6 yields 127 for raw 0..16 and 2 for raw >= 224; in the linear region the
;     black-key trim is a flat -16 on the delivered velocity.
;   * curves 0..8 all cross at velocity 80 for a medium strike (strength ~150-151); curve 9
;     does not -- its pivot_out is 130 where the pattern predicts 124.75, so it is uniformly
;     ~5 velocity louder rather than merely steeper.

;     the 2560 curve/raw combinations by one velocity, all in the soft half; the endpoints

edits.why: Same inverted bit-7 claim, plus the header gives the formula but none of the behaviour; these are the numbers anyone reimplementing KN5000 touch response actually needs, and they are checkable from the ROM.

uncertain: Whether TLCS-900 DIVS truncates toward zero or floors. It changes 387 of the 2560 (curve, raw) velocity results by one, all in the soft half of the range. I documented the formula and only the rounding-independent endpoints; resolving it needs the Toshiba manual or a hardware/emulator check.

What the value 0x0003 written to (0x110002) by INIT_MEMORY_TEST means. It is the ONLY write to the keybed port in either ROM, so nothing constrains it from software. Marked INFERENCE in the proposed comment.

Whether the payload's P6.7 toggle is functionally required. The boot ROM reads the same two ports with the same decode and never touches P6, which argues address bit 1 alone selects status vs data -- but I cannot rule out that the boot path works only because P6.7 happens to sit at its reset level, or that the factory test is simply broken on real hardware. Felipe could settle it by fitting the CN12 strap on a real KN5000 and seeing whether the checking-device LED follows held keys.

The 61-key / MIDI 36..96 span. The ROMs prove a bound of 64 (both bitmaps are 8 bytes and both mask the index to 6 bits) and prove the +0x24 offset, but the actual key count is external knowledge; I marked it INFERENCE in the comment.

Whether touch curves 0..9 are exactly the panel's TOUCH SENSITIVITY setting. Audio_CmdHandler_A0_BF range-checks the value at <= 9, which matches the 10 rows, and the main CPU has a TchSens_EventDispatch widget (v9/maincpu/ui/ui_mode_handlers.s:7027), but I did not trace that widget through to the 0xA0..0xBF command that writes 0x004A48. Nothing in my proposed text asserts the link.

A NAME COLLISION I did not touch: symbols/subcpu_symbols_reference.txt names 0x01F418/0x01F41A/0x01F420/0x01F43E/0x01F53E as Keybed_Touch_TimeRef / Keybed_Touch_Divisor / Keybed_Touch_Curve_Table / Keybed_Time_To_Strength / Keybed_Strength_To_Velocity (curated block, 2026-07-26), while v142/subcpu/subcpu_data_tables.s labels the same addresses ToneGen_VelCurve_Pivot / _Divisor / (unlabelled) / ToneGen_Velocity_Input_Curve / ToneGen_Velocity_Output_Curve, and the map-generated part of that same file lists neither. The curated names are the more accurate ones (the input curve really is time -> strength), but renaming is out of scope here and the labels are referenced from the boot ROM's comments too. Someone has to decide.

Out of scope but adjacent, and worth a look: HARDWARE_CALIBRATION_SEQUENCE reads the tone generator's status at 0x100004, which falls OUTSIDE MAME's map(0x100000, 0x100003). It therefore reads the unmapped value 0, and 0 is exactly the value the probe treats as success -- so the power-on TG liveness probe passes in emulation for the wrong reason. I did not investigate further and proposed no edit for it.

packages.area: KN5000 inter-CPU latch protocol (IC22/IC23) and the main-CPU /INT0 receive ISR, plus a review pass over the boot CP-serial modules from 3de6871 / 72242c0
packages.summary:
VERIFIED FROM THE ROM BYTES. (1) The transport is a pair of 8-bit latches — IC22 main→sub, IC23 sub→main — mapped at 0x140000 (main) / 0x120000 (sub), and each load asserts the receiver's /INT0. (2) The main CPU's receive ISR at 0xEF3525 is genuinely NOT re-entrant, and the mechanism is sharper than "no guard": there ARE two guards (MSTAT1 at 0xEF3525, SSTAT0 at 0xEF3536) but they are read 0x18 bytes before the latch read at 0xEF353D and the flag is only released 0x9F bytes later at 0xEF35C4, and the ISR never masks interrupts. INT0 runs at level 1, so acceptance sets IFF=2 and self-masks — the ONLY thing preventing re-entry. INTT3 (the RTOS tick) runs at level 2, preempts it, and at 0xEF1B8D INTT3_EnterScheduler executes `ei 0 / nop / ei 6`, which drops the mask to 0 and admits a nested INT0. The nested dispatch eats the header and acks; the outer dispatch resumes at 0xEF353D and reads a PAYLOAD byte as a header, reprogramming DMAC0 from its low 5 bits so the count can never complete and MSTAT1 is never raised again. (3) A key structural fact nobody had written down: the main CPU never arms DMA0V — it pulls each payload byte with a SOFTWARE micro-DMA request, `stdi8 (265), 1` = DMAR bit 0 (265 = 0x0109), an uncommented line that reads like a RAM flag. The sub CPU does the opposite (DMA0V←10), so its payload bytes bypass its ISR entirely — which is exactly why the trap exists on the main side only.

The package is 15 edits, all COMMENTS ONLY — no instruction, directive, label or branch target is touched, and no rename is proposed. The ISR block is source-identical in v7/v9/v10, so the same annotation goes to all three (v7 carries its own addresses: the whole block sits 0x2A lower).

Also corrected two comments that are demonstrably wrong: `Audio_DMA_Transfer` claims to use "DMA channel configuration set up by Audio_InitDMAChannels" — it is a pure software byte-bang loop (0xEF341B: post-increment read, `ld (0x140000),A`, 3-iteration delay) and `Audio_InitDMAChannels` is not a symbol in this ROM; and MICRODMA_CH2_HANDLER's "Stops Timer 8" is 8-bit Timer 2 (T8RUN bit 2; DMA2V=22=INTT2). Review of 3de6871/72242c0: the boot CP-serial comments check out — INTCLR 0x12/0x22/0x23 really are INTA/INTRX1/INTTX1, INTEAB=0xE3, and the +0x600000 boot alias is right; the one thing worth warning about there is that all three epilogues clear all three requests, so I added a note.

; =============================================================================
; INT0_HANDLER - inter-CPU latch receive ISR (sub CPU -> main CPU)
; =============================================================================
; ** NOT RE-ENTRANT.  Read the hazard note at the end of this block. **

;        Other = Standard command (1-32 bytes based on bits 4-0, state 1)

; ASYMMETRY WITH THE MAIN CPU'S INT0_HANDLER (0xEF3525, v10 program ROM).

; CPU's INT0_HANDLER (a nested dispatch eats the header, the outer dispatch
; then reads a payload byte as a header and wedges the link) has no direct
; analogue here once DMA0V is armed.  The same non-atomic shape IS present in

; SSTAT1 is only cleared at INT0_Ack, at the end.

; main-CPU/sub-CPU inter-CPU LATCH link, which also runs on /INT0 but on the

edits.why: Reviewing 3de6871 I could confirm every factual claim already in this header (INTCLR values, INTEAB = SFR 0xE3, the +0x600000 boot alias, the raw-offset state byte). The one behaviour not written down is that each epilogue clears all three requests; and the file never says which /INT0 link it is NOT, which is precisely the confusion this task started from.

uncertain: Whether the real KN5000 hardware can hit this trap at all. IIMC=0x00 makes INT0 falling-edge triggered, so on silicon the request is latched once and cleared on acceptance -- a nested dispatch would need a genuine second edge from the sub CPU. The observed duplicate was produced by MAME's acceptance-time /INT0 re-assertion. My comments therefore describe the ISR as structurally unsafe and the duplicate as an emulation-observed event; they do NOT claim the real machine wedges. If someone can scope /INT0 on hardware during a chunk, that would settle it.

Whether the recovery routine at 0xEF3689 (v7: 0xEF365F) is ever executed. Its body decodes cleanly (samples DMAC0, ~10-poll stuck counter, then DMA0V<-0, state 0x05E2<-0, `set 1,(PZ)`), but no direct caller appeared when I scanned the ROM for its address; it may be reached through a pointer table. That is why the claim is marked INFERENCE / UNVERIFIED in the comment. Note also that this routine clears DMA0V, which the main CPU never arms -- so its effective action is the state reset plus forcing MSTAT1 high.

Whether the main CPU's micro-DMA channel 2 (DMAD2 = 0x140000, DMAM2 = 0x08 source-increment, TREG2 = 7, all set up in SubCPU_Init_DMA_Channels) is used by any send path at all. Every send I traced goes through the software loop in Audio_DMA_Transfer, and DMA2V is never written, which would make INTTC2_HANDLER unreachable -- but I did not audit every caller, so I made no claim about it in the comments.

The IC22/IC23 designations come from the memory-map comments in MAME's kn5000.cpp; I did not open the service-manual schematics to confirm them independently. The comment attributes the numbers to that source rather than asserting them.

The address of the main CPU's dispatch table is verified (SeqRingBuf_WriteDispatch_Table at 0xE00012, matching `lda XDE,0xe00012` at ef3625), but I did not evaluate whether that existing NAME is right for the sub->main command path. No rename is proposed.

packages.area: table_data ROM — multisample SET descriptors (ToneDB_EnvDescTable, 0x857914), their zone records (the ToneEnv_* chunks) and the directory slots that index them
packages.summary:
WHERE THEY ARE. The multisample SET descriptors are `ToneDB_EnvDescTable` at ROM 0x857914 (SubCPU 0x077914) — 487 records of 15 bytes, ending exactly at 0x85959D. The stride is not implicit: it is the directory word +0xEC / +0xF2, both 15. Directory slots +0x30/+0x34/+0x38 all hold the same offset, so the three tone families share one block.

SET DESCRIPTOR LAYOUT (15 bytes): +0x00 flags; +0x01 LE32 offset of the SET key map (ToneEnv_*_A); +0x05 LE32 offset of the zone-record array (ToneEnv_*_B); +0x09/+0x0A low/high key of the SET's range; +0x0B root key (pivot = root*256+0x80); +0x0C LE16 base pitch in 8.8 log semitones (the units of TG register +0x400); +0x0E unidentified (0 in 473 of 487). Flags: bit 7 = zone stride (set → 6 bytes, clear → 4); bit 1 = the pitch trap; bit 0 = "reserve level 0xFF"; bit 3 = unidentified (10 records); bits 2,4,5,6 never set, which is why the 15/12/13/10 strides `WaveSel_StageB_Build_Reg040` can also emit never occur.

HOW ZONES HANG OFF. The A chunk is `LE32 key→band table pointer` + a `band → zone index` byte array; the B chunk is the array of zone records. `WaveSel_KeyTable_Lookup` (0x022A32) indexes the 128-byte table with the *key* — `and bc,0x7F00 / sra bc,8` on the voice's pitch — giving a band; `A[+0x04+band]` gives the zone-record index. The five tables in use are the block currently labelled `ToneDB_VelocityCurve_0..5`: that name is a misnomer, the input is the key, not velocity, and the 487 A-chunk heads are the only things in the whole 2 MB ROM that point there.

ZONE RECORD (6 bytes when flags bit 7 set, else 4): +0x00 LE16 recording selector `(class<<12)|entry`, copied verbatim into staging word 0x0451CE = TG register +0x040; +0x02 output-level field select — **bit 7 set → bits 6..4 go verbatim into bits 14..12 of TG register +0x080 (`and wa,0x70 / sll wa,8` in `Voice_Build_OutputLevel` 0x0232C7), bit 7 clear → those bits come from the subcpu table at 0x00FBE4 instead**; +0x03 signed 1/256-semitone fine trim; +0x04 LE16 coarse trim in 8.8 semitones, stride-6 only (the stride-4 emitter writes 0 to 0x293E). Byte +0x02 takes only nine values across all 2134 zone records — 0x00, and 0x80|(f<<4) for f = 0..7 — low nibble always zero, never bit 7 clear with bits 6..4 set: the field structure showing itself in the data.

THE BIT-1 RULE. Exactly 13 SETs set flags bit 1 (49,50,52,61,63,64,66,67,68,73,74,75,78) and they are exactly the 13 whose root byte is not the universal 0x42; all 13 carry base pitch 0x417F. On that arm `Voice_Pitch_ApplyPortamento` (0x023738) reads neither field — it subtracts and re-adds the literal 0x4280 — so an extractor that computes (base pitch − pivot) unconditionally fabricates +48.996/+56.996/+64.996 semitones, on the 112 of 1444 selectors (7.8%) reachable only from those SETs. One correction I am adding to the existing wording: the fields are NOT unread everywhere — `Voice_Build_Partial_Descriptor` (0x02B717) reads the root byte for keys ≥ 0x78 and `Voice_Pitch_CopyBase` (0x023809) reads the base pitch without testing bit 1. The rule is about the subtraction, not about the bytes.

A structural bonus that fell out and is now documented: the table splits at record 341. Records 0..340 are melodic (ToneIndexMapC/D top out at 338/340 and never reach 341; all 328 with bit 1 clear have base pitch − pivot = 0 exactly), and 341..486 are percussion, reached only from DrumToneIndexMap, all single-zone, stride 4, range 12..120, each with the fixed pitch of its one-shot in +0x0C.

10 edits, all comment-only. Five land in the two .s files and five mirror them in the generators that produce those files, so a regeneration cannot silently revert the documentation. VERIFIED: applied to scratch copies, `grep -v '^;'` of before/after is byte-identical in both .s files, and running the patched generators reproduces the hand-edited files exactly. I could not run the byte-match gate (make is forbidden here); the no-byte-change claim rests on the line-level diff plus the fact that every added line begins with ';'.

ALSO TO COMMIT (I am read-only, so I could not add it): the consolidated probe that re-derives every number above lives at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-fsanches-compartilhado-KN7000/d0e1b1c2-9dd7-40da-b88c-9bcc60bcc85a/scratchpad/pkg/probe_set_descriptors.py and expects to sit at /home/fsanches/compartilhado/kn5000-roms-disasm/scripts/analysis/probe_set_descriptors.py (it locates the ROM relative to its own path, needs no arguments, and its docstring names the question each of its seven sections answers). Please copy it in with the same commit — otherwise every figure in these headers is a claim nobody can re-check.

NO RENAMES PROPOSED. `ToneDB_VelocityCurve_0..5` is demonstrably misnamed, but I left the label alone and said so in its header instead. If you do want the rename later, the complete reference set is two files: table_data/tone_database_aux.s (the six label definitions) and scripts/generators/gen_tonedb_aux.py (the f-string that emits them, plus the structure-map line). It appears in no other .s, no symbols/*.txt, no linker script and no code — nothing branches to it and nothing else names it.

; 487 envelope/modulation descriptor records x 15 bytes (dir +0x30/+0x34/+0x38).
; Record layout: flags byte, two LE32 ToneDB_Base-relative offsets (A and B),
; 6 parameter bytes.  The 2x487 offsets are all distinct and exactly tile the
; ToneEnv data region 0x85B09D-0x863078 (974 chunks).  Flag byte census:
; 0x00 x318, 0x80 x134, 0x02 x13, 0x08 x10, 0x81 x9, 0x01 x3.
; NOTE: 487 records here + 142 records in ToneDB_PercMixerDefaultTable's
; sibling group = 629, the entry count of the tone-record offset table at
; 0x831B00 (DSP1_ResolveStreamPtr's table), suggesting one descriptor per tone.
edits.replacement:
; MULTISAMPLE SET DESCRIPTORS -- 487 records x 15 bytes (dir +0x30/+0x34/+0x38;
; the stride is the directory word +0xEC / +0xF2, both 15).
;
; One record describes one multisample SET: which recordings it is built from,
; where each one sits on the keyboard, and where the SET sits in pitch.  The
; subcpu keeps the pointer to it in the voice slot at +0x1F and in the per-part
; patch cache written by WaveSel_Cache_SetDescPtr.
;
; RECORD LAYOUT
;   +0x00  u8    flags -- see below
;   +0x01  LE32  ToneDB_Base-relative offset of the SET key map (ToneEnv_*_A)
;   +0x05  LE32  ToneDB_Base-relative offset of the zone records (ToneEnv_*_B)
;   +0x09  u8    lowest key of the SET's range  (0..28; it is 12 in 462 of 487)
;   +0x0A  u8    highest key of the SET's range (65..120; it is 120 in 212)
;   +0x0B  u8    root key; the pitch pivot is root*256 + 0x80
;   +0x0C  LE16  base pitch, 8.8 log semitones -- the units of TG reg +0x400
;   +0x0E  u8    0x00 in 473 records, 1..5 in the other 14.  No reader located
;                in the v1.42 subcpu -- UNIDENTIFIED.
; +0x09 and +0x0A are the range that Pitch_Fold_Octaves_Into_Range (0x0229EC)
; and Pitch_Clamp_Into_Range fold or clamp the played key into.
;
; FLAGS BYTE (+0x00).  Census: 0x00 x318, 0x80 x134, 0x02 x13, 0x08 x10,
; 0x81 x9, 0x01 x3 -- so only bits 0, 1, 3 and 7 are ever set.
;   bit 7  zone-record stride: set -> 6 bytes (143 records), clear -> 4 bytes
;          (344 records).  WaveSel_StageB_Build_Reg040 (0x023849) tests bits
;          6, 7 and 5 and can also select strides 15, 12, 13 and 10, but bit 6
;          is clear in every record here, so those four forms never occur.
;   bit 1  PITCH TRAP -- see below.
;   bit 0  reserve level 0xFF: Voice_Calc_LevelPair_Full_CheckMax (0x025DBE)
;          and _Mono_CheckMax (0x026083) decrement an output level of exactly
;          0xFF when it is set.  12 records.
;   bit 3  set in 10 records; no reader located -- UNIDENTIFIED.
;
; HOW A SET IS REACHED (WaveSel_StageA2_FindSetDesc, subcpu 0x032750): a SET is
; named by a bank byte and a wave byte.
;   family = bank & 0xC0, sub = bank & 0x0F, wave = wave & 0x7F
;   set = u16[ dir[+0x24 | +0x28 | +0x2C] + 2*((sub << 7) | wave) ]
;         family 0x00/0xC0 -> +0x24 ToneDB_ToneIndexMapC
;         family 0x80      -> +0x28 ToneDB_ToneIndexMapD
;         family 0x40      -> +0x2C ToneDB_DrumToneIndexMap
;   descriptor = ToneDB_Base + dir[+0x30 | +0x34 | +0x38] + set*15
; Bit 2 of the global mode word 0x041343 substitutes slots +0x9C/+0xA0/+0xA4
; for the three index tables; those slots hold the same three offsets in this
; ROM, so the alternate path is a no-op here.  All three descriptor slots hold
; the same offset, so the three families share this one block.
;
; TWO POPULATIONS, split at record 341, and the index maps confirm the split:
;   000..340  MELODIC SETs.  ToneIndexMapC/D top out at 338 and 340 and never
;             reach 341.  223 are multi-zone, 143 use the 6-byte zone record.
;             All 328 with bit 1 clear carry root 0x42 and base pitch 0x4280,
;             i.e. base pitch - pivot = 0 exactly, so the note tracks the key.
;   341..486  PERCUSSION SETs, reached only from DrumToneIndexMap (whose values
;             are 335 and 341..486).  All 146 are single-zone, 4-byte stride,
;             range 12..120, root 0x42, and every one of them has a base pitch
;             other than 0x4280 -- the fixed pitch of a one-shot, which
;             Voice_Pitch_CopyBase (0x023809) loads straight into the voice.
;
; FLAGS BIT 1 -- THE PITCH TRAP.  Exactly 13 records have it set: 49, 50, 52,
; 61, 63, 64, 66, 67, 68, 73, 74, 75 and 78.  They are exactly the 13 whose
; root byte is not the universal 0x42 (it is 0x00, 0x08 or 0x10), and all 13
; carry the same base pitch 0x417F.  On the bit-1 arm the pitch chain reads
; NEITHER field: Voice_Pitch_ApplyPortamento (0x023738) subtracts and re-adds
; the literal 0x4280 instead (Voice_Pitch_Portamento_Active_SubBias, 0x023786),
; so these SETs contribute no pitch offset at all.  Anything that computes
; (base pitch - pivot) unconditionally fabricates +48.996, +56.996 or +64.996
; semitones here, and these 13 SETs are the sole source of 112 of the 1444
; distinct recording selectors this table produces (7.8%).  That bug shipped in
; a generated pitch table used by an emulator until 2026-08-19.
; Neither field is dead everywhere on the bit-1 arm, so do not read this as
; 'the bytes are ignored': Voice_Build_Partial_Descriptor (0x02B717) reads the
; root byte for keys >= 0x78, remapping the layer to key - 0x78 + root (a layer
; whose SET has bit 1 clear is dropped at that key instead), and
; Voice_Pitch_CopyBase reads the base pitch without testing bit 1 at all.  The
; rule is about the SUBTRACTION, not about the bytes.
;
; RETRACTED: this header used to say `487 records here + 142 records in
; ToneDB_PercMixerDefaultTable's sibling group = 629 ... suggesting one
; descriptor per tone`.  SETs are indexed by the 1024-entry maps above, not by
; the 629-entry tone-record table at 0x831B00; the arithmetic was a
; coincidence.
;
; The 2x487 offsets are all distinct and exactly tile the ToneEnv data region
; 0x85B09D-0x863078 (974 chunks); the chunk header below has their layout.
edits.why: The table this header sits on IS the multisample SET descriptor table, but the header named it 'envelope/modulation descriptors', gave no field offsets past '6 parameter bytes', and did not mention the pitch trap at all. Every figure is re-derived by the probe script; the retracted 487+142=629 sentence is dropped because SETs are indexed by the 1024-entry maps, not by the 629-entry tone-record table (ToneIndexMapC/D max at 338/340, DrumToneIndexMap at 486).

packages.summary:
I swept the tree for stale documentation rather than adding any, using four mechanical checks plus manual verification of every hit: (1) banner ranges `; --- 0xS-0xE Name` cross-checked against `symbols/*_reference.txt` and against the next real label; (2) banner size arithmetic (`N x M bytes`, `N u16`, …) against the span; (3) every `Symbol (0xADDR)` citation in a comment against the symbol map; (4) every file path and `~line NNNN` cross-reference resolved. Most of the repo held up — `table_data/boot_fdc_driver.s`'s 29 "Twin: fdc_routines.s:N" references are almost all still correct, the hdae5000 graphics-bank banner's five palette/bitmap boundaries reproduce exactly, and the banner size arithmetic had zero real errors. The defects cluster in `v142/subcpu/`, where a later wave stacked new banners on top of old ones without retiring the old text.

THE TEN WORST, worst first (severity = how likely it is to get "fixed" into a bug):

1. **`kn5000_subprogram_v142.s:19762` — "The four tables are exactly 10/9/9/10 entries … which is what PINS COUNT to 0..9 and INDEX to 0..8".** This is the flagged failure mode twice over. (a) `Voice_Selector_ComputeMixWeights` loads FIVE distinct table bases — `lda_24 xbc,0x00f786`, `0x00f79a`, `0x00f7d2`, `0x00f7ac`, `0x00f7be` (lines 19791/19802/19809/19815/19821) — and the very next comment line already lists five boundary equations, which only close if there are five tables (10/9/9/10/10, tiling 0x00F786-0x00F7E5 exactly and ending where `Voice_Portamento_Rate_Table` starts at 0x00F7E6). (b) The word "pins" asserts a bounds guarantee that does not exist: `Voice_Selector_FindBestSlot`'s own header 100 lines above says "★ Both candidates start at 0xFF and there is NO fallback", and the code confirms it (`ldb e,0xFF / ldb l,0xFF`, no post-loop default). INDEX = 0xFF makes the 0x00F79A read address 0x00F79A+0x1FE = 0x00F998, inside `AUDIO_CMD_TONEEDIT_JUMPTABLE` (0x00F973-0x00F99A) — a jump-table word written into part+0x112. Someone trusting "pins" will not add the bounds check; someone trusting "four" may delete or merge `Voice_Part_Trim_Base`.

2. **`kn5000_subprogram_v142.s:37180-37181` — the legacy `RingBuf_ReadByte` banner has the read and write pointers SWAPPED.** It says "+0 = read pointer / +2 = write pointer". The code increments the index at **+2** on a read (`lda xbc,(xwa+2) / ld de,(xbc) / incm 1,(xbc)`), so +2 is the read index. Three independent corroborations inside the same file: the prose block directly beneath it says "+0x00 write index, +0x02 read index"; `RingBuf_SkipToEnd_Epilogue` does `ld wa,(xiz+2) / ld (xiz),wa`, i.e. write := read; and `RingBuffer_Write4K`'s header 15 lines later says "[0]=write_ptr(16)". Acting on the stale banner corrupts the 4 KB MIDI ring.

3. **`subcpu_data_tables.s:555` — "Four adjacent u16 tables … " immediately followed by an enumeration of five.** Same defect as #1 at its second site; the comment contradicts itself in six lines. The neighbouring banner at line 564 already says "the five part trim tables", so the repo has answered this. The banner also headlines `VOICE_SELECTOR_MIXWEIGHT_TABLES`, which is not a symbol in any build.

4. **`subcpu_data_tables.s:3964` — the 0x014739 dispatch is attributed to `DSP_BytecodeInterpreter_Init`; it is in `DSP_BytecodeInterpreter_Loop`.** The instruction sequence the banner quotes (`add wa,wa / lda_24 xix,0x014739 / ldw_sri WA / lda_24 xix,0x03c32e / jp_ind`) appears verbatim at the tail of `_Loop` (0x03C2CB, lines 51955-51961). `_Init` (0x03C259) contains no dispatch at all — it copies the descriptor's four words and one long into the frame and falls through to `CheckEnd`. The duplicate banner three lines below already states the correct routine.

5. **Three banners headline symbols that do not exist**, so a grep for them returns nothing: `DSP_Bytecode_HandlerOffsetTable` (line 3969, real label `OFFSETS_14739`), `DSP_Translator_OpcodeOffsetTable` (line 3987, real label `OFFSETS_14745`), `DSP_EFFBytecode_ProgramTable` (line 4029, real label `ToneGen_WorkArea`). None appears in `symbols/subcpu_symbols_reference.txt` or as a label anywhere.

6. **`kn5000_subprogram_v142.s:39956` — "Called from Audio_Process_Init (0x032197)".** `Audio_Process_Init` is 0x034CDB; 0x032197 falls inside `VoiceParam_Update_ActiveMain` (0x03218A), an unrelated routine. The call really is in `Audio_Process_Init` (source line 37163), so only the address is wrong — which is worse than a wrong name, because the address looks authoritative.

7. **`kn5000_subprogram_v142.s:2656` — "Sole caller: MIDI_Dispatch (0x0374F5)".** `MIDI_Dispatch` is 0x034D93; 0x0374F5 is inside `EFF_DspChanInit_AlgoType4F_SubB`. Line 18466 of the *same file* already cites "MIDI_Dispatch (0x034D93 family)", so the repo contradicts itself.

8. **Eight stale source-line cross-references, all of which now point at unrelated code.** Seven `(subcpu source ~line NNNN)` in `subcpu_data_tables.s` (lines 339, 387, 465, 550, 586, 615, 2205) and one `subcpu source 44822/44863/44883/44912` (line 4027). Line numbers rot on every wave — the fix replaces them with symbol+address, which is what the repo's better comments already do.

9. **`CLAUDE.md:1067-1071` "ROM Components" — four source paths that do not exist, and two percentages the repo formally retracted.** `maincpu/kn5000_v10_program.asm`, `subcpu/kn5000_subprogram_v142.asm`, `table_data/kn5000_table_data.asm`, `hdae5000/hd-ae5000_v2_06i.asm` are all absent (the ASL mirror lives under `archive/asl/`; the authoritative sources are `v10/maincpu/…​.s`, `v142/subcpu/…​.s`). The "~33%" and "~5%" are exactly the figures `DISASSEMBLY_PLAN.md` retracted on 2026-08-08. This is the agent-instruction file, so it misdirects every session that opens it.

10. **`kn5000_subprogram_v142.s:38653` — the legacy `DSP2_Init` banner says "Clears DSP2 control variables at 0x3B60-0x3B64".** The prose beneath it and the code disagree: the block is the *shared* DSP command-ring control block (write index 0x3B60, read index 0x3B62, count 0x3B64), used for both DSPs' traffic — `Audio_Process_DSP`'s header calls it "the DSP ring buffer (2KB at 0x3B60)" and `subcpu_data_tables.s:17` calls it "DSP command ring consumed by AUDIO_PROCESS_DSP". problems: BLOCKER — EDIT [0] IS TRUNCATED AND WOULD DELETE CODE. Its REPLACEMENT ends mid-word ("...ToneGen_WriteVoice_Direct (0x02") and, unlike edit [1], never re-emits the anchor's four lines. The anchor is `Voice_Build_GateCommand:` + `push xiz` / `ld xiz, xwa` / `ld xwa, (xiz + 23)`. Applying it removes a label called from 4 sites (v142/subcpu/kn5000_subprogram_v142.s lines 17073, 20789, 21631; also symbols/subcpu_symbols_reference.txt:1386) plus three real instructions — assembled bytes change and it will not assemble. Cannot be reviewed either: the missing tail holds the whole command-set table the summary rests on.

BLOCKER — EDIT [2] IS TRUNCATED AND WOULD DELETE A LABEL. Its REPLACEMENT ends "...the only hand-off values this register ever receives are " and never re-emits `ToneGen_WriteSingleReg:`, which is part of its anchor. Twelve `call ToneGen_WriteSingleReg` sites reference that label. Same consequence as [0].

FACTUAL, EDIT [2] — "All ten call sites were read" is wrong: there are TWELVE explicit call sites plus the .byte-encoded one at 0x02E0FF = thirteen. Lines 14076, 14667, 22764, 22881, 23073, 23191, 23305, 23483, 23516, 25701, 38408, 38454. The three missed are Voice_Step_DelayTimers (0x026E5B, line 14076), ToneGen_SetupPolyVoice (0x0355AD, line 38408), ToneGen_SetupPercussionVoice (0x035656, line 38454). So "Eight of the ten pass BC = the word at 0x0430BB + slot*0x47" is also wrong — it is NINE of thirteen (line 14076 also does `ld bc, (xbc + 45)`). The qualitative conclusion (WA is always a bare voice/slot number, so the register is always 0x0000+slot) does survive at all thirteen sites; only the counts and the list are wrong.

FACTUAL, EDIT [1] — "★ THIS IS WHERE 0xF000 COMES FROM ... every F000 the chip receives is this literal" is FALSE. ToneGen_SetupPolyVoice (0x0355AD, line 38352) copies the 68-byte template at ROM 0x012115 into 0x3B1C, never touches word 0, and passes that word to ToneGen_WriteSingleReg. ROM file offset 0x3215 reads `00 f0` = 0xF000. The auxiliary 8-voice pool therefore sends 0xF000 to the control register on every one of its note-ons.
