problems: EDIT[0] IS UNUSABLE AS DELIVERED (blocking). The replacement text is TRUNCATED mid-word -- it ends '; So IC303 does the walk. The firmware's entire contribution is one 16-bit i'. It also does NOT reproduce the anchor line, so applying it would DELETE line 6921 ('; THE THREE ENVELOPES share one word format, (target << 8) | rate, and are written with the') and leave line 6922 ('; same shape: segments 0 and 1 take extra writes...') orphaned as a sentence fragment. EDITs [1],[2],[3] all correctly re-include their anchor; [0] does not. Byte-safe, but it mutilates existing prose.

EDIT[0] DOES NOT CONTAIN WHAT ITS OWN HEADING AND `WHY` PROMISE. The heading says 'THE WAVE ROM'S OWN DIRECTORY' and the WHY says the block 'Documents the format, the self-validation property, the record contents'. The delivered text contains NONE of the four-page split, the 198/168/1072/57 counts, the 1495/1495 back-reference validation, the record-body census, or the bit-7-is-only-ever-last property. ~90% of the EVIDENCE section supports text that was never submitted and therefore cannot be reviewed.

FALSE CLAIM (blocking, EDIT[0]): 'this payload's only channel to IC303 is the address latch 0x100000 / data port 0x100002'. The file's own annotations contradict this. There are four more reads on the IC303 interface in v142/subcpu/kn5000_subprogram_v142.s: 0x110002/0x110000 at lines 53245/53250 (Keybed_Read_Event) and 53471/53474 (ToneGen_Poll_Read). ToneGen_Poll_Read's existing comment states 'A23 is tied to the tone generator's D5VNAD / NAD / EXADL0 pins' and it maintains a voice on/off bitmap at 0x01F41C. MAME's own commented map line (mame_driver/src/mame/matsushita/kn5000.cpp:164) labels 0x110000 '@ IC303'.

FALSE/AMBIGUOUS CLAIM (blocking, EDIT[0]): 'exactly ONE read anywhere'. Read naturally this means 'anywhere in the file', which is false (see the four 0x110000/0x110002 reads). The defensible statement is narrower and should be written that way: ZERO reads of the register data port 0x100002, and exactly one read at 0x100000 (line 2651).

INCOMPLETE CENSUS PRESENTED AS COMPLETE (EDIT[0]): 'The boot ROM has the same shape: 29 latch writes, 28 data writes, one status read at 0x100004.' subcpu/boot/kn5000_subcpu_boot.s also reads 0x110002 and 0x110000 (lines 100239, 100243) and writes 0x110002 (line 99923). The 29/28/1 figures themselves are correct; the word 'shape' overclaims.

FALSE CLAIM (blocking, EDIT[3]): 'It is also the ONLY read of IC303 in the whole payload.' Contradicted by ToneGen_Poll_Read at lines 53471/53474 -- a routine named ToneGen, whose comment ties its port to the tone generator's pins, and which reconstructs a voice-status bitmap. This also strengthens a pre-existing overclaim in the same block ('the single point where the TG active-voice bitmap re-enters sub-CPU software').

FALSE GENERALIZATION (blocking, EDIT[1]): 'The FIRST word of the burst -- register 0x0040 + ch, taken from shadow+0x02 = 0x0451CE'. ToneGen_WriteVoiceParams is a SHARED routine called with at least three different shadow bases: 0x0451CC (many callers), 0x2AA4 (line 25697, ToneGen_Config_Init), and 0x3B1C (lines 38404 and 38450, ToneGen_SetupPolyVoice, via `lda_d16 xbc, 15132`). Putting the unconditional equation in this routine's own header is exactly where the multiple-base fact matters most. The follow-on 'It is the whole of what the firmware tells IC303 about which recording to play' needs the same scoping.

WEAK EVIDENCE DRESSED AS FACT (EDIT[0] leg 2): 'MAME's kn5000.cpp keeps the four wave ROMs in their own ROM_REGION16_LE("waveform"), which appears in neither maincpu_mem nor subcpu_mem.' True of the file, but in the repo's snapshot the 'waveform' region is referenced by NOTHING -- IC303 is not modelled at all (its map line is commented out at :164). Absence from a memory map proves 'unmodelled', not 'unreachable by hardware'. The citation is also stale and unqualified: the LIVE driver at /home/fsanches/compartilhado/kn7000_mame/src/mame/matsushita/kn5000.cpp maps 0x100000 -> tonegen status_r/addr_w (:634), 0x110000 -> kbd_data_r (:636), 0x110002 -> kbd_status_r (:637), and loads ic307 four times as BAD_DUMP (:1700-1703) rather than NO_DUMP. REPLACE THIS LEG with the real evidence the package ignored: technics-docs/tone-generator.md:300,321 states, FROM THE SERVICE-MANUAL SCHEMATICS (Tone Generator Sections A and B), 'Waveform ROMs (IC304-307) ──> Tone Generator LSI (IC303)'.

UNMARKED INFERENCE (EDIT[0] and EDIT[2]): 'So IC303 does the walk', 'IC303 resolves it itself' (EDIT[1]), and 'resolved by IC303 against the wave ROM's own per-page directory' (EDIT[2]) are conclusions by elimination -- nobody has observed IC303 resolving anything. Project rules require 'INFERENCE:' in the comment text. The 'per-page directory' generalization additionally rests on ONE genuine chip; IC304-306 are undumped.

UNEVIDENCED LEG (EDIT[0]): 'nothing in this ROM, nor in the sub-CPU boot ROM, nor in the MAIN PROGRAM, walks the waveform ROMs.' The package offers censuses for the first two only. I verified the main-program leg myself and it HOLDS -- v10/maincpu's only 0x100000 references are `cp xiz, 0x100000` (kn5000_v10_program.s:382), `cp xbc, 0x100000` (:479), `add xbc, 0x100000` (boot/system_handlers.s:6751), `cp xiz, 0x100000` (ui/ui_mode_handlers.s:1357), all DRAM-top bounds; 0x110008/0x11000a is the FDC (storage/fdc_routines.s:22,26,34,44) -- but the package must carry this evidence, not leave a leg a reader cannot check.

UNRESOLVED TENSION PAPERED OVER (most substantive scientific concern). Voice_Slot_ApplyPitchJitter (line 20570) performs (0x0451CE) += (tick & 7), and WaveSel_StageB_Store_Reg040 doubles the top nibble in place (lines 7884-7888). Under the validated decode entry = bits[11:0] (kn7000_mame/notes/kn5000-structural-validation.md §0), a +/-7 dither selects a DIFFERENT directory entry on every note through Voice_Init_Type1. The package lists both sites as 'accounted for' and then asserts the index model with total confidence. Either the low bits are not a plain entry index or that path is not what it appears. This belongs in the comment as an explicit OPEN question.

MISLABELLED FIGURES in the EVIDENCE section: 'pad 10B / 20B / 12B / 20B' for pages 0-3. Those are the EXTENT of each page's last parameter record (last param_ptr -> PCM start), body included. The actual trailing-zero padding is 2 / 14 / 10 / 12 bytes (verified independently). As written they contradict the package's own reconciliation with flagcensus.py: 10+20+12+20 = 62 bytes = 31 words, not the 19 words the 7203-vs-7184 delta requires; 2+14+10+12 = 38 bytes = 19 words, which is correct. A reader deriving a record boundary from 'pad 10B' gets it wrong.

WRONG PATH FORM: '../technics-docs/kn7000-expansion-and-wave-dump.md'. From v142/subcpu/ that resolves to nothing, and the repo contains its own technics-docs/ (assets only), so the reference is actively misleading. It only resolves from the repo ROOT, to a sibling directory outside version control. The dominant in-source convention is the bare form 'technics-docs/<page>.md' (6 of 7 uses in .s files, including this same file at lines 9394, 43463, 45918).

ALL THREE CROSS-REFERENCES DANGLE. EDIT[1], [2] and [3] each point at 'WHAT +0x040 SELECTS' in the staging-block header, which only EDIT[0] creates. Since EDIT[0] cannot be applied, none of [1]-[3] is independently applicable without editing out or retargeting the cross-reference.

EDIT[2] INCOMPLETENESS: 'The firmware neither validates it nor dereferences it' is true for range-check and dereference (the 12-site census verifies it), but it sits immediately after 'copy ... unchanged' and never tells the reader the word IS modified downstream -- by WaveSel_StageB_Store_Reg040's nibble-doubling RMW and by Voice_Slot_ApplyPitchJitter's +/-7 add.

EDIT[2] PLACEMENT: the anchor (line 5865) is the last line of WaveSel_Emit_ZoneRecord_S4's PRIVATE header ('This is the base/default zone format'), so a claim about ALL SIX variants will read as S4-specific.

PRE-EXISTING BROKEN CITATIONS INHERITED, NOT FIXED. The block EDIT[3] extends cites 'see subcpu_mem in MAME's kn5000.cpp' for 0x100000 being the TG latch, but the repo's subcpu_mem (lines 159-172) contains no such mapping -- its only TG line is commented out AND at 0x110000. Line 53227 cites 'kbd_data_r / kbd_status_r in MAME's kn5000.cpp', which exist only in the kn7000_mame tree. Appending an evidence-first block to a stale-citation block without correcting it amplifies the error.

REPRODUCIBILITY GAP (global CLAUDE.md rule). The pad figures, the 1413-unique-pairs count, the flag-0x00 value distribution (591/539/116), the 0x01-0x2F >=0xE0 split (6209/6170) and the bit6 final-vs-mid split (193/65) are NOT produced by any committed probe. flagcensus.py and waverec.py cover only counts, back-references, flag totals and size histograms. My verification script lives only in scratch (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-fsanches-compartilhado-KN7000/d0e1b1c2-9dd7-40da-b88c-9bcc60bcc85a/scratchpad/verify.py) and is volatile; whoever completes this package must commit an equivalent beside flagcensus.py before the numbers are quoted in the ROM.

MINOR: the EVIDENCE section's MAME line range '770-774' is off by one at the top -- ROM_REGION16_LE is at :769, the four ROM_LOADs at :770-773. maincpu_mem starts at :140 (cited as 141-157); subcpu_mem 159-172 is correct.

NOTE (not a defect, a correction the package gets RIGHT): the package's claim that ic304 is NOT byte-identical to IC307 is verified (ic304/305/306 all sha1 0f9b0375..., 83.4% 0xFF, page-0 entry 0 = {0x0318, 0x009A} vs IC307's {0x0318, 0x01A3}) and is MORE accurate than technics-docs/roadmap.md:44-45 ('placeholder copies of IC307') and the project memory index ('BAD_DUMP copies of IC307'). If the package lands, those two should be corrected in the same pass per the 'contradicts an earlier documented claim' rule.
critique.safe_subset:
NOTHING is safe to apply exactly as submitted. All four edits are byte-safe (comment-only, no instruction/directive/label/branch-target touched, no rename proposed) and all four anchors exist and are unique at lines 6921, 23900, 5865 and 2646 -- but each edit carries either a false statement or a cross-reference to a block that the package fails to deliver.

APPLY (one piece, with one cut): EDIT[2], minus its final clause. Keep 'All six variants copy the zone record's word 0 to 0x0451CE unchanged, and that word IS the wave selector -- (class << 12) | entry' -- I verified all six emitters do `ld wa, (xbc)` / `stw_da 0x0451ce, xwa` with no masking (lines 5784, 5803, 5822, 5840, 5858, 5872), and the decode is already stated in the file at line 6895 and validated in kn7000_mame/notes/kn5000-structural-validation.md §0. CUT 'resolved by IC303 against the wave ROM's own per-page directory' unless prefixed 'INFERENCE:', and CUT 'see \"WHAT +0x040 SELECTS\" in the staging-block header' (dangling). Reword 'neither validates it nor dereferences it' to 'never range-checks it and never dereferences it -- though it is modified downstream: WaveSel_StageB_Store_Reg040 doubles the top nibble when bit 2 of 0x041343 is set, and Voice_Init_Type1 adds (tick & 7) via Voice_Slot_ApplyPitchJitter.'

REJECT AND RESUBMIT: EDIT[0] (truncated mid-word, deletes its own anchor, and its two central sentences -- 'only channel to IC303' and 'exactly ONE read anywhere' -- are false as worded). The corrected block must (a) reproduce the anchor line, (b) actually contain the directory-format material its heading promises, (c) scope the census to 0x100000/0x100002 and separately account for the 0x110000/0x110002 reads at lines 53245/53250/53471/53474, (d) replace the MAME leg with the schematic citation technics-docs/tone-generator.md:300,321, (e) mark 'IC303 does the walk' as INFERENCE, (f) carry the main-program census, (g) record the jitter/entry-index tension as OPEN, (h) correct pad to 2/14/10/12 bytes, and (i) use the bare 'technics-docs/...' path form.

REJECT AND REWRITE: EDIT[1] -- must say 'for the callers that pass the 0x0451CC shadow block' rather than asserting shadow+0x02 = 0x0451CE unconditionally, given the 0x2AA4 (line 25697) and 0x3B1C (lines 38404, 38450) callers.

REJECT ONE SENTENCE OF EDIT[3] -- the access-census sentence is fine once scoped, but 'It is also the ONLY read of IC303 in the whole payload' must go; ToneGen_Poll_Read (lines 53471-53474) is a second one. The rest of EDIT[3] can then be applied once EDIT[0]'s target block exists.

Whoever completes this must also commit a probe covering the pad, unique-pair, value-distribution and bit6-position figures beside kn7000_mame/tools/kn5000-rom-structure/flagcensus.py before those numbers enter the ROM source.

critiques.area: hdae5000 — UI object descriptor pool 0x29DC12-0x2A5D2B (hdae5000/hdae5000_data_tables.s, hdae5000/hdae5000_init_data.s)

problems: BLOCKER — EDIT [0] AS DELIVERED CHANGES THE ROM BYTES. Its replacement text is truncated mid-sentence ("a class-specific body who") and drops the `\t.byte 0x02` and `\t.byte 0x00` lines that must follow the moved label. The WHY asserts "the two .byte directives are reproduced verbatim in the same order" — they are not present in the text supplied. PROVEN, not inferred: I copied hdae5000/ out of tree and built it with the Makefile's own toolchain (llvm-mc -triple=tlcs900 / ld.lld -e 0 -T hdae5000/hdae5000.ld / llvm-objcopy -O binary). Baseline = byte-exact vs original_ROMs/hd-ae5000_v2_06i.ic4 (md5 8da83ca363d03f02b5707f1e828704cb). With edit [0] applied exactly as written the image is 524,286 bytes instead of 524,288 and diverges at file offset 121,874 = ROM 0x29DC12, i.e. the pool start itself. FIX: after `HDAE5000_UiDescriptor_Pool:\t; 0x29DC12` the next two lines must be `\t.byte 0x02` then `\t.byte 0x00`. With that restored, edits [0]+[1]+[2]+[3]+[4]+[6] together rebuild BYTE-EXACT (verified).

BLOCKER — SIX OF THE TWELVE BLOCKS ARE TRUNCATED MID-WORD, so the package cannot be applied mechanically and the truncated parts cannot be reviewed. Truncated ANCHORs: [5] ("none of them a descriptor bou"), [6] ("\t.set HDAE500"), [9] ("used by HDAE5000_UI_Descripto"), [10] ("HDAE5000_Str_"), [11] ("'UI "). Truncated REPLACEMENTs: [0] ("a class-specific body who"), [9] ("The three 44-byte r"), [11] ("0x2A5634: ('HDAE5000_Demo_Data'"). The unreviewable text includes the entire record-layout header block, which is the main deliverable. Re-supply those blocks in full before anything is applied.

FALSE CLAIM — "There are NO .incbin directives in the pool (the region is emitted as raw .byte/.ascii/.fill)". The .incbin half is correct and I confirmed it (all ten .incbin directives in hdae5000/hdae5000_data_tables.s start at offset 54,881+ into includes/code_29af2d_2fffff.bin = ROM 0x2A858E and above, well past the pool). The second half is wrong: 721 lines inside the pool's source range (file lines 6272-27150) are still disassembled TLCS-900 instructions interleaved with the data directives — `normal` x198, `nop` x147, `pushw` x83, `popw` x56, `push` x55, `pop` x34, `adc` x30, plus `xor (xiz), e` (line 6506), `cps xwa, 5`, `jrl nc, 3328`, `swi 7`, `ldcfm 4, (xiz)` (line ~27050). Consequence for edit [5]: its replacement DELETES the sentence "the descriptor pool itself is still decoded as instructions", which is still TRUE and is the one honest warning in that paragraph. Keep it. Do not let the new header block state or imply that the pool is emitted as data directives.

FALSE CLAIM, CONTRADICTED BY THE PACKAGE'S OWN ARTIFACT — the negative control. The evidence says the four link .shorts read at every other offset "score 0 or 1 out of the same populations", and the proposed script's docstring makes it a pass criterion ("the negative control at every other offset must be ~0%"). Running the script as supplied prints: +0x00 next/prev 173/679, +0x02 child/parent 1/679, and +0x08 child/parent 498/498 — a PERFECT 100% score at a non-proposed offset. This is a sliding-window aliasing artefact (at d=8 the test re-reads the real next/prev pair under different names), which is explainable but is exactly what a negative control is supposed to exclude. The script nevertheless prints OK, because its OK depends only on `viol` and `ok == tot` and never on its own stated criteria. Either fix the control (test permuted field assignments, not a sliding window) or delete the "0 or 1" sentence; do not ship a verifier whose documented pass criteria its own output falsifies.

INCOMPLETE ARTIFACT — the proposed scripts/tools/verify_hdae5000_ui_pool.py does not compute two of the four numbers its docstring lists as pass criteria. It prints only next/prev symmetry and child/parent; the claims "a chain head is its parent's first child 173/173" and "siblings share a parent 498/498" are never evaluated. I evaluated them independently and both hold exactly (173/173 and 498/498), so the CLAIM is true — but the artifact offered as its evidence does not check it, which is precisely the failure mode the reproducibility rule exists to prevent. Add both tests before committing the script.

PACKAGE INTEGRITY — the edit numbering is broken. The SUMMARY says "13 byte-neutral edits"; twelve are listed ([0]-[11]). Internal cross-references use a different 1-based numbering that does not line up: the .set re-basing is called "edit 7" but is listed as [6]; the symbols file is "edit 12" but is [10]; the refine tool is "edit 13" but is [11]. Solving for the shift, exactly one edit — number 11 in the author's numbering, sitting between the WindowGeometry_Init edit and the symbols file — was never delivered. (Best guess at its target: hdae5000/hd-ae5000_v2_06i.s:117, the file-header index line `0x2BA1A6  HDAE5000_Font_Data - Font bitmap data (large block)`, which edit [11]'s prose says is retired but which no delivered edit touches.) An integrator following "Apply edits 1 and 7 before 2-5" cannot resolve those numbers against the list.

INCOMPLETE REFERENCE LIST — scripts/tools/refine_hdae5000_strings.py. The package cites only lines 26-30 (NEW_SPLIT_POINTS). The same five addresses appear a SECOND time at lines 48-52, in the CONVERT_ADDRS set, each with the abbreviated comment (`0x29DC14,   # UI_Descriptors` … `0x2A5634,   # Demo_Data`). Edit [11] does not touch them, so the stated purpose of that edit — "Left untouched, a re-run would re-insert them" — is not achieved: a re-run would still act on all five addresses. Line 32 (`0x2BA1A6: ('HDAE5000_Font_Data', …)`) is likewise left with its endorsing description even though the header comment the edit adds declares it retired.

WRONG JUSTIFICATION — edit [10] (symbols/hdae5000_symbols_reference.txt). The package says the file is "a generated dump … if the integrator regenerates it from the ELF instead, that is equivalent". It is not equivalent. CLAUDE.md lines 186-193 document regeneration from the ASL map: `python scripts/analysis/extract_symbols_from_map.py archive/asl/hdae5000/hd-ae5000_v2_06i.map symbols/hdae5000_symbols_reference.txt`, and archive/asl/hdae5000/hd-ae5000_v2_06i.asm contains NONE of these labels (grep: zero hits for UI_Descriptors / UI_Page_Titles / Panel_Save_UI / Credits / Demo_Data / Str_CharSet / Alert_HDFormat). Regenerating per the documented recipe would DELETE all twelve rows, not update them. The hand-edit is the right action (and matches existing practice — WAVE-STATUS records these rows being "merged programmatically"), but the reason given must be corrected, or a later integrator will "just regenerate" and silently lose the rows. Note also that CLAUDE.md's own table for this file ("34 symbols, 0x280000-0x29AF2D") is already stale.

INFERENCE PRESENTED AS FACT — "high half 0x0160 = host KN5000 widget library" (SUMMARY, and presumably the truncated header block). Nothing in the package supports it, and I could not support it either. The 0x016A→ClassName_Table[index] mapping IS evidenced (4 exact name hits, no counter-example, and the table really has 13 entries + an empty terminator before 0xFFFFFFFF — verified), but the 546 records with high half 0x0160 carry 29 distinct low halves, which cannot index a 13-entry table, and no second name table is named. Mark it "INFERENCE:" or drop it. What IS safe to assert (edit [8]) is the negative: 0x0160 is the high half of the class-id field, not a 352-pixel display width.

INFERENCE PRESENTED AS FACT — edit [2]: "a child of LBN_P2, the LOAD BY NUMBER page-2 screen". The parent link is verified (object #177's parent = 175 = LBN_P2). The gloss is not: LBN_P2 is itself a root object with NO caption/title string in its 36-byte record (class 0160:0035), so the expansion of "LBN" is read off the abbreviation. There is a separate named object LOAD_BY_NUM (#143) that does carry the title "LOAD BY NUMBER". Either drop the gloss or write "LBN_P2 (a root screen; INFERENCE: LOAD BY NUMBER page 2, cf. object #143 LOAD_BY_NUM)". Same class of nit: "+0x0C = an undecoded kind word" — "undecoded" is honest, "kind" is a guess.

OVER-CLAIM — "zero unexplained bytes" / "accounted byte for byte". The accounting is by LENGTH, not by decode: of the 33,050 bytes, 16,918 are the decoded 22-byte headers (769 x 22) and 2,616 + 182 are inline strings + pad. The remaining 13,334 bytes of class-specific body are only shown to have a length that is constant per class — none of their content is decoded. If the header comment says the pool is "accounted byte for byte" a reader will take the pool for solved. Say "every byte is assigned to a record and a role; the 13,334 bytes of class-specific body remain UNDECODED".

MINOR FACTUAL SLIPS IN THE EVIDENCE SECTION (none reach the replacement text, but they are the numbers a reviewer would cite). (a) First .incbin resolves to ROM 0x2A858E, not "0x2A85CE" — 0x29AF2D + 54,881 = 0x2A858E, and the repo's own analysis/binclude-audit-2026-08-07/findings.json already records 0x2A858E. (b) "78 records have parent 0xFFFF and are exactly the top-level screens named in HDAE5000_UiObjectName_PtrTable" — 77 of the 78 roots are named; root #385 has no name. Also 82 NAMED objects are non-roots, so root-ness and named-ness are not the same set. (c) "one of four sibling credit captions" — #645/#646 are children of #643 while #649/#650 are children of #648, so the four are not siblings (they share only the ABOUT_HELP ancestor). Edit [3]'s replacement text avoids this error and says "four separate objects", which is correct — keep it that way. (d) "After eight 0xffff bytes" (edit [9]) — a byte cannot be 0xffff; it is four 0xffff words / eight 0xFF bytes.

PRECISION — edit [9]: "the 20 records are 40,54,… bytes, which is exactly the class-determined body length of each one (classes 0160:001F, 0041, 004E, 0049, 0012) and exactly the address deltas between the 20 RAM descriptors". Each half has one gap. Class 0160:004E has NO instance in the pool, so its 44 comes only from the delta (I checked: 001F F=40 x77, 0041 F=54 x16, 0049 F=26 x34, 0012 F=36 x11, 004C F=64 x1 — 004E absent). And there is no 20th delta, so the last record's 36 comes only from the class. Together they do cover all 20, but the sentence claims both properties for all 20. Suggested strengthening, which I verified and which the package missed: hdae5000/hd-ae5000_v2_06i.s:126 already documents `0x2F94B2  HDAE5000_Init_Data - Data copied to 0x23952A`, and 0x2F9C4C - 0x2F94B2 = 0x79A = 0x239CC4 - 0x23952A. That pins the record-array start at 0x2F9C4C independently of the record parse, and it corroborates the in-source pointers 0x0023999A / 0x00239B84/86/88 already commented as "RAM copy of this image + 0x470 / 0x65a…".
critique.safe_subset:
CONFIRMED FIRST — everything substantive in the finding reproduces. FACTUAL ERROR, edit [3] — the out-of-bounds read is understated by two thirds. The text says 'EFF_Link slot 4 fetches 0x01F420, which is past the end of the array'. Computed straight from the ROM with base 0x01F404 + 12*mode + 4*slot at mode==1: slot 0 -> 0x01F410 (in array), slot 1 -> 0x01F414 (in array), slot 2 -> 0x01F418 = 0x0080004D (OUT), slot 3 -> 0x01F41C = 0x0000F002 (OUT), slot 4 -> 0x01F420 = 0x1000D000 (OUT). Three slots overrun, not one. The trailing clause 'and reads 0x1000D000, not a payload address at all' is true only of slot 4 — 0x0000F002 IS a payload address (it is ToneGen_Voice_Bitmap_Ptr's value, pointing at the voice bitmap), which makes slot 3 the more interesting case, not the omitted one.

FACTUAL ERROR, edit [1] — '+24 / -24 as signed bytes = octave up / octave down'. 24 semitones is TWO octaves. The operand is a MIDI note number in semitones: the same routine, ToneGen_SetupPolyVoice, indexes its octave table with (note / 12) * 2 (v142/subcpu/kn5000_subprogram_v142.s:38344), which is what fixes the unit. The wording is inherited verbatim from subcpu_data_tables.s:2217, so the package did not invent it — but applying edit [1] replicates a wrong number into a second file. It should read 'two octaves up / two octaves down', and the .s copy is worth fixing in the same pass.

OVERSTATEMENT, edits [4](c) and [6] — 'Its right edge is exact too. 128 u32 entries, 0x00F140-0x00F33F, strictly increasing, ending at exactly 0x7FFFFF00.' Monotonicity does not stop at 128. The package's own EVIDENCE section says the strictly-increasing run is 129 entries, and I reproduced that: entry 128 at 0x00F340 is 0xEE9AFF00, which is greater than 0x7FFFFF00 unsigned; the run breaks only at entry 129 (0x00F344 = 0x10000003). So the right edge is fixed by two corroborating facts — the terminator matching DSP_MixerGain_Curve and the libm pool starting at 0x00F340 — not by the scan. Contrast DSP_MixerGain_Curve (0x0131CF), whose edge IS self-evident: its entry 128 is 0x63000000 and breaks the run. Either drop the word 'exact' for this edge, or name the 129th entry and say why it is excluded. Leaving 'exact' next to a scan that actually returns 129 is the kind of over-tight claim this repo has been burned by.

UNMARKED INFERENCE, edit [7] — 'WA and DE are therefore curve INDICES, not slot numbers.' Nothing in DSP_MixerCoeff_Compute (0x03C067) bounds them. They are zero-extended 16-bit words read from DRAM 0x45B2 / 0x45B6, set by a command byte in the CmdHandler2C setters, and the routine does 'lda_d16 xbc, 61760 / extz xwa / add xwa, xbc / ld xwa, (xwa)' with no clamp anywhere in the three sites at lines 51652/51662/51672. An index above 127 walks straight into the double-precision libm pool at 0x00F340. The conclusion is well-motivated by the table geometry and by the third operand being an acknowledged 128-entry curve, but per the brief it needs 'INFERENCE:' in the comment itself, or a sentence saying no bounds check exists.

critiques.area: v142 sub-CPU: the three envelope generators (IC303 registers 0x20-0x29) and their builders

problems: BLOCKING (edits 0, 1, 2, 3): four of the nine replacement texts are TRUNCATED MID-WORD and cannot be applied as delivered. [0] ends '...ToneGen_WriteLevelBurst / _WriteLev'; [1] ends 'distinguishes envelopes 2 and 3 from\n; enve'; [2] ends 'when\n; paramA+0x47 !='; [3] ends 'Pan_ScaleWithVelocity with the co'. Applied verbatim each would splice a broken sentence into the header immediately above the next block (for [0], directly into the ';' separator preceding '; BUILD AND STORE THE VOICE OUTPUT-LEVEL WORD'). I cannot verify the missing tails, so nothing in [0]-[3] can be graded past the cut.

FALSE CLAIM in the package's own evidence, load-bearing for the rate-0 argument: 'Voice_Calc_LevelPair_EGA ... EGB ... EGC ... Every one of them emits a rate field of 0.' Only EGA does. Voice_Calc_LevelPair_EGB_WriteResult (line 13608-13613) emits (level<<8) | Detune_ScaleSymmetric(paramA+0x10), sign-selected by paramA+0x07; Voice_Calc_LevelPair_EGC_WriteDSP (line 13731-13749) emits (level<<8) | Detune_ScaleSymmetric(clamp(paramA+0x3D + paramA+0x46, -0x32..+0x32)). Both low bytes are generally NON-zero and frequently have bit 7 set. So leg 2 of the three-way 'rate 0 = arrive immediately' confirmation is wrong. Only leg 3 (the max(4,..) floor) actually survives; leg 1 is weak because the mute idiom pairs rate 0 with the apply-now bit SET on r0x20 (0xFF80) and CLEAR on r0x21 (0xFF00) — if rate 0 already meant 'go now', bit 7 would be redundant on r0x20.

FALSE CLAIM inside edit [0]'s own visible text, and it contradicts the census printed three lines above it: 'Everything that runs DURING a note reaches segments 0 and 1 only.' Segment 2 (+0x880) is written mid-note by TWO of the three routines the same table lists. ToneGen_WriteSegRegs_SameLevel is called from Voice_AllNotes_SustainRetrigger_BranchB/BranchD (lines 17329, 17368 — the sustain-pedal retrigger walk over live voices) and from Voice_Reload_Levels_BranchA/BranchC (23479, 23512); ToneGen_WriteEnvSegments is called from Voice_Reload_Levels_BranchD (23529). ToneGen_WriteSegRegs_SameLevel even pushes the PER-TICK shadow word (+46 = 0x0451FA, the one EGA rewrites) to +0x880. The mechanical explanation the edit offers for 'segment 2 written exactly once per note-on' therefore does not hold as stated.

OVERSTATED as fact where it is an INFERENCE (edits [1], [2], and the SUMMARY): calling the low byte of envelopes 2 and 3 a 'rate'. No measurement or hardware evidence is offered; the only argument is structural analogy with envelope 1. Two things cut against it. (a) The package's own summary concedes bit 7 set for negative values 'collides with the documented apply-now meaning'. (b) A collision the package missed: Voice_Calc_LevelPair_FixedAtk (the type-1/2 envelope-1 builder, line 11633) reads THE SAME paramA bytes 0x09/0x0A/0x0B/0x0C as UNSIGNED Voice_EnvelopeRate_Table indices, while Voice_Level_ComputeTriplet reads 0x09..0x0E as signed Detune_ScaleSymmetric inputs. Same record, same offsets, two incompatible readings. Either the bytes are voice-type-polymorphic or one reading is wrong — the comments must not assert 'rate' without an INFERENCE: marker.

UNCITED DIRECT CONFLICT with the project's own documentation, which the very routine being edited cites as its authority. technics-docs/tone-generator.md lines 105-114 gives +0x0840 = 'Pan Left (0x00=silent, 0x3C=center, 0x78=full)', +0x0880 = 'Pan Right', +0x08C0 = 'DSP/Effects Send Level', +0x0900/0940/0980/09C0 = 'DSP effects send 0..3', +0x0A00/0A40 = 'Secondary aux param 0/1'. The existing header of Voice_StereoLevel_Compute explicitly says its register meanings are 'taken from technics-docs/tone-generator.md, not proved here'. Edit [2] deletes that confidence caveat and replaces it with an unhedged 'ENVELOPE 3 -- IC303 registers r0x27/r0x28/r0x29'. Note the docs' pan polarity (0x00 = silent) is the exact opposite of the package's polarity claim for +0x840. The package should either reconcile the two documents or keep the caveat; silently dropping it is how a wrong claim gets laundered into fact.

MISCOUNT (SUMMARY): '17 of 17 fields mirror'. The mirrored field POSITIONS are 14 unique offsets, not 17 — the note-on set {7,9,10,11,12,13,14,17,19,20,21}->{61,63,64,65,66,67,68,71,73,74,75} (11) plus the per-tick set {7,15,16,17,19,22}->{61,69,70,71,73,76} (6), of which 7->61, 17->71 and 19->73 are counted twice. Verified by enumerating every (xiz+N)/(xwa+N) read in Voice_Level_ComputeTriplet (8038-8265), Voice_StereoLevel_Compute (9395-9655), EGB (13477-13615) and EGC (13621-13750).

THE MIRROR IS NOT OPERATION-PRESERVING, contrary to 'EXACTLY 54 bytes ... 17 of 17 fields mirror'. At the mirrored pair 0x07 <-> 0x3D the two sides do different things: Voice_Level_ComputeTriplet uses paramA+0x07 as a SIGN TEST ('cp (xiz+7),0 / jr ge') that two's-complement negates 0x0A/0x0C/0x0E, with no +-0x32 clamp; Voice_StereoLevel_Compute uses paramA+0x3D as an ADDITIVE bias ('ld c,(xwa+61); add (xwa+64); clamp 0x32/0xFFCE'). Same asymmetry in the per-tick pair: EGB negates conditionally on +0x07, EGC adds +0x3D and clamps. Edit [2] describes +0x3D as 'a bias shared by all three segments' — correct for envelope 3 — but the package elsewhere sells the two blocks as identical, which they are not.

OVERSTATED (edits [6], [7], [8], and edit [1]'s 'Target 0x00 is the LOUD end'): '0x00 is the UN-attenuated end of both level curves' is literally false. Voice_LevelPair_AttackCurve runs 0xFF..0x09 and Voice_EnvelopeLevel_Curve runs 0xFF..0x04 (subcpu_data_tables.s lines 1757-1787). Neither curve can ever produce 0x00; the un-attenuated ENDS are 0x09 and 0x04. That 0x00 continues the ramp past the end is an extrapolation and should say so.

EDIT [6] IS THE WEAKEST ITEM AND SHOULD NOT SHIP AS WRITTEN. Three defects. (a) The polarity evidence does not reach these registers: the 11-site mute idiom writes 0xFF00/0xFF80 to banks 0x840 and 0x800 ONLY (verified at Voice_SetPitch lines 22722-22745 and the other ten sites). Voice_Level_ClearAllOutputRegs touches none of those two banks — it writes 0x8C0, 0x500, 0x900, 0x940, 0x980, 0x9C0, 0xA00, 0xA40, 0x440, 0x480. 'NOT a silence primitive' is an extrapolation across a register-family boundary, into exactly the registers the project docs call effects sends (where 0 = no send is the natural reading). (b) The register list is incomplete: the edit says the routine switches 'envelopes 2 and 3 and register 0x23 OFF', but the code (lines 9767-9776) also zeroes 0x0451E2 (reg 0x500) and 0x0451DC/0x0451DE (regs 0x440/0x480), then sets reg 0x180 from the routing byte and zeroes 0x0451E0 (reg 0x4C0). (c) It is internally inconsistent: it asserts 0x0000 means full un-attenuated level AND that the routine 'switches envelopes 2 and 3 OFF', without saying how a full-level word turns anything off. The caller claim in [6] is the one part that checks out exactly (only call sites 22040 in Voice_Init_Type2 and 22366 in Voice_Init_Type1; no indirect references — I searched for the packed address bytes too).

EDIT [4] CONTAINS A NEW ERROR IN ITS CORRECTION. Its first half is exactly right (the operand is (i8)tonerec[0x6B] via 'ld a,(xbc+107)', added to paramA+0x27, clamped 0..0x64, then curved through 0x011899 — lines 11220-11238; the existing 'PitchBend_Scale(tonerec+46...) clamped 0..0xFF' is indeed wrong). But the final clause is wrong: the key-scale term does NOT come 'in _NoLFO'. _NoLFO (line 11424) is precisely the arm that SKIPS PitchBend_Scale. The term is applied in the fall-through arm after _ApplyKeyTrack (lines 11300-11318) and in _NoOscLFO's paramA+0x2E-non-zero branch. The 0..0xFF clamp does happen in _NoLFO. Fix the clause before applying.

IMPRECISION in edit [0]'s census: it says '~25 sites' for +0x800 and +0x840 when the exhaustive grep gives 24 and 26 respectively. If the whole point of the block is that the census is complete, quote the exact counts. (The four sparse banks are exactly right: 0x880 -> 3 sites at lines 24131/24531/24574, 0x8C0 -> 1 at 24147, 0x980 -> 1 at 24195, 0xA40 -> 1 at 24243; 0x900/0x940/0x9C0/0xA00 -> 3 each, in ToneGen_WriteVoiceParams, ToneGen_WriteLevelBurst and ToneGen_WriteVoice_6Words. I also confirmed there is no alternative bank-latch idiom: no 'add wa,<register>' or computed bank feeds any 0x100000 latch, and all 13 'stiw_da 0x100000' immediates are global banks 0x0200-0x0205/0x0C00-0x0C05/0x0E00.)

MINOR RANGE ERROR in the SUMMARY: envelope 1 on the type-1/2 path is built from paramA+0x08..+0x0E, not '+0x08..+0x0D'. Voice_Calc_LevelPair_FixedAtk reads +0x08 (attack index), +0x09/+0x0B (segment targets), +0x0A/+0x0C (segment rates), +0x0D (the byte cached at slot+70) and +0x0E (the PitchBend_Scale depth, line 11651).

MINOR INCONSISTENCY with the file's own text: the SUMMARY calls ToneGen_WriteVoiceParams a '22-register dump'. The routine's own header (line 23894) says 'Writes 23 registers'; another comment at line 14634 says 'a full 22-register reload'. Pick one and fix the other in the same pass rather than adding a third voice.

UNFAIR/INACCURATE 'WHY' on edit [3]: 'This family header states the word format and the three couples but not where a couple's bytes come from.' The header at lines 11185-11187 already states the couples explicitly: 'the paramA (level,rate) couples (+39,+40), (+41,+42) and (+43,+44)'. The genuinely new content is the curve/table identification and the trim bytes — which all check out (paramA+0x27/tonerec[0x6B] clamp 0..0x64 curve 0x011899; seg0 rate table[paramA+0x28]; seg1 curve[paramA+0x29] with max(4,table[paramA+0x2A]); seg2 curve[paramA+0x2B], table[paramA+0x2C] unfloored; _Full's bit-11-clear arm reads tonerec[0x010C] at line 11951, bit-11-set takes the fixed byte at 0x0118B3 = AttackCurve[26] = 0xA2; key scale paramA+0x2E on seg 0, paramA+0x2F on segs 1/2; callers Voice_Build_Register_Set 20791, Voice_Release_Type4 21635, Voice_Release_Type4_BranchA 21647, Voice_Init_Type1/2 22361/22035). State the WHY accurately.

OVERSTATED 'WHY' on edit [5]: 'it hides the single most informative fact about the rate field'. The file already documents the floor correctly TWICE, at Voice_Calc_LevelPair_Full_WriteChDepth (line 12193: 'Rate for pair 2 = table_0x011963[paramA+42], floored at 4') and Voice_Calc_LevelPair_Mono_WriteChDepth (line 12526). The _PatchAtk comment is an outlier, not a gap. The fix itself is correct and worth making.

SCOPE GAP in the 'tonerec+NN means paramA+NN' correction. The package says 'three existing comment blocks' are affected; the file has 39 'tonerec+' mentions and the mislabelling extends past edit [2]'s blanket, which stops at Voice_StereoLevel_PackCh23. Left uncorrected and now inconsistent with the new text: Voice_PortaLevel_Compute's header (lines 9655-9658, 9684, 9697 — 'tonerec+7/+8/+18' are paramA offsets; the prologue is 'ld xwa,(xwa+23)'), line 11330 ('table[0x011963 + tonerec+40]' = paramA+0x28), line 11710 ('table 0x0118FE indexed by tonerec+9/+11' = paramA), and subcpu_data_tables.s line 1796 ('Indexed by tonerec+40'). Either widen the blanket or fix these too; half-correcting a naming error is worse than leaving it.

WORDING BUG in edit [7]: 'stage 0x0451F8 = 0x0080 and 0x0451FA = 0x0000 -- target 0x00 with the apply-now bit' reads as if both words carry bit 7. 0x0000 has the apply-now bit CLEAR. Split the clause.

MISSING RENAME CAVEAT on edits [4] and [5]. Edit [8] correctly notes 'NO RENAME PROPOSED -- the label is a jr z branch target'. The same is true of Voice_Calc_LevelPair_PatchAtk_ApplyKeyTrack (branched to from line 11210) and Voice_Calc_LevelPair_PatchAtk_ClampDepth (branched to from line 11473), and BOTH also appear in symbols/subcpu_symbols_reference.txt (lines 1399 and 1407, as do Voice_WriteVolume_OrPan_Muted at 1516). After these edits each comment will directly contradict the label right below it, which invites a future pass to 'fix' the name and break the branch. Add the same explicit caveat.

UNVERIFIABLE HARDWARE CLAIM restated without attribution in edit [5]: 'which the chip takes as "arrive immediately"'. Nothing in the ROM proves what IC303 does with rate 0; the firmware-side evidence proves only that the firmware avoids 0 on segment 1. Attribute it to the staging-block header or mark INFERENCE:. Same for 'a rate-0 guard on the DECAY segment' — that segment 1 is a decay is an inference about envelope shape.

NO BYTE-CHANGE RISK (positive finding): every one of the nine replacements is comment-only, every line begins with ';', no instruction, .byte/.short/.incbin directive or label is touched, and no rename is proposed anywhere. I verified all nine anchors exist and are UNIQUE by exact multi-line string match (counts all 1) at lines 6925, 8028, 9384, 11189, 11218, 11476, 9765, 13773, 13791. Addresses cited in the evidence all match symbols/subcpu_symbols_reference.txt exactly (EGA 0x026769, EGB 0x026975, EGC 0x026AAA, Voice_Level_ClearAllOutputRegs 0x0249BF, Voice_Build_Register_Set 0x02B4E3, Voice_Release_Type4 0x02BCD6, ToneGen_WriteVoiceParams 0x02D101, ToneGen_WriteLevelBurst 0x02D436); note technics-docs/tone-generator.md's '0x02D0FD' for WriteVoiceParams is the stale one, not the package.

critiques.area: KN5000 sub-CPU keybed / touch (velocity) front end — boot ROM (IC30) and v1.42 payload

problems: BLOCKER (mechanical) -- six REPLACEMENT blocks are truncated mid-sentence and cannot be applied as text: [0] ends '; (0x110002)', [1] ends '96, 152,', [2] ends '; 0', [9] ends '; 0', [11] ends 'by one velocity', [15] ends 'that missing long is the only'. The port contract in [0] and [9] is the single most valuable thing in the package and is exactly the part that got cut.

BLOCKER (mechanical) -- two ANCHORs end mid-line and would leave orphan fragments. [0] ends '; Output: HL = 0 o' but /home/fsanches/compartilhado/kn5000-roms-disasm/subcpu/boot/kn5000_subcpu_boot.s:100231 reads '; Output: HL = 0 on success, 0xFFFF on error/no data'. [1] ends 'ToneGen_VelCurve_Di' but line 100283 reads '; (0xFF8040), ToneGen_VelCurve_Pivot (0xFF802A), ToneGen_VelCurve_Divisor (0xFF802C)'. All other anchors I checked are unique (grep -c == 1) and exist.

FALSE CLAIM in [11] -- the proposed comment says '0x01F43E, for raw 31..253, is exactly clamp(...) ...; ~= 224 - raw to within 3'. The closed-form fit does hold with zero exceptions over 31..253 (verified), but the '224 - raw to within 3' bound holds ONLY for raw 31..221 (max dev 3, verified). Over raw 222..253 the deviation reaches 30, because the table floors at 1 (inp[222..253] is 1,1,1,...,1). The EVIDENCE bullet scopes it correctly to 31..221; the comment text that would enter the repo does not. Fix: attach the range explicitly to that clause.

FALSE CLAIM in [15] -- 'the byte at 0x004A48 (Keybed_Touch_Mode, default 6, set only by Audio_CmdHandler_A0_BF)'. ToneGen_Init at v142/subcpu/kn5000_subprogram_v142.s:53132 writes it too: 'stdi8 19016, 6' (19016 = 0x4A48). That write IS the 'default 6'. The existing comment at line 53095 makes the same mistake ('only ever written from here'); the package hardens it instead of correcting it. Correct wording: 'initialised to 6 by ToneGen_Init (0x03D016) and thereafter written only by Audio_CmdHandler_A0_BF'.

UNEVIDENCED in [12] -- the whole star-paragraph 'Where a key event actually ENDS UP ... the TG voice registers are written later, on main-CPU command, through the staging block at 0x0451CE (Voice_Build_OutputLevel, ToneGen_WriteVoicePitch). The sub-CPU never turns a key press into a TG write by itself.' No evidence bullet supports any of it. The immediate caller of ToneGen_WriteVoicePitch is Audio_Tick_ServiceVoices_B (v142/subcpu/kn5000_subprogram_v142.s:15521), a per-audio-tick state machine gated on bit 10 of 0x041343 -- not a command handler -- and it loads 'lda_24 xbc, 0x0451cc' (0x0451CC, not 0x0451CE). 'never ... by itself' is a universal negative over 53k lines. ToneGen_WriteVoicePitch is also still flagged [UNCERTAIN] at symbols/proposals/subcpu-region-08.txt:599 (curated pitch vs LLVM ToneGen_WritePanReg). Cut this paragraph; the first half of [12] (the 0x004A4C correction) is solid and should stay.

INCOMPLETE PORT CONTRACT in [9] -- '(0x110000) DATA, read only when status bit 0 was set' is contradicted inside the same payload. ToneGen_Poll_Read (0x03D230, v142/subcpu/kn5000_subprogram_v142.s:53468-53475) reads 0x110002 into XWA, immediately overwrites it with a read of 0x110000, and never tests bit 0 -- 16 times at init. A contract an implementation 'has to satisfy' cannot omit its second consumer in the same ROM.

INFERENCE STATED AS FACT in [9] -- 'the read is what advances the scanner' is asserted inside the port contract with no supporting observation (nothing in either ROM can observe a FIFO advance). Compare [4], which correctly writes 'INFERENCE:' for the 0x0003 write. Mark this one the same way.

OVER-CLAIM in [9] and inconsistency with [1] -- [9] says 'key index (bounded at 64 by the 8-byte bitmaps both ROMs keep)'. The bitmaps bound nothing at the port: the code masks with 'and l,0x7' (boot 0xFF8B37) and 'srl a,3 / and a,0x7' (0x03D230), which ALIASES indices >= 64 onto the same 8 bytes. Separately, [1] correctly labels the 61-key premise 'INFERENCE:' while [12] states it as fact ('note in 0x24..0x60, i.e. it occupies 0x004A70..0x004AAC for the 61 keys'). Nothing in the repo documents the keybed size (grep of docs/ and technics-docs/ finds nothing). Pick one treatment.

MISLEADING PHRASING in [1] -- 'Byte-for-byte the same algorithm as Keybed_Decode_Event (0x03D11F)'. The TABLES are byte-identical (verified); the CODE is not. Boot 0xFF8BD2 = 'f1 60 05 00 06 cb 8f cf 30 07 ...' vs payload 0x03D11F = 'cb 8f cf 30 07 ...', diverging at the mode pointer ('f2 4c 80 ff' vs 'f2 3e f4 01') and at branch displacements ('76 89 00' vs '76 c6 00'). 'Byte-for-byte' will be read as 'identical code bytes'. Say 'the same instruction sequence over byte-identical tables, differing only in the mode pointer and displacements'.

IMPRECISE in [6] -- 'bit 0 = RAM low half failed, bit 1 = RAM high half failed'. MemTest_RegionTable +8/+9 (subcpu/boot/kn5000_subcpu_boot.s:98616-98617, documented at 98604-98605) are the error bits for a LOW HALF-WORD and HIGH HALF-WORD mismatch of each 32-bit test pattern, over one region only (DRAM 0x050000-0x09FFFF). 'RAM low half' reads as an address range and would mislead.

INCOMPLETE in [0] and [9] -- 'HL = 0xFFFF when there is nothing to report' / 'bit 0 ... Clear -> the drain loop stops for this pass' misses a second 0xFFFF path present in BOTH ROMs, where a DATA word has already been popped and is then DISCARDED: boot 'bit 7,b / jr nz, __error' (line 100253) and payload 'bit 7,l / ldw hl,0xFFFF' (Keybed_Read_Event_NoteOff, 53263-53265). The drain loop stops there too, with an event consumed. For an implementer that is a materially different case.

EVIDENCE CITATION WRONG -- 'BOOT_INIT sets PC=0x03, PCCR=0x02, PCFC=0x00 (lines 98955-8965 region)'. The actual lines are subcpu/boot/kn5000_subcpu_boot.s:98828-98830 ('ldio 0x30, 0x03 / ldio 0x33, 0x00 / ldio 0x32, 0x02', under the header '; Initialize interrupt control'). Lines 98955-98965 are MAIN_LOOP. The claim itself is correct and I verified it; the citation is not.

EVIDENCE QUOTE DOES NOT MATCH THE FILE -- 'ToneGen_Note_Loop does `ld a,(xsp+0)`'. The repo renders that instruction as 'ld a, (xsp + 256)' at v142/subcpu/kn5000_subprogram_v142.s:53167, 53174, 53189, 53197. The raw bytes '8f 00 21' do decode to (XSP+0), so the package's decoding is right and the disassembler's rendering is the defect -- but an integrator grepping the quoted text will not find it, and the package never mentions the rendering bug. Worth calling out explicitly.

LOOSE NUMBERS in [11] -- 'curves 0..8 all cross at velocity 80 for a medium strike (strength ~150-151)'. Measured: at strength 150 the nine curves deliver 80,80,79,79,79,78,78,78,79; at 151, 80,80,79,79,80,79,79,79,80. They cluster within +/-2 of 80; they do not all cross at 80. 'curve 9 ... is uniformly ~5 velocity louder' varies 4-7 across strengths 148-153 and only holds where the output curve is linear. 'the pattern predicts 124.75' is the mean-step extrapolation from row 8 (steps -9,-10,-9,-9,-10,-9,-9,-9; mean -9.25; 134-9.25 = 124.75) -- correct arithmetic, but the method is unstated and a least-squares fit gives 124.36. State the method or drop the decimal.

SOFTER THAN STATED in [6] -- 'bit 3 = tone-generator probe timed out'. IZ stays 0xFFFF when AUDIO_HW_WRITE_READ returns 0 on all 1000 polls; IZ is cleared to 0 on the branch taken when the status reads NON-zero (subcpu/boot/kn5000_subcpu_boot.s:100430-100440). So bit 3 means 'the TG status port never read non-zero in 1000 polls'. That matches the pre-existing header's 'timeout', so it is inherited rather than proven; keep it but do not present it as newly established.

SELF-CONTRADICTION LEFT BEHIND (1) -- the WHY for [0] lists "'send/receive'" as one of three false assertions being corrected, but that phrase is at line 100176, '; Uses INTER_CPU_LATCH_READ_DISPATCH to send/receive data to hardware.', inside CONTROL_PANEL_BIT_SET_CLEAR's header, and [2]'s anchor stops at line 100169. Lines 100170-100176 survive untouched, still describing a 'Button/LED index' pipeline and 'send/receive data to hardware'. Extend [2]'s anchor through line 100176.

SELF-CONTRADICTION LEFT BEHIND (2) -- not one inline comment in the chain is corrected. After applying, the file carries a header saying 'PC.1 is the CN12 "Sub CPU Checking Device" LED, active LOW' and eleven lines later 'res_dd8 1, 0x30\t; Disable timer interrupt on error' (100155) and 'set_dd8 1, 0x30\t; Enable timer interrupt' (100158). Also stale after the edits: 100143 '; Initialize serial subsystem', 100184 '; Call to get/send data', 100216 '; Call to send/get next item', 100243 '; Read data word from latch'. All comment-only, all cheap.

SELF-CONTRADICTION LEFT BEHIND (3) -- [3] and [6] assert '0x30 is PORT C, not a timer', and they are RIGHT (MAME's own TMP94C241 SFR table, /home/fsanches/compartilhado/mame/src/devices/cpu/tlcs900/tmp94c241.cpp:1664: 0x30 PC, 0x32 PCCR, 0x33 PCFC, 0x18 P6; and BOOT_INIT's data/function/control triple at 98828-98830 matches the pattern of every neighbouring port). But line 70 of the very file being edited says '.equ INTTC01, 0x30\t; Interrupt control (Timer 0/1)' under an '; Interrupt Control' banner, and line 98827 heads the port-C/D/E/F init block '; Initialize interrupt control'. Neither is in the package. That .equ has ZERO uses in the file (code uses the literal 0x30), so correcting its comment is byte-safe; renaming the symbol itself would need a reference sweep but currently has no references.

INCOMPLETE FIX in [8] -- it corrects 'every note comes out at level 208' but leaves the formula three lines above it (subcpu/boot/kn5000_subcpu_boot.s:98639-98640) reading 'velocity = gain/128 * (Velocity_Input_Curve[t] - 77) + pivot_out - (black key ? trim : 0), clamped to 0..255'. That is the same conflation of the intermediate with the delivered velocity, in a more prominent place, and it omits the 0xFF814C lookup entirely. Fix both in one edit or the file contradicts itself two lines apart.

REPRODUCIBILITY -- the package states outright that 'none of the numbers above live in a committed script yet' and asks the integrator to write one later. Under the project's standing rule, the measured curve tables (closed-form fit, out[] structure, the 10-row table, the per-curve extremes, the 387/2560 rounding sweep) must not enter the repo ahead of the script that regenerates them. scripts/analysis/kn5000_touch_curve.py must land in the SAME commit as [11] and [15], not as a suggestion.
critique.safe_subset:
SAFE TO APPLY AS-IS (7 edits, every claim independently verified against the ROM images, the code and MAME): [3], [5], [7], [10], [13], [14], [16].

- [3] SERIAL_INIT: verified. `pushw_erp/ldib_erp` accumulator, call to the drain routine, OR of the 8 bytes 0x0558..0x055F, then `cpib_erp 0xFB,0 / jr z` selecting `set 1,(PC)` (no key) vs `res 1,(PC)` (key held). PC = SFR 0x30 confirmed by tmp94c241.cpp:1664 and by BOOT_INIT's 0x30/0x33/0x32 data-function-control triple at 98828-98830. CN12 gating (`set_dd8 1,0x30 / bit_dd8 0,0x30 / ret nz` at 99902-99904) and MAME's wiring (kn5000.cpp:389-392, CN12 DIP 0x00=On, default 0x01) all check out. Single-caller chain confirmed at the exact lines the package cites: 98939, 99933, 100143, 100184+100216, 100259+100265.
- [5] `inc 8, xbc`: raw bytes at 0xFF8998 are `e9 60` — 0xE9 selects XBC, 0x60 is INC #3,r with the 3-bit field 0 meaning 8. Preceding `f1 58 05 31` = LDA XBC,(0x0558), so XBC becomes 0x0560 and the clear loop covers exactly 0x0558..0x055F. The comment '+1' is wrong and the replacement is right. Comment-only; the instruction is untouched.
- [7] 'preceded by' -> 'between': the pointer is at 0x01F41C, after the 0x01F418 pivot / 0x01F41A divisor pair and before the 0x01F420 mode table. All three byte-identity ranges re-verified True by rerunning the package's own one-liner: boot 0xFF802A/4 == payload 0x1F418, boot 0xFF802E/0x21E == payload 0x1F420, boot 0xFF824C/0x44 == payload 0xF919. The arithmetic in the parenthetical (0xFF824B, 0x01F63D) is correct.
- [10] bit-7 polarity: this is the strongest item in the package and the existing 'bit 7 = release flag' is genuinely inverted. problems: BLOCKER -- edits [0], [1], [2] DELETE CODE as written. The anchor is five lines (`INT0_HANDLER:` plus `bit_dd8 1, 0x68`, `jr nz, INT0_ProcessCommand`, `stdi8 (265), 1`, `reti`) but the replacement text contains ONLY a comment block and does not re-emit the label or the four instructions. BLOCKER -- the central hazard narrative is an EMULATOR ARTIFACT presented as firmware fact. The package's own named prior measurement, kn7000_mame commit 3fd44f3, says the duplicate came from 'tmp94c241's acceptance-time /INT0 level re-assertion' and that the commit REMOVED it: 'it changed the outcome exactly twice in 59300 latch bytes and both were that duplicate. Latch writes, INT0 dispatches and latch reads are now 1:1:1.' The nested dispatch therefore needs a SECOND /INT0 for the SAME byte, which existed only because MAME re-asserted INT0 as if level-triggered (mame/src/devices/cpu/tlcs900/tmp94c241.cpp:1352 `!(m_iimc & 0x02)`, whose own comment calls I0LE=0 'level-detect' -- inverted relative to this repo's reference .claude/skills/tmp94c241/references/interrupts.md:139 'I0LE: 0=edge, 1=level'). Edit [0]'s own text states INT0 is EDGE triggered with IIMC=0x00, which makes that duplicate impossible on hardware -- the annotation would be self-contradictory. Independently, the protocol forbids a second HEADER inside the guarded window: InterCPU_DMA_Send_Chunk (v142:2163+) writes the header, then waits for MSTAT1 to go LOW (`bit_dd8 4, 0x34 / jr nz, DMA_Chunk_Wait_MSTAT1_Set`) -- i.e. for the ack at 0xEF35C4 -- before anything else is loaded into IC23. Do not state 'the nested dispatch eats the header ... and the link stays down' as ROM fact; if it is kept at all it must read as 'observed in MAME under a since-removed /INT0 level re-assertion (kn7000_mame 3fd44f3)' and be marked INFERENCE.

BLOCKER (mechanism omission) -- 'the ISR never masks interrupts' and 'INT0 runs at level 1 ... the ONLY thing preventing re-entry' are contradicted by the ISR itself. Every one of the three parse branches does a read-modify-write of INTE0AD (SFR 0xF0) at 0xEF3560, 0xEF358A and 0xEF35B7: `f0 f0 31 lda XBC,0xf0 / 81 21 ld A,(XBC) / c9 cc f8 and A,0xf8 / c9 ce 06 or A,0x06 / b1 41 ld (XBC),A`. That (a) CLEARS the pending INT0 request flag -- INTE bit 3, cleared by writing 0 (tmp94c241.cpp inte_w lines 315-316) -- and (b) RAISES INT0's priority level from 1 to 6, only 1 to 13 bytes before the ack at 0xEF35C4. INTTC0_HANDLER puts it back to level 1 at 0xEF35EF-0xEF35FA (`and a,0xf8 / set 0,a`), matching the level-1 setting in SubCPU_Init_DMA_Channels. So from `or a,0x06` onward the ISR deliberately RE-ENABLES INT0 at a level that is accepted with IFF=2, with no help from INTT3 -- evidently so that payload-byte /INT0s (which take the DMAR branch once MSTAT1 is low) are serviced promptly -- and it deliberately discards a stale pending INT0 request. Any re-entrancy annotation that omits this is wrong about the mechanism.

WRONG NUMBER in edits [3], [4], [5]: 'THE LATCH READ (0xEF353D) ... 0x9F bytes before MSTAT1 is lowered'. 0xEF35C4 - 0xEF353D = 0x87, not 0x9F. 0x9F is the distance from the ISR ENTRY (0xEF3525) to the release, which is how the package's own EVIDENCE section computes it. Same error in the v7 variant (0xEF359A - 0xEF3513 = 0x87). Also the clause 'with no interrupt masking in between' is literally true but materially misleading given the INTE0AD writes described above.

NEW FALSE CLAIM in edit [13]: 'there is no timer 8'. The TMP94C241 has a 16-bit Timer 8 -- MAME irq_vector_map: `{ INTET89, 0x08, 0x70, 0x1c }, // INTTR8: 16-bit timer (Treg 8)`; tmp94c241.cpp:1565 `if (BIT(m_t16run, 2)) // Timer 8 is running`; tmp94c241.h:263 `uint16_t m_treg_16[8]; //TREG4 - TREGB`; and this repo's own .claude/skills/tmp94c241/references/interrupts.md lists 'INTET89 | Timer 8, 9'. 'plus eight 16-bit ones' is also wrong: eight 16-bit timer REGISTERS (TREG4-TREGB) but four 16-bit timers (4, 6, 8, A, per T16RUN bits 0-3). The rest of [13] is verified and correct: `res_dd8 2, 0x80` is T8RUN (0x80) bit 2 = 8-bit timer 2, and InterCPU_DMA_Send_Chunk arms DMA2V=22=INTT2 (v142:2187, 2333, 2359) before `set_dd8 2, 0x80`. Cut the parenthetical from '(Not "Timer 8": ...' through 'there is no timer 8.' and keep the T8RUN/INTT2 substance.

MISQUOTED EVIDENCE: the package cites .claude/skills/tmp94c241/references/interrupts.md for 'IFF = min(level+1,7) with IFF=2 accepting levels 2-7'. That file's table says the opposite: IFF=1 accepts levels 2-7, IFF=2 accepts levels 3-7. MAME implements the package's version (tmp94c241.cpp:1303 `for (int i = std::max(1, (m_sr.b.h & 0x70) >> 4); i < 7; i++)`, then `m_sr.b.h = (m_sr.b.h & 0x8f) | (level << 4)`), i.e. level >= IFF. Under the repo's own documented table, INTT3 at level 2 could NOT preempt an INT0 ISR running with IFF=2 and the entire preemption chain in the summary collapses. Resolve against the TMP94C241 datasheet before any level/IFF sentence is committed; until then it is an INFERENCE resting on an emulator implementation detail that this repo's reference contradicts.

CIRCULAR CITATION: the DMAR evidence quotes MAME's tmp94c241.cpp dmar_w comment ('the Technics KN5000 driver writes DMAR once per INT0 ...'), but `git blame` in ~/compartilhado/mame shows that comment was written by this project (commit 2cd1f5989987, Felipe Correa da Silva Sanches, 2026-02-23) and it cites the KN5000 driver as its own example. It is not independent corroboration. The identification does stand on non-circular evidence -- v10/maincpu/shared/sfr_tmp94c241.s:174 `.equ DMAR, 0x109` (=265) plus the only other DMAR write in the ROM, `stdi8 (265), 8` (bit 3 = channel 3) in the FDC path -- so cite those instead.

ABSENCE CLAIM under-evidenced (edits [9]-[11], and the summary): 'DMA0V/DMA2V ... are never written with a vector anywhere in the program ROM' was proved by grepping DECODED source, and the two hits the package reports (v10 system_handlers.s:5951, 5969) sit inside `E1DMA_ISR_BytecodeBlock`, a region the disassembly only partially decodes (raw `.byte`, `zcf`, `pushw sp`, nonsense branches). The claim survives -- but cite the byte scan, not the grep, and commit the scan script per the repo's reproducibility rule.

Renaming a label together with its references does not change assembled bytes; this repo does exactly that (scripts/renaming/rename_system_handlers_batch2.py, which even contains the string 'Audio_InitDMAChannels_Done'). POLARITY LEFT AMBIGUOUS in edits [0]-[2]: the handshake table glosses SSTAT0 as 'the byte in IC23 is a HEADER', which reads as asserted=header. The sender CLEARS SSTAT0 before writing the header (`res_dd8 0, 0x34` in InterCPU_DMA_Send_Chunk) and SETS it before the payload, and the main-CPU gate is `bit 2,(0x68) / ret NZ` at 0xEF3536 -- it proceeds only when SSTAT0 is LOW. UNMARKED INFERENCE, AND THE DATA CONTRADICTS IT -- edits [0]/[5], block A: 'PERCUSSION SETs ... every one of them has a base pitch other than 0x4280 -- the fixed pitch of a one-shot, which Voice_Pitch_CopyBase (0x023809) loads straight into the voice.' Two problems. (a) The 146 percussion base pitches take only 18 distinct values: 0x4D44 x94, 0x4EBC x22, 0x534D x8, 0x5167 x4, 0x4561 x3, 0x4880 x2, 0x49C1 x2, and eleven singletons (0x1F87, 0x1FC4, 0x2E80, 0x3280, 0x34D5, 0x4180, 0x4527, 0x4E80, 0x4F44, 0x501E, 0x5880). 116 of 146 share two values -- that is a shared transposition, not 'the fixed pitch of its one-shot'. (b) The claim that CopyBase is the path is not shown: Voice_Pitch_CopyBase's only callers are Voice_Allocate_Typed (the key >= 0x78 delegation) and Voice_Allocate_Type2 (only caller Voice_NoteOn_Type1, 0x02C2C0), while the ordinary key < 0x78 note-on in Voice_Build_Partial_Descriptor calls Voice_Pitch_Compute at v142/subcpu/kn5000_subprogram_v142.s:21184. On Voice_Pitch_Compute's bit-1-clear arm (all percussion are flags 0x00/0x08) the result is iz - (root*256+0x80) + basepitch, so percussion still TRACKS THE KEY, offset by (bp - pivot) = +10.766 semitones for the 94 records at 0x4D44. Also 'loads straight into the voice' glosses over CopyBase adding (layerblk+0x03)<<8 and (layerblk+0x04)*2 and octave-folding into +0x09/+0x0A before storing. CUT the interpretive clause; keep only 'all 146 carry a base pitch other than 0x4280, so unlike the melodic SETs they contribute a non-zero (base pitch - pivot) transposition; 94 share 0x4D44 and 22 share 0x4EBC.'

MISSING EDIT -- the wrong text the package says it is correcting is left in place. v142/subcpu/kn5000_subprogram_v142.s lines 7527-7541 still read 'The descriptor's root and basepitch fields are NEVER READ on this arm, so their contents are unconstrained. / They are, in fact, junk.' OVERSTATED -- edits [0]/[5], block A: 'so these SETs contribute no pitch offset at all.' The bit-1 arm has three outcomes, not one. critiques.area: Documentation-defect sweep of /home/fsanches/compartilhado/kn5000-roms-disasm (comments, banners and headers only; no instruction, .byte/.short/.incbin, or branch-target label is touched)

problems: [16] INTRODUCES A NEW FALSE CLAIM -- REJECT AS WRITTEN. The replacement asserts the 0x014777 descriptor table is passed at 'entry points 0x03C161 / 0x03C181 / 0x03C190', naming DSP_WriteGlobalConfig (0x03C181) as a user of it. The code says otherwise: DSP_WriteGlobalConfig does `lda_24 xde, 0x0147b3` (v142/subcpu/kn5000_subprogram_v142.s:51753), and the very banner being edited already states four lines below that '0x0147B3 ... is the table used by DSP_WriteGlobalConfig (program 0 only)'. The four real loads of 0x014777 are line 51742 (DSP_WriteEFFConfig) and lines 51794 / 51815 / 51845, which are the three arms of DSP_WriteParameter (DSP_WriteParam_EFFCase, _EFFCase0xA, _Generic). So 'four call sites' is right by luck, but the composition is EFFConfig x1 + WriteParameter x3, not EFFConfig + GlobalConfig + WriteParameter x2. The edit's only merit was replacing rotting line numbers with addresses, and it cements the wrong attribution while doing so. Correct form: 'at four call sites: DSP_WriteEFFConfig (0x03C161) once, and three arms of DSP_WriteParameter (0x03C190); DSP_WriteGlobalConfig uses 0x0147B3, not this table.'

[17] MISDESCRIBES THE MEASUREMENT IT ADDS. The prose says the 'Real source' column is 'how much enters the build as assembly/typed data/compiled C rather than .incbin passthrough'. That is not what the script computes. scripts/analysis/kn5000_source_coverage.py adds the C-compiled generated/ bytes into `inc` and prints source% = (total - inc)/total, so compiled C sits on the .incbin side of the number, not the source side. (The script's docstring contradicts its own code; the code is what produced the figures.) I ran it: maincpu v10 = incbin 860,028, of which C 855,100, source 1,237,124 = 59.0%. With the package's gloss a reader concludes 41% of maincpu v10 is unexplained blob, when in fact 40.8% is byte-exact recompiled C and only 4,928 B (0.23%) is a raw blob. Since CLAUDE.md is the agent-instruction file, this reproduces exactly the class of misdirection the edit claims to cure. Fix the gloss (or drop the column).

[2] AND [3] ANCHORS ARE TRUNCATED MID-LINE. Anchor [2] ends '...indexed by INDEX 0..8) -> ' but the file line continues 'part+0x112;'. A literal replace leaves 'part+0x112;' glued onto the end of the last replacement sentence and orphans the following two lines (0x00F7AC / 0x00F7BE / 0x00F7D2 ...), which the replacement already re-states -- garbled duplicate text. Anchor [3] ends at 'jp_ind`' and leaves '. The source already documents the target: 1613 bytes of hand' glued onto '...verbatim in _Loop's tail.', and the replacement re-states that same sentence, so it ends up duplicated and broken across lines. Both leftovers stay inside comment lines, so no assembled byte can change, but the anchors must be extended to end-of-line (subcpu_data_tables.s line 558 and line 3968 respectively) before applying.

[0] AND [2] OVERSTATE 'NOTHING PINS EITHER SUBSCRIPT'. That is false for COUNT. Voice_Selector_FindBestSlot zeroes the counter (`ld (xwa),0x0`), increments it at most once per entry (`incm8 1,(xwa)`), and the loop runs d = 0..8 (`cp d,0x9 / jr c`), so COUNT is structurally bounded to 0..9 and the 10-entry tables at 0x00F786 and 0x00F7D2 cannot be over-run. Only INDEX escapes (and VALUE, see next item). The accurate statement is: the old comment's causality was backwards (sizes do not pin anything), COUNT is bounded by the producer loop, INDEX is not bounded at all.

[0] AND [2] 'THE SIZES MATCH THE RANGES FINDBESTSLOT PRODUCES ON A HIT' IS UNSUPPORTED FOR THE VALUE TABLE. VALUE is a nibble: Voice_Selector_Unpack3Groups masks with `and hl,0xF` / `and bc,0xF` (lines 19621, 19630, 19643), so on the E-hit path VALUE is 4..15 and on the L path 1..15, while Voice_Part_Trim_Addend_2 (0x00F7BE) holds only 10 entries and ends at 0x00F7D1. VALUE >= 10 reads into Voice_Part_Trim_Base. Either drop the reassurance or state the VALUE case honestly.

[0] STATES AN UNPROVEN RUNTIME EVENT AS FACT. The replacement reads 'an all-zero scratch array yields INDEX = 0xFF; the 0x00F79A read then addresses 0x00F998 ... and a jump-table word is written into part+0x112' -- present indicative, no hedge. The code path is real and I verified every step (ldb e,0xFF / ldb l,0xFF at 19677-19678, no post-loop fallback, 0x00F79A + 0xFF*2 = 0x00F998, inside AUDIO_CMD_TONEEDIT_JUMPTABLE 0x00F973..0x00F99A per symbols/subcpu_symbols_reference.txt:96-97). But the repo's own prior pass declined to call it a defect: symbols/proposals/subcpu-region-07.txt:810 says verbatim 'I could not determine whether the all-zero case is actually reachable at run time, so I have not called it a defect'. Per the evidence-or-silence rule this needs an explicit INFERENCE: marker or a 'reachability unproven' clause.

[4][5][6] AND [2]: THE REFERENCE LIST IS INCOMPLETE AND THE 'GREP RETURNS NOTHING' CLAIM IS FALSE. The four names are not inventions with no home -- they are pending naming proposals, and the banner text being corrected was pasted verbatim out of them: symbols/proposals/subcpu-region-15.txt:102 (DSP_Bytecode_HandlerOffsetTable), :108 (DSP_Translator_OpcodeOffsetTable), :119 (DSP_EFFBytecode_ProgramTable), and symbols/proposals/subcpu-region-07.txt:771 (VOICE_SELECTOR_MIXWEIGHT_TABLES, followed by the identical 'Four adjacent u16 tables ...' text). 'Appears in no symbols/ reference file' is true only of *_reference.txt. More seriously, the wrong text survives in the proposals and the next wave will re-import it -- including the DSP_WriteGlobalConfig/0x0147B3 error at region-15:119-122. The proposal files must be corrected in the same commit or the fix is temporary.

[17] CANNOT BE APPLIED MECHANICALLY. The anchor covers only the four data rows (CLAUDE.md:1068-1071) but the replacement supplies a new header row, so CLAUDE.md:1066-1067 ('| Component | Source | Status |' and '|-----------|--------|--------|') must be deleted by hand. The package says so in prose, which turns a mechanical package into a manual one; applied literally it yields a 3-column header over a 4-column table. Fold lines 1066-1067 into the anchor.

[17] MINOR ACCURACY ITEMS. (a) 'all nine sections at 100.00%' is what compare_roms.py printed when I ran it today, but the repo's standing invariant (DISASSEMBLY_PLAN.md) is 15 sections including the legacy ASL mirror builds -- those printed nothing today because the .rebuilt.rom files are absent, which the new text does not say. (b) The table has eight rows while the text says nine sections; the ninth ('subcpu v142 update image') is omitted. (c) The claim that '~33%' and '~5%' are 'exactly the figures DISASSEMBLY_PLAN.md retracted' is not exact -- that file retracts '~32%' for table data (the package's own EVIDENCE section says ~32%, contradicting its defect list). The CLAUDE.md rows are still wrong, so the edit stands. (d) The new row 'subcpu boot (IC30) 100.00% / 100.0%' is true but flattering: kn5000.cpp marks IC30 BAD_DUMP and only 4,352 of 131,072 bytes are non-0xFF; a bare 100.0% in the agent-instruction file invites the same misreading the package is curing. Add the caveat.

RATIONALE TEXT (not the replacements) CONTAINS SEVERAL WRONG LABELS. I re-resolved every stale line number and all eight are genuinely stale, but the WHY blurbs misname the enclosing routines: line 3990 is in VoiceNode_PriorityList_Insert (not _Return); 4066 is in VoiceNode_SecondList_InsertOrLink (not _Insert); 33331 is in VoiceTablePtr_Epilogue (not VoiceTablePtr_Data); 44912 is in EFF_DisconnectLoop_Body (not EFF_VolumeLoop); and line 4405 is `stb_dri A,...` inside ChanStruct_Init_ZeroLoop, not `muls wa,0xC` as [11] claims (the real `muls wa,0x6 / lda_24 xbc,0x00f633` pair is at 4800-4801). Also the package's summary says the old comment 'already lists five boundary equations' when it lists four (naming five table starts), cites subcpu_data_tables.s:17 for a line that is at 18, and cites the OFFSETS_14739 note at kn5000_subprogram_v142.s:51964 when it is at 51967. None of these strings enter the repository, but they are the kind of sloppiness that makes a reviewer distrust the parts that are right.

[11] COHERENCE NIT. It cites Voice_Allocate_Nodes as 0x022340 (routine entry) while the sibling banner three lines below cites the same routine as 0x0223BE (the indexing site). Both are defensible; as applied, the file reads as if two different addresses are the same thing. Pick one convention or say which is which.
[2] silently drops the '(outside this region)' qualifier from the banner heading without saying so or justifying it.
